docs.text:
Each one-call table reads the data sets of setup.sas; %table_tte also reads adttde of %tte.

  1. %table_summary
  2. %table_ae
  3. %table_visit
  4. %table_model
  5. %table_response
  6. %table_tte
  7. %table_shift

docs.title: ADaM steps
docs.text:
Each step of an ADaM program changes a data set in place. Its example first copies the records it needs into a data set of its own (vs, lb, sl or tt), so advs, adlb, adsl and adtte stay as setup.sas made them.

  1. %merge_subject
  2. %pick
  3. %summarize
  4. %flag_if_any
  5. %pool
  6. %param_wide
  7. %summarize_groups
  8. %visits
  9. %windows
  10. %locf
  11. %baseline
  12. %flag_first
  13. %relchange

docs.title: 3. Compare with the pages
docs.text: The output under each call on a reference page is the output of this run: the first rows of each data set of out=, the first lines of each .lst and CSV file, and each figure. The tables, listings and figures are in the output folder examples/out (&spl_out.), in its folders tlf, listings, figures and ard.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Reference: the families of the macros.
  • How-to: Use the macros in your own program.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text: One page per macro. Every page has the same parts in the same order: the syntax with every default, the parameters, the result, the details (when the macro has them), examples with their output, the messages, the macros of the same family, and the proof.

docs.title: Start a program
docs.text:
Set up a program and read the data.

Macro It makes %study Starts a program: sets the study, the program and the output folder, opens the ADaM library, sets the options. %import_xpt Copies SAS transport files (XPORT version 5, .xpt) into SAS data sets in a folder.

docs.title: Describe the data
docs.text:
Counts, percents, descriptive statistics, rates, and the records a count needs.

Macro It makes %describe Returns the descriptive statistics of a numeric variable in each group: n, mean, SD, median, minimum and maximum. %freq Counts the subjects in each category and group, with their percent of the subjects of the group. %proportion Returns the percent of subjects in each category and group, with its confidence interval by a method you name. %rate Returns the exposure-adjusted incidence rate of each group, with its exact Poisson confidence limits. %worst Keeps the records of each subject at its worst level, such as the highest severity or toxicity grade. %termflags Returns one record per subject and term, with a flag that says whether the subject has the term.

docs.title: Test the groups
docs.text:
One test of the groups per call: its p-value in the result.

Macro It makes %anova Returns the p-value of the F test of a one-way analysis of variance of a variable between the groups. %ttest Returns the difference of the means of each pair of groups, with its confidence limits and the t-test p-value. %wilcoxon Returns the p-value of the Wilcoxon rank-sum test of each pair of groups, with the Hodges-Lehmann shift and its limits. %chisq Returns the p-value of the Pearson chi-square test of the groups against the categories of a response. %fisher Returns the p-value of Fisher's exact test of the subjects with a record against the subjects without, between groups. %cmh Returns the p-value of the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test of the groups against the categories of a response, within strata. %ancova Returns the Type III p-value of one numeric term in a linear model, such as the test of a dose response (test = trt01pn): the test of one numeric term, not a comparison of the groups. %adjust Adds the adjusted p-values of a family of pairs of groups to a result: one row padj per pair.

docs.title: Compare groups with a model
docs.text:
Estimates of the difference between pairs of groups, with their confidence intervals and p-values.

Macro It makes %lsmeans The ANCOVA of the groups: returns the differences of the LS means of pairs of groups in a linear model, with confidence limits and p-values. %mmrm Returns the differences of the LS means of pairs of groups at one visit from a repeated measures mixed model. %logistic Returns the odds ratios of pairs of groups from a logistic regression, with their Wald confidence limits and p-values. %risk Returns the risk difference, relative risk or odds ratio of pairs of groups, with its confidence interval and p-value. %rateratio Returns the rate ratios of pairs of groups from a Poisson or negative binomial model, with confidence limits and p-values.

docs.title: Time to an event
docs.text:
Kaplan-Meier estimates, the log-rank test, and hazard ratios.

Macro It makes %km Returns the Kaplan-Meier summary of a time in each group: subjects, events, the median time and its confidence limits. %logrank Returns the p-value of the log-rank test that compares the time to an event between the groups. %cox Returns the hazard ratio of pairs of groups from a Cox proportional hazards model, with its confidence limits and p-value.

docs.title: Subgroups
docs.text:
The test of the treatment-by-subgroup interaction, one model per call.

Macro It makes %interaction_glm Returns the p-value of the treatment-by-subgroup interaction in a linear model of a continuous variable. %interaction_logistic Returns the p-value of the treatment-by-subgroup interaction in a logistic regression of a response. %interaction_genmod Returns the p-value of the treatment-by-subgroup interaction in a Poisson or negative binomial model of a count. %interaction_phreg Returns the p-value of the treatment-by-subgroup interaction in a Cox model of a time to an event.

docs.title: Build a table
docs.text:
Stack the results, make the columns, keep every number, lay out the rows, print.

Macro It makes %stack Stacks results one under another into one table, a block per result, in the order given. %columns Returns the columns of a table: one row per column, with its N and the header that shows the N. %ard Writes every number of a table to a CSV file, the numbers file. %layout Returns the display data set of a table: one row per printed line and one column per group. %print Prints a table or a listing with one PROC REPORT into an RTF file and a monospace listing file. %csv Writes the records of a listing, or the numbers of a figure, to a CSV file.

docs.title: Tables in one call
docs.text:
A whole standard table in one call: the statistics, the columns, the numbers file and the print.

Macro It makes %table Makes a table from the stacked results in one call: %columns, %ard, %layout and %print, in that order. %table_summary Makes a summary table of the subjects in one call, such as demographics: one block per variable. %table_ae Makes a table of the subjects with adverse events by system organ class and preferred term in one call. %table_visit Makes a table of the descriptive statistics of each variable by group, parameter and visit in one call. %table_shift Makes a shift table in one call: the subjects in each category at baseline against each category after baseline. %table_response Makes a response table in one call: the responders in each group, and the comparisons of pairs of groups. %table_model Makes a table of a continuous endpoint in one call: descriptive statistics, and the LS means of a model. %table_tte Makes a time-to-event table in one call: the Kaplan-Meier summary, the log-rank test and the hazard ratios.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
One call per figure: the macro computes what it draws and keeps those numbers.

Macro It makes %kmplot Draws the Kaplan-Meier curve of each group as PNG and RTF files and returns the numbers drawn. %forestplot Draws a forest plot of estimates in subgroups as PNG and RTF files and returns the numbers drawn. %meanplot Draws the mean or median of each group by visit as PNG and RTF files and returns the numbers drawn. %lineplot Draws lines through given values, one line per group, as PNG and RTF files and returns the numbers drawn. %boxplot Draws box plots of a variable in each group as PNG and RTF files and returns the numbers drawn. %barplot Draws bars of the percent of each category by group as PNG and RTF files and returns the numbers drawn. %aeplot Draws the percent and risk difference of each adverse event as PNG and RTF files and returns the numbers drawn. %profileplot Draws one line per subject through its values by visit as PNG and RTF files and returns the numbers drawn. %scatterplot Draws the values of two variables against each other as PNG and RTF files and returns the numbers drawn.

docs.title: ADaM steps
docs.text:
The steps of an ADaM program that read other records: baselines, flags, windows, last observation carried forward.

Macro It makes %merge_subject Copies variables from a data set with one row per subject to every row of that subject, matched by USUBJID. %pick Gives each subject the value of its first or last record in another data set, as a new variable. %summarize Gives each subject the sum, mean, largest or smallest value of a variable over its records in another data set. %summarize_groups Returns one record per group with the sum, mean, largest or smallest value of each variable over the group. %baseline Gives every record of a group the value of the group's baseline record, as a new variable such as BASE. %flag_first Flags the first or last record of each group, among the records that meet a condition, with Y. %flag_if_any Flags with Y every row of each subject that has a record in another data set that meets a condition. %windows Puts each record into its analysis window by its study day, and gives it AVISIT, AVISITN and the window variables. %visits Gives each record its analysis visit, AVISIT and AVISITN, from the value of its variable VISIT. %locf Adds last-observation-carried-forward records (DTYPE = 'LOCF') to the analysis windows in which a group has no analysed record. %relchange Returns new records with the change from the record before, relative to the normal range, flagged in ANRIND. %param_wide Returns the values of several parameters side by side: one record per group, with the variables of each parameter. %pool Pools small groups, such as sites, into one group: a new variable that is the group, or the pooled value. %tte Returns one time-to-event parameter: for each subject the date of the first event, or else of the latest censoring.

docs.title: Messages every macro shares
docs.text:
Every macro checks its parameters before it runs. A wrong call writes two lines to the log and stops; no procedure runs. These checks are the same in every macro:

Message Fix <parameter>= is required give <parameter>=<value> (see <macro>.sas). <parameter>=<data set> does not exist give <parameter>= a data set that exists (make it first). <parameter>=<value> is not a variable of <data set> give <parameter>= a variable of <data parameter>=. Where the macro has a second data parameter: give <parameter>= a variable of <data parameter>= or <other data parameter>=. <parameter>=<value> is not one of: <the values it accepts> give <parameter>= one of them.

docs.title: %adjust
docs.text:
Adds the adjusted p-values of a family of pairs of groups to a result: one row padj per pair.

Procedure: PROC MULTTEST (INPVALUES=); a DATA step · Family: Test the groups

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%adjust(
     data    =
   , by      =
   , family  =
   , method  =
   , weights =
   , pattern = "X.XXX"
   , out     =
   , debug   = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= A result of pairs with the variables of by=, VERSUS, STAT and VALUE: the out= of %lsmeans, %mmrm, %cox and the other macros of pairs. (required) by= The groups: the variable of data= with the group of each pair (by = trt01p). (required) family= The pairs of the family in their order, separated by #: each the group first and then the group it is compared with, each value in quotes: family = "High" "Placebo" # "Low" "Placebo". A pair is in the direction of the rows of data= (the group in by=, then VERSUS): "Placebo" "High" does not find the row of High against Placebo. (required) method= The adjustment: bonferroni, holm, hochberg or hierarchy. (required) Accepts: bonferroni, holm, hochberg, hierarchy. weights= The weights of a weighted Bonferroni test: one number per pair, in the order of family=, separated by blanks (weights = 0.8 0.2). Only with method=bonferroni. (optional) pattern= The pattern of the printed adjusted p-value, in quotes. (optional, default "X.XXX") out= The name of the result data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets adjust. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the rows of data=, then one row per pair of the family with STAT padj, VALUE the adjusted p-value and TEXT the printed value. When data= has no p-value of a pair of family=, out= is data= as it is and the log has a NOTE.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use it after %lsmeans, %mmrm, %cox, %logistic, %risk, %rateratio, %ttest or %wilcoxon: it reads their rows with STAT pval. The family is the hypotheses of one multiplicity block: the pairs of family=, in their order. method= gives the adjustment:

  • bonferroni: Bonferroni (PROC MULTTEST); with weights=, the weighted Bonferroni test in a DATA step (the p-value divided by its weight, at most 1)
  • holm: Holm, the step-down Bonferroni test (PROC MULTTEST STEPBON)
  • hochberg: Hochberg (PROC MULTTEST)
  • hierarchy: the fixed sequence in a DATA step; each adjusted p-value is the largest p-value of its hypothesis and of the hypotheses before it

Every row of data= with STAT pval and a pair of family= is one hypothesis of the family. When data= has a pair in several rows (the terms, visits or subgroups of within=), all of them are adjusted together, as one family. For a family in each term, call %adjust once per term, on a data set with only the rows of that term (a DATA step with WHERE first).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples run on the example data after examples/setup.sas. The output under each call is the output of that run. They also read sbp_ls (made by the example of %lsmeans). All examples of the reference run as one program: examples/reference.sas.

Before these examples: the calls that make their inputs

Run examples/setup.sas, then these calls from the examples of %lsmeans, in this order. Then the examples of this page run as shown.

/* from the example of %lsmeans */
* Gives the difference of the LS means of every pair at Week 12, adjusted for baseline and sex.;
%lsmeans(
     data   = advs
   , where  = (paramcd = 'SYSBP' AND avisit = 'Week 12' AND anl01fl = 'Y')
   , var    = chg
   , by     = trt01p
   , covars = base
   , class  = sex
   , pairs  = all
   , order  = trt01pn
   , out    = sbp_ls
 )

Adjusts the p values of the two comparisons against Placebo by Hochberg: PADJ after PVAL.

%adjust(
     data   = sbp_ls
   , by     = trt01p
   , family = "Xanomeline High Dose" "Placebo"
            # "Xanomeline Low Dose"  "Placebo"
   , method = hochberg
   , out    = sbp_adj
 )

sbp_adj, the rows of the p-values where stat IN ('pval' 'padj'): 5 rows

Xanomeline High Dose  Placebo              TRT01P VERSUS  pval  0.0383969398  0.038
Xanomeline High Dose  Xanomeline Low Dose  TRT01P VERSUS  pval  0.0707974243  0.071
Xanomeline Low Dose   Placebo              TRT01P VERSUS  pval  0.9584423033  0.958
Xanomeline High Dose  Placebo              TRT01P VERSUS  padj  0.0767938796  0.077
Xanomeline Low Dose   Placebo              TRT01P VERSUS  padj  0.9584423033  0.958

docs.text:

The macro also writes these NOTE lines to the log, without stopping:

  • NOTE: [adjust] No data qualified: data=<data> has no p-value of a pair of family=.
  • NOTE: [adjust] out=<out> has no adjusted p-value.

docs.title: %aeplot
docs.text:
Draws the percent and risk difference of each adverse event as PNG and RTF files and returns the numbers drawn.

Procedure: PROC SUMMARY, PROC SGPANEL (and PROC FREQ in %risk) · Family: Figures

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%aeplot(
     data      =
   , plot      =
   , par       =
   , columns   =
   , denom     =
   , where     =
   , term      = AEDECOD
   , by        =
   , reference =
   , threshold =
   , sort      = difference
   , ci        = wald
   , level     = 0.95
   , max       = 30
   , xlabel    =
   , file      =
   , width     = 6.5in
   , height    = 4.5in
   , out       =
   , outpar    =
   , debug     = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: the adverse event records. (required) plot= Draw again: the out= of an earlier %aeplot call, changed or not. It is drawn as it is, and no statistic is computed. Give it instead of data=. (optional) par= The drawing parameters of an earlier %aeplot call: its outpar=. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=. (optional) columns= The data set of %columns: it gives the order of the groups and their colours. When not given, the groups come in the order of denom=. (optional) denom= The population: a data set with one row per subject and the variable of by=. (required) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (trtemfl = 'Y'). (optional) term= The term of a row: one variable of data= (term = aebodsys). (optional, default AEDECOD) by= The groups: one character variable of denom=. (required) reference= The reference group of the risk difference: a value of by=, in quotes (reference = 'Placebo'). (required) threshold= A percent: only the terms that this percent of the subjects of a group or more have, in at least one group (threshold = 5). (optional) sort= The order of the terms from the top: difference (the risk difference of the first group that is not the reference, the largest first), frequency (the percent of all subjects, the largest first) or alphabetical. (optional, default difference) Accepts: difference, frequency, alphabetical. ci= The type of the interval of the risk difference, as ci= of %risk. (optional, default wald) level= The confidence level: a number between 0 and 1. (optional, default 0.95) max= The most terms to show: a positive whole number. The first terms in the order of sort= are shown. (optional, default 30) xlabel= The heading of the right panel: a text in quotes. When not given, Risk difference (%) with 95% CI, with the level of level=. (optional) file= The output file without its extension: the macro writes <file>.png (300 dpi) and <file>.rtf. (required) width= The width of the figure: a length with its unit (width = 9in). (optional, default 6.5in) height= The height of the figure: a length with its unit (height = 6in). (optional, default 4.5in) out= The name of the data set of the numbers drawn. When not given, they are not kept. (optional) outpar= The name of the data set of the drawing parameters, one row each. Give it to par= of a later call to draw the figure again. (optional) debug= yes: keep the work data sets aeplot. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the variable of term=, the variable of by=, KIND, X, LOWER, UPPER and N. A row of KIND percent is one term and group: X is the percent of its subjects and N the subjects with the term. A row of KIND difference is one term and group that is not the reference: X is the risk difference in percent (100 x RD of %risk), and LOWER and UPPER its limits in percent. The data set of outpar=: one row per drawing parameter, in the order of the table: PARAMETER ($32), its name, and VALUE ($500), its value as drawn (a label in quotes). The files: <file>.png and <file>.rtf.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use %barplot for the percents of the categories of one variable without a difference. The figure has two panels side by side that share the axis of the terms. The left panel shows the percent of the subjects of each group with the term, as dots. The right panel shows the risk difference of each group against the reference group, with its confidence interval and a line at 0. The flags are those of %termflags and the risk differences those of %risk (ci=, level=), so the figure and a table made with them cannot differ. The terms are those that reach threshold=, in the order of sort=, at most max= of them. To draw the figure again without computing, give plot= the out= and par= the outpar= of an earlier call.

Good to know

Draw again: plot= takes the out= of an earlier %aeplot call, changed or not, and draws it as it is, with no statistic computed: the terms from the top in the order of their first row (to drop or move a term, change its rows). par= takes the outpar= of that call and gives the drawing parameters: columns, term, by, xlabel, file, width, height. These change the picture, not the numbers. The other parameters compute (sort= and max= choose the rows of out= and their order); with plot= the log has a NOTE for each one given, as it is not used. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=, and the row wins over the default of the table.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples run on the example data after examples/setup.sas. The output under each call is the output of that run. They also read t14_2_1_cols (made by the example of %columns). All examples of the reference run as one program: examples/reference.sas.

Before these examples: the calls that make their inputs

Run examples/setup.sas, then these calls from the examples of %describe, %anova, %freq, %chisq, %stack, %columns, in this order. Then the examples of this page run as shown.

/* from the example of %describe */
* Summarizes age in each group and in the Total: n, mean, SD, median, minimum and maximum.;
%describe(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_describe
 )
/* from the example of %anova */
* Tests age across the three groups: one row, the p value of the F test.;
%anova(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_anova
 )
/* from the example of %freq */
* Counts each sex in each group and in the Total: n and the percent of the subjects of the group.;
%freq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_freq
 )
/* from the example of %chisq */
* Tests sex across the groups: one row, the p value of the chi square test.;
%chisq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_chisq
 )
/* from the example of %stack */
* Stacks four results in the order of the table: RESULT and ORD tell where each row came from.;
%stack(age_describe age_anova sex_freq sex_chisq, out=t14_2_1)
/* from the example of %columns */
* Makes the four columns with their N from adsl, the Total last, in the order of TRT01AN.;
%columns(
     data  = t14_2_1
   , n     = adsl
   , var   = trt01a
   , order = trt01an
   , total = yes
   , out   = t14_2_1_cols
 )

Draws the percent of each term of 5 percent or more and its risk difference against Placebo.

%aeplot(
     data      = adae
   , columns   = t14_2_1_cols
   , denom     = adsl
   , where     = (trtemfl = 'Y')
   , term      = aedecod
   , by        = trt01a
   , reference = "Placebo"
   , threshold = 5
   , file      = &spl_out./figures/f_ae_risk
   , out       = f_ae_risk
 )

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
A wrong call writes the message and its fix to the log and stops. The macro also gives the messages every macro shares.

Message Fix max=<max> is not a positive whole number give max= the most terms to show, such as 30. reference=<reference> is not a group of by=<by> in denom=<denom> give reference= a value of <by> in quotes. data= and plot= are both given give data= to compute, or plot= to draw an out= again. plot=<plot> does not exist give plot= an out= of %aeplot (make it first). plot=<plot> has no variable <variable> give plot= the shape of out=: <the variables of out=>. par=<par> does not exist give par= an outpar= of %aeplot (make it first). par=<par> has no variables PARAMETER and VALUE give par= an outpar= of %aeplot. par=<par> has a row of no drawing parameter (with the PARAMETER of the record) give par= rows of outpar= of %aeplot only.

The macro also writes these NOTE lines to the log, without stopping:

  • NOTE: [aeplot] %_spl_nobs(_aeplot_all) terms qualified: the first <max> are shown.

docs.title: %ancova
docs.text:
Returns the Type III p-value of one numeric term in a linear model, such as the test of a dose response (test = trt01pn): the test of one numeric term, not a comparison of the groups.

Procedure: PROC GLM · Family: Test the groups

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%ancova(
     data   =
   , where  =
   , var    =
   , covars =
   , class  =
   , test   =
   , level  = 0.95
   , stats  = pval="X.XXX"
   , label  =
   , out    =
   , debug  = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set, with USUBJID. (required) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (paramcd = 'SYSBP' AND avisit = 'Week 12'). (optional) var= The response: one numeric variable. (required) covars= The covariates: numeric variables separated by blanks (covars = base). (optional) class= The class factors: variables separated by blanks (class = sex). (optional) test= The tested term: one numeric variable, such as a dose or the number of a treatment (test = trt01pn). (required) level= The confidence level of the limits: a number between 0 and 1. (optional, default 0.95) stats= The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with the pattern of its printed number, separated by blanks. The names are pval, estimate, se, lcl and ucl. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns. (optional, default pval="X.XXX") label= The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table. (optional) out= The name of the result data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets ancova. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the result shape: one row per statistic, of all subjects together (GROUPS is blank). STAT is pval, estimate, se, lcl or ucl.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
For the ANCOVA comparison of the groups, use %lsmeans; for a model of repeated visits, %mmrm. The model is PROC GLM: the class factors, the covariates and the tested term, one record per subject (the first with a value; when where= leaves a second record of a subject, the log has a NOTE with their number). Give a where= that leaves one record per subject, such as one parameter at one visit with anl01fl = 'Y'; otherwise each subject has the first of its records in the order of data=, whichever it is. The coefficient of the term, its standard error and its confidence limits come when stats= asks for them.

Good to know

This macro gives no comparison of the groups: the ANCOVA comparison of the groups (the differences of the LS means) is %lsmeans, and %table_model with method=ancova calls %lsmeans, not %ancova.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples run on the example data after examples/setup.sas. The output under each call is the output of that run. All examples of the reference run as one program: examples/reference.sas.

Tests a linear dose response of the change at Week 12, adjusted for baseline: one p value.

%ancova(
     data   = advs
   , where  = (paramcd = 'SYSBP' AND avisit = 'Week 12' AND anl01fl = 'Y')
   , var    = chg
   , covars = base
   , test   = trt01pn
   , label  = "Dose response"
   , out    = sbp_dose
 )

sbp_dose: 1 row
GROUPS  BLOCK          STAT         VALUE   TEXT
        Dose response  pval  0.0682011221  0.068

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
The macro gives only the messages every macro shares.

The macro also writes these NOTE lines to the log, without stopping:

  • NOTE: [ancova] <ndup> record(s) of where= are a second record of a subject:
  • NOTE: [ancova] the first record of each subject is used.

docs.title: %anova
docs.text:
Returns the p-value of the F test of a one-way analysis of variance of a variable between the groups.

Procedure: PROC GLM · Family: Test the groups

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%anova(
     data  =
   , where =
   , var   =
   , by    =
   , stats = pval="X.XXX"
   , label =
   , out   =
   , debug = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set. (required) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (anl01fl = 'Y'). (optional) var= The variable to analyse: one numeric variable. (required) by= The groups to compare: one variable. (required) stats= The statistic with its pattern of the printed number: pval. (optional, default pval="X.XXX") label= The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table. (optional) out= The name of the result data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets anova. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the result shape, one row: STAT pval, with GROUPS blank (all the groups together), BLOCK, VALUE and TEXT. When no record qualifies, the result has no row.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: Use %ttest or %wilcoxon to compare pairs of groups, and %ancova when the model has covariates. The model is var= by by= (PROC GLM). The p-value is that of the model, one test of all the groups together. A record with a missing value or a missing group is not used.

docs.title: %ard
docs.text:
Writes every number of a table to a CSV file, the numbers file.

Procedure: DATA steps (FILE, PUT) · Family: Build a table

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%ard(
     data    =
   , columns =
   , file    =
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The stacked results (out= of %stack). (required) columns= The columns (out= of %columns). When given, the N of each column comes first, as the result N. (optional) file= The name of the numbers file, without its extension. When not given, it is the name of the program that %study set; without %study, file= is required. (optional)

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The files: <out>/ard/<file>.csv, where <out> is the output folder that %study set and <file> is in lower case. Its columns: result (the name of the result), stat (the statistic), g1_value to g5_value (the values of the group variables in the order of GROUPS of the result: the column first, then the levels of the row, such as VERSUS of a comparison), raw (the value written with BEST32.: at most 15 significant digits and at most 14 decimals, the last digit cut, not rounded, so that 664/9 is 73.7777777777777; a whole number in full; blank for a missing value) and formatted (the printed text).

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use %csv for the records of a listing or the numbers of a figure. The numbers file has one line per number: the result it comes from, its statistic, the values of its groups, and the number as stored and as printed. The number as stored is the value written with the format BEST32.: at most 15 significant digits and at most 14 decimals, the digits after them cut, not rounded (664/9 is 73.7777777777777); the number as printed is the TEXT of the result. It reads the results, never the printed page, so that a second program, in SAS or R, can compare its numbers with this file.

  • With columns=, the first lines are the N of each column (the result N).
  • A number has the values of at most five groups (g1_value to g5_value), in the order of GROUPS.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples run on the example data after examples/setup.sas. The output under each call is the output of that run. They also read t14_2_1 (made by the example of %stack), t14_2_1_cols (made by the example of %columns). All examples of the reference run as one program: examples/reference.sas.

Before these examples: the calls that make their inputs

Run examples/setup.sas, then these calls from the examples of %describe, %anova, %freq, %chisq, %stack, %columns, in this order. Then the examples of this page run as shown.

/* from the example of %describe */
* Summarizes age in each group and in the Total: n, mean, SD, median, minimum and maximum.;
%describe(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes

docs.title: %barplot
docs.text:
Draws bars of the percent of each category by group as PNG and RTF files and returns the numbers drawn.

Procedure: PROC FREQ, PROC SGPANEL · Family: Figures

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%barplot(
     data    =
   , plot    =
   , par     =
   , columns =
   , denom   =
   , where   =
   , var     =
   , by      =
   , panel   =
   , stat    = percent
   , stacked = no
   , labels  = yes
   , xlabel  =
   , ylabel  =
   , ref     =
   , file    =
   , width   = 6.5in
   , height  = 4.5in
   , out     =
   , outpar  =
   , debug   = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: one record per subject and category, or per event. (required) plot= Draw again: the out= of an earlier %barplot call, changed or not. It is drawn as it is, and no statistic is computed. Give it instead of data=. (optional) par= The drawing parameters of an earlier %barplot call: its outpar=. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=. (optional) columns= The data set of %columns: it gives the order of the groups and their colours. When not given, the groups come in the order of the data. (optional) denom= The population: a data set with one row per subject (USUBJID) and the variable of by=. Its subjects in a group are the N of the percent. When not given, the N is the records of the group. (optional) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (anl01fl = 'Y'). (optional) var= The category: one variable (var = aesev). (required) by= The groups: one variable, one colour per group. (required) panel= A variable: one panel per value (panel = sex). (optional) stat= The statistic of a bar: percent or count. (optional, default percent) Accepts: percent, count. stacked= yes: stack the groups in one bar. (optional, default no) Accepts: yes, no. labels= yes: write the value on each bar. (optional, default yes) Accepts: yes, no. xlabel= The label of the x axis: a text in quotes. When not given, the label of var= (or its name). (optional) ylabel= The label of the y axis: a text in quotes. When not given, Subjects (%) or Records (%) for a percent, Subjects or Records for a count. (optional) ref= Reference lines on the y axis: one value or several, separated by blanks (ref = 0 50). (optional) file= The output file without its extension: the macro writes <file>.png (300 dpi) and <file>.rtf. (required) width= The width of the figure: a length with its unit (width = 9in). (optional, default 6.5in) height= The height of the figure: a length with its unit (height = 6in). (optional, default 4.5in) out= The name of the data set of the numbers drawn. When not given, they are not kept. (optional) outpar= The name of the data set of the drawing parameters, one row each. Give it to par= of a later call to draw the figure again. (optional) debug= yes: keep the work data sets barplot. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: one row per bar: the variables of panel= and by=, KIND (bar), X (the category as printed), Y (the percent or the count), N (the subjects or the records of the bar) and DENOM (the N of the percent). A category with no record in a group has no bar. The data set of outpar=: one row per drawing parameter, in the order of the table: PARAMETER ($32), its name, and VALUE ($500), its value as drawn (a label in quotes). The files: <file>.png and <file>.rtf.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use %aeplot for adverse events with their risk differences. With denom=, a bar is the percent of the subjects of the group in the population, and a subject counts once in a category; without it, the percent of the records of the group. stat=count gives the count instead of the percent. The groups stand side by side, or stacked in one bar with stacked=yes; the value is written on each bar. A record with a missing category, group or panel is not used. To draw the figure again without computing, give plot= the out= and par= the outpar= of an earlier call.

Good to know

Draw again: plot= takes the out= of an earlier %barplot call, changed or not, and draws it as it is, with no statistic computed: the categories in the order of their first row, and the value on a bar with one decimal unless every Y is its N (a count). par= takes the outpar= of that call and gives the drawing parameters: columns, by, panel, stacked, labels, xlabel, ylabel, ref, file, width, height. These change the picture, not the numbers. The other parameters compute; with plot= the log has a NOTE for each one given, as it is not used. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=, and the row wins over the default of the table.

docs.title: %baseline
docs.text:
Gives every record of a group the value of the group's baseline record, as a new variable such as BASE.

Procedure: PROC SORT, MERGE · Family: ADaM steps

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%baseline(
     data    =
   , value   =
   , by      =
   , flag    = ABLFL
   , replace = no
   , new     =
   , debug   = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The data set to change in place, such as advs. (required) value= The variable whose baseline value is taken, such as aval. (required) by= The groups, each with one baseline record: variables separated by blanks (by = usubjid paramcd). (required) flag= The baseline flag: a character variable that is 'Y' on the baseline record. (optional, default ABLFL) replace= yes: data= has the variable new= already; the macro drops it and makes it again, with the type and length of value=. With no, the values are written into the variable new= of data= when it has one (its type, length and label stay). (optional, default no) new= The name of the new variable, such as base. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets baseline. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data sets: data=, changed in place: the variable new= on every record, with the value of value= on the baseline record of its group. A group with no baseline record gets a missing value.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: The macro does not make the change from baseline: CHG = AVAL - BASE is a DATA step after %baseline (the how-to guide "Derive analysis visits, the baseline and the change from baseline" shows all the steps). The baseline record is the one whose flag= variable is 'Y'. A group with no baseline record gets a missing value. The rows of data= keep their order. When a group has two baseline records, the log has an ERROR line that names the group, and data= is not changed.

docs.title: %boxplot
docs.text:
Draws box plots of a variable in each group as PNG and RTF files and returns the numbers drawn.

Procedure: PROC MEANS, PROC SGPANEL · Family: Figures

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%boxplot(
     data     =
   , plot     =
   , par      =
   , columns  =
   , where    =
   , y        =
   , x        =
   , by       =
   , panel    =
   , outliers = yes
   , mean     = yes
   , xformat  =
   , xlabel   =
   , ylabel   =
   , ref      =
   , file     =
   , width    = 6.5in
   , height   = 4.5in
   , out      =
   , outpar   =
   , debug    = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: one record per value. (required) plot= Draw again: the out= of an earlier %boxplot call, changed or not. It is drawn as it is, and no statistic is computed. Give it instead of data=. (optional) par= The drawing parameters of an earlier %boxplot call: its outpar=. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=. (optional) columns= The data set of %columns: it gives the order of the groups and their colours. When not given, the groups come in the order of the data. (optional) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (anl01fl = 'Y'). (optional) y= The variable of the boxes: one numeric variable (y = aval). (required) x= The category of the x axis: one variable, such as the visit (x = avisitn). When not given, there is one box per group. (optional) by= The groups: one variable, one box per group. (required) panel= A variable: one panel per value, one under the other, each with its own y axis (panel = paramcd). (optional) outliers= yes: show the values beyond the whiskers as markers. (optional, default yes) Accepts: yes, no. mean= yes: show the mean as a marker in the box. (optional, default yes) Accepts: yes, no. xformat= The format of the categories of x, as in a FORMAT statement (xformat = visfmt.). When not given, the format of x. (optional) xlabel= The label of the x axis: a text in quotes. When not given, the label of x= (or its name). (optional) ylabel= The label of the y axis: a text in quotes. When not given, the label of y= (or its name). (optional) ref= Reference lines on the y axis: one value or several, separated by blanks (ref = 0 50). (optional) file= The output file without its extension: the macro writes <file>.png (300 dpi) and <file>.rtf. (required) width= The width of the figure: a length with its unit (width = 9in). (optional, default 6.5in) height= The height of the figure: a length with its unit (height = 6in). (optional, default 4.5in) out= The name of the data set of the numbers drawn. When not given, they are not kept. (optional) outpar= The name of the data set of the drawing parameters, one row each. Give it to par= of a later call to draw the figure again. (optional) debug= yes: keep the work data sets boxplot. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: one row per box: the variables of panel= and by=, KIND (box), X (the category; missing without x=), N, MEAN, MEDIAN, Q1, Q3, MIN, MAX, WLOW and WHIGH. WLOW and WHIGH are the ends of the whiskers: the smallest and the largest value within Q1 - 1.5 IQR and Q3 + 1.5 IQR. The data set of outpar=: one row per drawing parameter, in the order of the table: PARAMETER ($32), its name, and VALUE ($500), its value as drawn (a label in quotes). The files: <file>.png and <file>.rtf.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use %meanplot for the mean and its error bars only. With x=, there is one box per group at each visit. The box goes from Q1 to Q3, with a line at the median and a marker at the mean. The whiskers go to the most extreme values within 1.5 times the interquartile range of the box; the values beyond them are outliers. The quantiles are those of PROC MEANS with QNTLDEF=5 and of VBOX (its default PERCENTILE=5; R quantile type 2). A record with a missing value, category, group or panel is not used. To draw the figure again without computing, give plot= the out= and par= the outpar= of an earlier call.

Good to know

Draw again: plot= takes the out= of an earlier %boxplot call, changed or not, and draws it as it is, with no statistic computed, each box from its statistics: the whiskers from WLOW to WHIGH, the box from Q1 to Q3 with the line of the MEDIAN, the MEAN, and as outliers only MIN and MAX when they are beyond a whisker (out= has no other value; from data= every outlier is drawn). par= takes the outpar= of that call and gives the drawing parameters: columns, by, panel, outliers, mean, xformat, xlabel, ylabel, ref, file, width, height. These change the picture, not the numbers. The other parameters compute; with plot= the log has a NOTE for each one given, as it is not used. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=, and the row wins over the default of the table.

docs.title: %chisq
docs.text:
Returns the p-value of the Pearson chi-square test of the groups against the categories of a response.

Procedure: PROC FREQ (CHISQ, FISHER) · Family: Test the groups

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%chisq(
     data   =
   , where  =
   , var    =
   , by     =
   , within =
   , exact  = no
   , stats  = pval="X.XXX"
   , label  =
   , out    =
   , debug  = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: the records, with USUBJID. (required) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (avisit = 'Week 24'). (optional) var= The categories of the response: one variable, numeric or character. (required) by= The groups to compare: one variable. (required) within= One test in each group of these variables, separated by blanks, such as a parameter and a visit (within = paramcd avisit). (optional) exact= yes: Fisher's exact test of the same table instead of the chi-square test. (optional, default no) Accepts: yes, no. stats= The statistic pval and the pattern of its printed number, such as stats = pval="X.XXXX". (optional, default pval="X.XXX") label= The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table. (optional) out= The name of the result data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets chisq. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the result shape: one row with STAT pval, or one row per group of within= with the variables of within=. GROUPS has the names of the within= variables. VALUE is missing where PROC FREQ makes no test (a table with one row or one column).

docs.title: Details
docs.text: Use %fisher for subjects with a record against subjects without (an adverse event), and %cmh for a test within strata. The test has no continuity correction. Each subject counts once in each group and category. A record with a missing group, category or value of within= is not used. With exact=yes the macro gives Fisher's exact test of the same table.

docs.text:

 )

docs.title: %cmh
docs.text:
Returns the p-value of the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test of the groups against the categories of a response, within strata.

Procedure: PROC FREQ (CMH) · Family: Test the groups

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%cmh(
     data      =
   , where     =
   , var       =
   , by        =
   , strata    =
   , within    =
   , statistic = general
   , stats     = pval="X.XXX"
   , label     =
   , out       =
   , debug     = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: the records, with USUBJID. (required) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (avisit = 'Week 24'). (optional) var= The categories of the response: one variable; numeric for statistic=rowmean. (required) by= The groups to compare: one variable. (required) strata= The stratification variables, separated by blanks (strata = sitegr1). When not given, the test has one stratum. (optional) within= One test in each group of these variables, separated by blanks, such as a parameter and a visit (within = paramcd avisit). (optional) statistic= The test: general (general association) or rowmean (the mean scores of the groups differ). (optional, default general) Accepts: general, rowmean. stats= The statistic pval and the pattern of its printed number, such as stats = pval="X.XXXX". (optional, default pval="X.XXX") label= The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table. (optional) out= The name of the result data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets cmh. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the result shape: one row with STAT pval, or one row per group of within= with the variables of within=. GROUPS has the names of the within= variables. VALUE is missing where PROC FREQ makes no test.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use %chisq for the same test without strata. Each subject counts once in each group, category and stratum. A record with a missing group, category or value of within= is not used. statistic= chooses the test:

  • general: the test of general association
  • rowmean: the test that the mean scores of the groups differ; the scores are the values of the numeric response (SCORES=TABLE)

docs.title: %columns
docs.text:
Returns the columns of a table: one row per column, with its N and the header that shows the N.

Procedure: PROC SUMMARY · Family: Build a table

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%columns(
     data  =
   , n     =
   , var   =
   , order =
   , page  =
   , total = no
   , out   =
   , debug = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The stacked results (out= of %stack). (required) n= The population: a data set with USUBJID and the column variable, such as adsl. Each subject counts once in the N of its column. When not given, the columns have no N. (optional) var= The column variable: one variable, the first variable of by= of the statistics macros (var = trt01a). (required) order= The numeric twin of var= in n=, such as order = trt01an: the columns are in its order. When not given, the columns are in the order of their values. (optional) page= A variable of the results and of n=, such as page = sex: one page per value. The N of a column is then the N of its page. Give %layout the same page=. (optional) total= yes: the results have the group Total (total = yes of the statistics macros); it is the last column, and its N is all subjects of n=. A text in quotes is the other name that the statistics macros gave the Total. (optional, default no) out= The name of the data set of the columns. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets columns. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: one row per column: COL (its number: 1, 2 ...), COLVALUE (the value of var=), BIGN (the N) and HEADER (the value, a | and (N=86); %print splits a header at the |). With page=: one row per page and column, the page variable first; BIGN is the N of the page (0: no subject of the column on the page).

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
A header is the value, a | and the N: Placebo|(N=86). %layout reads it to place each number and to label each column; the N comes from the population of n=, not from the counts of %freq.

  • The columns are the values of the column variable in the results and in the population.
  • They are in the order of the numeric twin of order=, else of their values; the Total is last.
  • The N of a column is the number of subjects of n= with its value; the N of the Total is all subjects of n=.
  • Without n= the columns have no N, and the header is the value alone.
  • With page= each page has the same columns, and the N of a column is the N of its page: with page = sex on the example data, Placebo|(N=33) on the page of the males and Placebo|(N=53) on the page of the females.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples run on the example data after examples/setup.sas. The output under each call is the output of that run. They also read t14_2_1 (made by the example of %stack), t14_1_1 (made by the example of %stack). All examples of the reference run as one program: examples/reference.sas.

Before these examples: the calls that make their inputs

Run examples/setup.sas, then these calls from the examples of %describe, %anova, %freq, %chisq, %stack, in this order. Then the examples of this page run as shown.

/* from the example of %describe */
* Summarizes age in each group and in the Total: n, mean, SD, median, minimum and maximum.;
%describe(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_describe
 )
* Adds sex as a second BY variable: the rows of each group and sex, for a page per sex.;
%describe(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a sex
   , total = yes
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_sex
 )
/* from the example of %anova */
* Tests age across the three groups: one row, the p value of the F test.;
%anova(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_anova
 )
/* from the example of %freq */
* Counts each sex in each group and in the Total: n and the percent of the subjects of the group.;
%freq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_freq
 )
* Adds sex as a second BY variable: the age groups of each group and sex, for a page per sex.;
%freq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = agegr1
   , by    = trt01a sex
   , total = yes
   , label = "Age group"
   , out   = agegr_sex
 )
/* from the example of %chisq */
* Tests sex across the groups: one row, the p value of the chi square test.;
%chisq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_chisq
 )
/* from the example of %stack */
* Stacks four results in the order of the table: RESULT and ORD tell where each row came from.;
%stack(age_describe age_anova sex_freq sex_chisq, out=t14_2_1)
* Stacks age and the age groups by sex: the results of a table with a page per sex.;
%stack(age_sex agegr_sex, out=t14_1_1)

Makes the four columns with their N from adsl, the Total last, in the order of TRT01AN.

%columns(
     data  = t14_2_1
   , n     = adsl
   , var   = trt01a
   , order = trt01an
   , total = yes
   , out   = t14_2_1_cols
 )

docs.title: %cox
docs.text:
Returns the hazard ratio of pairs of groups from a Cox proportional hazards model, with its confidence limits and p-value.

Procedure: PROC PHREG (LSMEANS); PROC LIFETEST for pvalue=logrank · Family: Time to an event

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%cox(
     data   =
   , where  =
   , var    =
   , by     =
   , cnsr   = CNSR
   , within =
   , covars =
   , class  =
   , strata =
   , pairs  = all
   , order  =
   , ties   = efron
   , pvalue = wald
   , level  = 0.95
   , stats  = hr="XX.XX" lcl="XX.XX" ucl="XX.XX" pval="X.XXX"
   , label  =
   , out    =
   , debug  = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: one record per subject, with USUBJID, the time and the censoring variable. (required) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (paramcd = 'TTDE'). (optional) var= The time: one numeric variable, such as aval. (required) by= The groups of the model: one character variable. (required) cnsr= The censoring variable: one numeric variable, 0 for an event and a positive value for a censoring (the ADaM CNSR: 1, 2 ... name the reason). A missing or negative value on a record used stops the macro with an ERROR. (optional, default CNSR) within= One model in each group of these variables, separated by blanks (within = sex for the levels of a subgroup). A record with a missing value of one of them is not used. (optional) covars= The numeric covariates of the model, separated by blanks (covars = age). (optional) class= The class factors of the model, separated by blanks (class = sitegr1). (optional) strata= The strata of the model, separated by blanks (strata = sitegr1). When not given, the model has no strata. (optional) pairs= The pairs of groups to compare. all: each later group against each earlier one, in the order of order= (or of the values). Or a list of pairs separated by #: the group first, then the group it is compared with, each value in quotes ("Drug" "Placebo" # "High" "Low"). (optional, default all) order= The order of the groups: one numeric variable with one value per group (order = trt01pn). (optional) ties= The method for tied times: efron, breslow, or exact (TIES=DISCRETE of PROC PHREG, which coxph of R calls exact). discrete is accepted as another name of exact. (optional, default efron) Accepts: efron, breslow, exact, discrete. pvalue= The p-value of each pair: wald (the Wald test of the pair in the model) or logrank (the log-rank test of the two groups of the pair, in the strata). logrank is not possible with within=. (optional, default wald) Accepts: wald, logrank. level= The confidence level: a number between 0 and 1. (optional, default 0.95) stats= The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with its pattern of the printed number, separated by blanks. The names are hr, lcl, ucl and pval. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns. (optional, default hr="XX.XX" lcl="XX.XX" ucl="XX.XX" pval="X.XXX") label= The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table. (optional) out= The name of the result data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets cox. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the result shape, one row per pair and statistic: the BY variable (the group), VERSUS (the group it is compared with), the variables of within=, GROUPS, BLOCK, STAT, VALUE and TEXT. hr is the hazard of the group over the hazard of VERSUS (a hazard ratio below 1: fewer events in the group, as its hazard is lower), lcl and ucl its confidence limits, pval its p-value. With pairs=all the group is the later one in the order of order=. GROUPS is the name of the BY variable, VERSUS and the names of within=.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use %logrank for the test of all groups together without a model, and %interaction_phreg for the test of a treatment-by-subgroup interaction. The model has the groups, the covariates and the class factors. With strata=, each combination of the values of the strata variables is a stratum with its own baseline hazard. All pairs come from one fit: hr is the hazard ratio, lcl and ucl are its Wald confidence limits, and pval is the Wald p-value of the pair. With pvalue=logrank, pval is the log-rank test of the two groups of the pair, in the same strata (PROC LIFETEST); the hazard ratio and its limits stay those of the model. The model uses one record per subject (in each group of within=). CNSR 0 is an event and any positive value is a censoring, as in ADaM, where the value names the reason of the censoring: a CNSR of 2 is censored as 1 is. A record used with a missing or negative CNSR stops the macro with an ERROR.

Good to know

The ties of the library are Efron's, as in coxph of R; PROC PHREG by itself uses Breslow's.

Procedure: DATA steps (FILE, PUT) · Family: Build a table

docs.title: Syntax

%csv(
     data   =

 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The records: the data set of the listing, or out= of a figure macro. (required) var= The variables to write: names separated by blanks, in the order of the columns. (required) folder= The folder in the outputs: listings or figures. (optional, default listings) Accepts: listings, figures. file= The name of the CSV file, without its extension. (required)

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The files: <out>/<folder>/<file>.csv, where <out> is the output folder that %study set: a line with the names of var=, then one line per record.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: Use %ard for the numbers of a table. The first line has the names of the variables, in upper case; then one line per record, in the order of the data. The values are written with their formats, so that a second program, in SAS or R, can compare its listing or figure with this file.

docs.title: %describe
docs.text:
Returns the descriptive statistics of a numeric variable in each group: n, mean, SD, median, minimum and maximum.

Procedure: PROC MEANS · Family: Describe the data

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%describe(
     data    =
   , where   =
   , var     =
   , by      =
   , keep    =
   , total   = no
   , qntldef = 5
   , stats   = n="XX" mean="XX.X" sd="XX.XX" median="XX.X" min="XX" max="XX"
   , label   =
   , out     =
   , debug   = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set. (required) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (anl01fl = 'Y'). When not given, all records are used. (optional) var= The variable to describe: one numeric variable. (required) by= The groups: one variable or several, separated by blanks. The first variable gives the columns of the table; the others give its rows, such as a parameter and a visit (by = trt01a paramcd avisit). (required) keep= Other variables to keep in the result, separated by blanks, for the names and the order of the rows (keep = param avisitn). Each gets its largest value in the group (the ID statement of PROC MEANS). (optional) total= yes: add the group "Total", all groups of the first BY variable together. A text in quotes gives the Total another name ("All subjects"). A record with a missing group is counted in no group and not in the Total. (optional, default no) qntldef= The definition of the quantiles: a number from 1 to 5, as QNTLDEF= of PROC MEANS (5 is the default of SAS). (optional, default 5) stats= The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with its pattern of the printed number, separated by blanks. The names are n, mean, sd, median, min, max, q1, q3 and se. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: XX for n, min and max; XX.X for mean, median, q1 and q3; XX.XX for sd and se. (optional, default n="XX" mean="XX.X" sd="XX.XX" median="XX.X" min="XX" max="XX") label= The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table. (optional) out= The name of the result data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets describe. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the result shape, one row per group and statistic: the BY variables, the variables of keep=, GROUPS, BLOCK, STAT, VALUE and TEXT. A group with no value has no row. When no record has a value, the result has no row and the log has the NOTE "No data qualified".

docs.title: Details
docs.text: Use %freq for the subjects of each category of a variable. Only the values that are not missing count. Q1, Q3 and the standard error come when stats= asks for them. The default pattern of min and max is XX, a whole number: a lab value of 3.9 prints as 4. Give min="XX.X" max="XX.X" in stats= for values with decimals.

docs.title: %fisher
docs.text:
Returns the p-value of Fisher's exact test of the subjects with a record against the subjects without, between groups.

Procedure: PROC FREQ (FISHER, CHISQ) · Family: Test the groups

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%fisher(
     data   =
   , denom  =
   , where  =
   , by     =
   , within =
   , exact  = yes
   , stats  = pval="X.XXX"
   , label  =
   , out    =
   , debug  = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: the records (adverse events), with USUBJID. (required) denom= The subjects, one row each, with USUBJID and the variable of by=: a data set, with data set options if needed, such as denom = adsl(where = (saffl = 'Y')). (required) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (trtemfl = 'Y'). (optional) by= The groups to compare: one variable of denom=. (required) within= One test in each group of these variables of data=, separated by blanks, such as each preferred term (within = aedecod). (optional) exact= no: the Pearson chi-square test of the same table instead of Fisher's exact test. (optional, default yes) Accepts: yes, no. stats= The statistic pval and the pattern of its printed number, such as stats = pval="X.XXXX". (optional, default pval="X.XXX") label= The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table. (optional) out= The name of the result data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets fisher. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the result shape: one row with STAT pval, or one row per group of within= with the variables of within=. GROUPS has the names of the within= variables. VALUE is missing where no test can be made (one group, or all subjects with a record, or none).

docs.title: Details
docs.text: Use it for an adverse event between treatments; use %chisq for the categories of a response, and %cmh for a test within strata. Every subject of denom= counts, with a record in data= or without. A subject with a missing group in denom= is not used. With exact=no the macro gives the Pearson chi-square test of the same table.

Flags the first or last record of each group, among the records that meet a condition, with Y.

Procedure: PROC SORT, MERGE · Family: ADaM steps

docs.title: Syntax

%flag_first(
     data  =
   , where =
   , by    =
   , order =
   , which = first
   , new   =
   , debug = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The data set to change in place, such as advs. (required) where= The records that can be flagged: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (anl01fl = 'Y'). When not given, all records can be flagged. (optional) by= The groups: variables separated by blanks (by = usubjid paramcd). (required) order= The sort keys within a group: variables separated by blanks; write descending before a key as in a BY statement (order = descending adt). (required) which= first or last: the record of the group that gets the flag. (optional, default first) Accepts: first, last. new= The name of the flag variable to make. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets flag_first. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data sets: data=, changed in place: the character variable new= ($1), Y on the first (or last) record of each group among the records that meet where=, blank on the other records.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: Use %pick to copy the value of such a record to a subject. Use %flag_if_any to flag the subjects that have any record that meets a condition. The records of a group are sorted by order=. A missing sort key sorts last. Records with equal keys keep their order. The other records get a blank flag. The rows of data= keep their order.

docs.title: %forestplot
docs.text:
Draws a forest plot of estimates in subgroups as PNG and RTF files and returns the numbers drawn.

Procedure: PROC SUMMARY, PROC SGPLOT · Family: Figures

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%forestplot(
     data     =
   , plot     =
   , par      =
   , columns  =
   , where    =
   , estimate =
   , lower    = lcl
   , upper    = ucl
   , within   =
   , group    =
   , by       =
   , scale    = log
   , text     = yes
   , xlabel   = "Estimate (95% CI)"
   , ref      = 1
   , file     =
   , width    = 6.5in
   , height   = 4.5in
   , out      =
   , outpar   =
   , debug    = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: a result (rows of STAT and VALUE) of a comparison called with within=, with the variables of within=. (required) plot= Draw again: the out= of an earlier %forestplot call, changed or not. It is drawn as it is, and no statistic is computed. Give it instead of data=. (optional) par= The drawing parameters of an earlier %forestplot call: its outpar=. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=. (optional) columns= The data set of %columns: it gives the order of the groups and their colours. When not given, the groups come in the order of the data. (optional) where= The rows of the result to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (versus = 'Placebo'). (optional) estimate= The statistic of the estimate: a value of STAT, such as hr, or, irr, rr, rd or diff. (required) lower= The statistic of the lower limit: a value of STAT. (optional, default lcl) upper= The statistic of the upper limit: a value of STAT. (optional, default ucl) within= The factors: variables of the result separated by blanks, one per factor, in the order of the rows (within = sex agegr1). A row belongs to the first of them that has a value. (required) group= A variable with the heading of each factor. When not given, the heading is the label of the variable of within=. (optional) by= The group of a pair: a variable of the result. When the result has VERSUS, the pair is the group of by= against VERSUS. Each pair has its own colour. (optional) scale= The scale of the x axis: log (for a ratio) or linear (for a difference). (optional, default log) Accepts: log, linear. text= yes: write the estimate and its limits, as "estimate (lower, upper)", at the right under the name of the statistic, with the n when the result has a statistic n. (optional, default yes) Accepts: yes, no. xlabel= The label of the x axis: a text in quotes. (optional, default "Estimate (95% CI)") ref= The line of no difference on the x axis: one value, 1 for a ratio or 0 for a difference. (optional, default 1) file= The output file without its extension: the macro writes <file>.png (300 dpi) and <file>.rtf. (required) width= The width of the figure: a length with its unit (width = 9in). (optional, default 6.5in) height= The height of the figure: a length with its unit (height = 6in). (optional, default 4.5in) out= The name of the data set of the numbers drawn. When not given, they are not kept. (optional) outpar= The name of the data set of the drawing parameters, one row each. Give it to par= of a later call to draw the figure again. (optional) debug= yes: keep the work data sets forestplot. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: one row per level and pair: FACTOR (the variable of within=), LEVEL (its value as printed), PAIR (the group of by= against VERSUS; blank without by=), KIND (estimate), X (the estimate), LOWER, UPPER and N (missing when the result has no statistic n). The data set of outpar=: one row per drawing parameter, in the order of the table: PARAMETER ($32), its name, and VALUE ($500), its value as drawn (a label in quotes). The files: <file>.png and <file>.rtf.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
It computes no statistic: it draws a result of %cox, %logistic, %rateratio, %lsmeans or %risk called with within=, so the figure and the table of the same result cannot differ. A result is the data set a statistics macro writes, one row per number. For the test of the treatment-by-subgroup interaction, use the %interaction_* macros. Each factor of within= has a heading row, with one row per level under it. The estimate is a marker and its confidence interval a bar; a line marks no difference. A ratio has a log axis (scale=log). With text=yes, the estimate and its limits are also written as text at the right. To draw the figure again without computing, give plot= the out= and par= the outpar= of an earlier call.

Good to know

Draw again: plot= takes the out= of an earlier %forestplot call, changed or not, and draws it as it is, with no statistic computed: the factors, levels and pairs in the order of its rows, each factor under the heading of its name. par= takes the outpar= of that call and gives the drawing parameters: columns, estimate (with plot= only for the name over the text column), scale, text, xlabel, ref, file, width, height. These change the picture, not the numbers. The other parameters compute; with plot= the log has a NOTE for each one given, as it is not used. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=, and the row wins over the default of the table.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples run on the example data after examples/setup.sas. The output under each call is the output of that run. They also read hr_sub (made by the example of %stack), t14_2_1_cols (made by the example of %columns). All examples of the reference run as one program: examples/reference.sas.

Before these examples: the calls that make their inputs

Run examples/setup.sas, then these calls from the examples of %tte, %describe, %anova, %freq, %chisq, %cox, %stack, %columns, in this order. Then the examples of this page run as shown.

/* from the example of %tte */
* Makes TTDE. Log NOTE: 2 subject(s) with no event and no censoring date: no record (no TRTEDT).;
%tte(
     subjects      = adsl
   , events        = adae
   , event         = trtemfl = 'Y' AND aebodsys = 'SKIN AND SUBCUTANEOUS TISSUE DISORDERS'
   , date          = astdt
   , start         = trtsdt
   , censor_date   = trtedt
   , seq           = aeseq
   , censor_desc   = "End of treatment"
   , censor_source = "ADSL"
   , event_desc    = aedecod
   , source        = "ADAE"
   , paramcd       = "TTDE"
   , out           = adttde
 )
/* from the example of %describe */
* Summarizes age in each group and in the Total: n, mean, SD, median, minimum and maximum.;
%describe(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_describe
 )
/* from the example of %anova */
* Tests age across the three groups: one row, the p value of the F test.;
%anova(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_anova
 )
/* from the example of %freq */
* Counts each sex in each group and in the Total: n and the percent of the subjects of the group.;
%freq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_freq
 )
/* from the example of %chisq */
* Tests sex across the groups: one row, the p value of the chi square test.;
%chisq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_chisq
 )
/* from the example of %cox */
* Gives the hazard ratio against Placebo for each sex: the rows carry SEX, for a forest plot.;
%cox(
     data   = adttde
   , var    = aval
   , by     = trt01a
   , within = sex
   , pairs  = "Xanomeline High Dose" "Placebo"
            # "Xanomeline Low Dose"  "Placebo"
   , out    = hr_sex
 )
* Gives the hazard ratio against Placebo for each age group.;
%cox(
     data   = adttde
   , var    = aval
   , by     = trt01a
   , within = agegr1
   , pairs  = "Xanomeline High Dose" "Placebo"
            # "Xanomeline Low Dose"  "Placebo"
   , out    = hr_age
 )
/* from the example of %stack */
* Stacks four results in the order of the table: RESULT and ORD tell where each row came from.;
%stack(age_describe age_anova sex_freq sex_chisq, out=t14_2_1)
* Stacks the hazard ratios by sex and by age group, for one forest plot.;
%stack(hr_sex hr_age, out=hr_sub)
/* from the example of %columns */
* Makes the four columns with their N from adsl, the Total last, in the order of TRT01AN.;
%columns(
     data  = t14_2_1
   , n     = adsl
   , var   = trt01a
   , order = trt01an
   , total = yes
   , out   = t14_2_1_cols
 )

Draws the hazard ratios of each subgroup on a log scale, with the reference line at 1.

%forestplot(
     data     = hr_sub
   , columns  = t14_2_1_cols
   , estimate = hr
   , within   = sex agegr1
   , by       = trt01a
   , scale    = log
   , ref      = 1
   , file     = &spl_out./figures/f_hr_sub
   , out      = f_hr_sub
 )

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
A wrong call writes the message and its fix to the log and stops. The macro also gives the messages every macro shares.

Message Fix data=<data> has no STAT and VALUE: it is not a result give data= the out= of a comparison with within=. estimate=<estimate> is not a statistic (STAT) of data=<data>. give estimate= a statistic of the results (hr, or, rd). data= and plot= are both given give data= to compute, or plot= to draw an out= again. plot=<plot> does not exist give plot= an out= of %forestplot (make it first). plot=<plot> has no variable <variable> give plot= the shape of out=: <the variables of out=>. par=<par> does not exist give par= an outpar= of %forestplot (make it first). par=<par> has no variables PARAMETER and VALUE give par= an outpar= of %forestplot. par=<par> has a row of no drawing parameter (with the PARAMETER of the record) give par= rows of outpar= of %forestplot only.
