docs.title: %freq
docs.text:
Counts the subjects in each category and group, with their percent of the subjects of the group.

Procedure: PROC FREQ · Family: Describe the data

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%freq(
     data      =
   , denom     =
   , where     =
   , var       =
   , by        =
   , keep      =
   , levels    =
   , total     = no
   , threshold =
   , order     =
   , orderof   =
   , orderby   =
   , stats     = n="XX" pct="(XX.X%)"
   , label     =
   , out       =
   , debug     = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: the records to count, with USUBJID. (required) denom= The subjects of each group: the N of the percent and the columns. A data set with one row per subject and the variables of by=; data set options are allowed: adsl(where=(saffl = 'Y')). When not given, the subjects of data= (without where=). (optional) where= The records to count: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (trtemfl = 'Y'). (optional) var= The categories: one variable or several, separated by blanks, nested in their order (var = aebodsys aedecod: a term within its class). When not given, the macro counts the subjects with any record. (optional) by= The groups: one variable or several, separated by blanks. The first variable gives the columns of the table; the others give its rows or its pages (by = trt01a sex, with page= of %layout). (required) keep= Other variables to keep with the categories for their names and order, separated by blanks. PARAM and PARAMN go with PARAMCD, AVISITN with AVISIT, any <V>N with V. Each gets the value of the first record of its category. (optional) levels= The planned categories of some variables of var=: each variable followed by its values in quotes (levels = bnrind 'LOW' 'NORMAL' 'HIGH'). A planned category shows also without a subject; a record of another category is not counted. The rows of a planned variable V follow the order given, through its twin VN (1, 2 ...) in out=, unless keep= has VN. The categories of the other variables come from the records counted. (optional) total= yes: add the group "Total", all groups of the first BY variable together. A text in quotes gives the Total another name ("All subjects"). The first BY variable must be character. (optional, default no) threshold= A percent (threshold = 5): keep only the categories with this percent of the subjects or more in at least one group (the Total counts as a group). The macro compares the percent itself, not its rounded text. (optional) order= frequency: order the rows of orderof= by their subjects, the most first, and equal counts by their value. The rank goes into the twin <V>N, and %print orders the rows by it. When not given, the rows are in the order of the values. (optional) orderof= The variable of var= whose rows order=frequency ranks: one variable. When not given, the last variable of var=. (optional) orderby= The group whose subjects rank the rows for order=frequency: a value of the first BY variable, in quotes (orderby = "Placebo"). When not given, all groups together, without the Total. (optional) stats= The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with its pattern of the printed number, separated by blanks. The names are n, pct and events. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns. (optional, default n="XX" pct="(XX.X%)") label= The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table. (optional) out= The name of the result data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets freq. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the result shape, one row per group, category and statistic: the variables of by= and var=, the variables of keep=, GROUPS, BLOCK, STAT, VALUE and TEXT. Every group of denom= has every category: n = 0 when no subject has it. With levels=, the twin <V>N of each planned variable gives its place in levels=; with order=frequency, the twin of orderof= gives the rank.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: Use %proportion when the percent needs a confidence interval, and %worst for the worst grade of each subject. A subject is counted once in each cell. A record with a missing group or category is not counted. The percent is of the subjects of the group in denom=. Without var=, the macro counts the subjects with any record. The name events in stats= adds the number of records of each cell.

docs.title: %interaction_genmod
docs.text:
Returns the p-value of the treatment-by-subgroup interaction in a Poisson or negative binomial model of a count.

Procedure: PROC GENMOD · Family: Subgroups

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%interaction_genmod(
     data     =
   , where    =
   , var      =
   , by       =
   , factor   =
   , exposure =
   , covars   =
   , class    =
   , dist     = poisson
   , stats    = pval="X.XXX"
   , label    =
   , out      =
   , debug    = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: one record per subject, with USUBJID. (required) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (ittfl = 'Y'). (optional) var= The count: one numeric variable, such as the number of events of each subject. (required) by= The groups of the model, the treatment: one variable. (required) factor= The factor of the subgroups: one variable whose values are its levels (factor = sex). (required) exposure= The exposure of each subject: a numeric variable, or an expression of it (exposure = trtdurd / 365.25). It must be above 0, because the offset is its logarithm. (required) covars= The numeric covariates of the model, separated by blanks (covars = base). (optional) class= The other class factors of the model, separated by blanks (class = sitegr1). (optional) dist= The distribution of the count: poisson or negbin (nb is accepted as another name of negbin). (optional, default poisson) Accepts: poisson, negbin, nb. stats= The statistic with its pattern of the printed number: pval. (optional, default pval="X.XXX") label= The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table. (optional) out= The name of the result data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets interaction_genmod. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the result shape, one row for all groups and levels together: GROUPS (blank), BLOCK, STAT (pval), VALUE and TEXT.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: Use %interaction_glm for a continuous variable, %interaction_logistic for a response, and %interaction_phreg for a time to an event. The macro fits two models with PROC GENMOD, with the logarithm of the exposure as the offset: the groups, the covariates, the class factors and the factor; and the same model with the treatment-by-factor terms. In a negative binomial model, each fit estimates its own dispersion k. pval is the likelihood-ratio test: twice the difference of the full log likelihoods of the two fits, with the difference of the numbers of their estimated coefficients. The models use one record per subject: a record with a missing count, group or level is not used.

docs.text:

docs.text:
Returns the p-value of the treatment-by-subgroup interaction in a linear model of a continuous variable.

Procedure: PROC GLM · Family: Subgroups

docs.text:
%interaction_glm(
     data   =
   , where  =
   , var    =
   , by     =
   , factor =
   , covars =
   , class  =
   , stats  = pval="X.XXX"
   , label  =
   , out    =
   , debug  = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: one record per subject, with USUBJID. (required) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (ittfl = 'Y'). (optional) var= The variable of the model: one numeric variable, such as chg. (required) by= The groups of the model, the treatment: one variable. (required) factor= The factor of the subgroups: one variable whose values are its levels (factor = sex). (required) covars= The numeric covariates of the model, separated by blanks (covars = base). (optional) class= The other class factors of the model, separated by blanks (class = sitegr1). (optional) stats= The statistic with its pattern of the printed number: pval. (optional, default pval="X.XXX") label= The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table. (optional) out= The name of the result data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets interaction_glm. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the result shape, one row for all groups and levels together: GROUPS (blank), BLOCK, STAT (pval), VALUE and TEXT.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: Use %interaction_logistic for a response, %interaction_genmod for a count with its exposure, and %interaction_phreg for a time to an event. The model has the groups, the covariates, the class factors, the factor and the treatment-by-factor terms. pval is the Type III F test of the treatment-by-factor terms (PROC GLM). For this term of the highest order, the test is the same as the F test of the model with the terms against the model without them. The model uses one record per subject: a record with a missing value, group or level is not used.

docs.title: %interaction_phreg
docs.text:
Returns the p-value of the treatment-by-subgroup interaction in a Cox model of a time to an event.

Procedure: PROC PHREG · Family: Subgroups

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%interaction_phreg(
     data   =
   , where  =
   , var    =
   , by     =
   , factor =
   , cnsr   = CNSR
   , covars =
   , class  =
   , strata =
   , ties   = efron
   , stats  = pval="X.XXX"
   , label  =
   , out    =
   , debug  = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: one record per subject, with USUBJID, the time and the censoring variable. (required) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (ittfl = 'Y'). (optional) var= The time: one numeric variable, such as aval. (required) by= The groups of the model, the treatment: one variable. (required) factor= The factor of the subgroups: one variable whose values are its levels (factor = sex). (required) cnsr= The censoring variable: one numeric variable, 0 for an event and a positive value for a censoring (the ADaM CNSR: 1, 2 ... name the reason). A missing or negative value on a record used stops the macro with an ERROR. (optional, default CNSR) covars= The numeric covariates of the model, separated by blanks (covars = base). (optional) class= The other class factors of the model, separated by blanks (class = sitegr1). (optional) strata= The strata of the models, separated by blanks (strata = sitegr1). When not given, the models have no strata. (optional) ties= The method for tied times: efron, breslow, or exact (TIES=DISCRETE of PROC PHREG). discrete is accepted as another name of exact. (optional, default efron) Accepts: efron, breslow, exact, discrete. stats= The statistic with its pattern of the printed number: pval. (optional, default pval="X.XXX") label= The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table. (optional) out= The name of the result data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets interaction_phreg. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the result shape, one row for all groups and levels together: GROUPS (blank), BLOCK, STAT (pval), VALUE and TEXT.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: Use %interaction_glm for a continuous variable, %interaction_logistic for a response, and %interaction_genmod for a count with its exposure. The macro fits two models with PROC PHREG, in the strata of strata=: the groups, the covariates, the class factors and the factor; and the same model with the treatment-by-factor terms. pval is the likelihood-ratio test: the difference of the likelihood-ratio chi-squares of the two fits (twice the difference of the log partial likelihoods), with the difference of their degrees of freedom. The models use one record per subject: a record with a missing time, group or level is not used. CNSR 0 is an event and any positive value is a censoring, as in ADaM, where the value names the reason of the censoring: a CNSR of 2 is censored as 1 is. A record used with a missing or negative CNSR stops the macro with an ERROR.

docs.title: %km
docs.text:
Returns the Kaplan-Meier summary of a time in each group: subjects, events, the median time and its confidence limits.

Procedure: PROC LIFETEST · Family: Time to an event

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%km(
     data     =
   , where    =
   , var      =
   , by       =
   , cnsr     = CNSR
   , time     =
   , conftype = linear
   , level    = 0.95
   , stats    = n="XX" events="XX" median="XX.X" lcl="XX.X" ucl="XX.X"
   , label    =
   , out      =
   , debug    = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: one record per subject, with the time and the censoring variable. (required) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (paramcd = 'TTDE'). (optional) var= The time: one numeric variable, such as aval. (required) by= The groups: one variable. (required) cnsr= The censoring variable: one numeric variable, 0 for an event and a positive value for a censoring (the ADaM CNSR: 1, 2 ... name the reason). A missing or negative value on a record used stops the macro with an ERROR. (optional, default CNSR) time= One time at which to give the survival: a number, such as time = 180. When not given, the result has no survival. (optional) conftype= The transformation of the confidence interval: linear, log or loglog, as CONFTYPE= of PROC LIFETEST (the default of PROC LIFETEST itself is loglog). (optional, default linear) Accepts: linear, log, loglog. level= The confidence level: a number between 0 and 1. (optional, default 0.95) stats= The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with its pattern of the printed number, separated by blanks. The names are n, events, median, lcl, ucl and, with time=, surv. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns. (optional, default n="XX" events="XX" median="XX.X" lcl="XX.X" ucl="XX.X") label= The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table. (optional) out= The name of the result data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets km. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the result shape, one row per group and statistic: the BY variable, GROUPS, BLOCK, STAT, VALUE and TEXT. When no record qualifies, the result has no row and the log has the NOTE "No data qualified".

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use %kmplot to draw the curve, and %table_tte for the whole table of a time to event in one call. The statistics are n (the subjects), events, median, lcl and ucl. The limits of the median are those of Brookmeyer and Crowley, from PROC LIFETEST. A median or a limit that the curve does not reach has a missing VALUE and the TEXT NE (not estimable). Without time=, lcl and ucl are the limits of the median. With time=, surv is the survival at that time in percent, and lcl and ucl are the limits of that survival, in percent, not of the median; the default stats= has no surv, so give stats= with surv to show it. A record with a missing time or a missing group is not used. CNSR 0 is an event and any positive value is a censoring, as in ADaM, where the value names the reason of the censoring: a CNSR of 2 is censored as 1 is. A record used with a missing or negative CNSR stops the macro with an ERROR. In the first example n of Placebo is 85, while the column N of Placebo in %table_tte with adsl= is 86: the 2 subjects with a missing TRTEDT (one Placebo, one Low Dose) have no event and no censoring date, so %tte gives them no record in adttde.

Good to know

The macro does not give the number at risk at given times: %kmplot draws it and keeps it in its out= data set.

docs.title: %kmplot
docs.text:
Draws the Kaplan-Meier curve of each group as PNG and RTF files and returns the numbers drawn.

Procedure: PROC LIFETEST, PROC SUMMARY, PROC SGPANEL · Family: Figures

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%kmplot(
     data     =
   , plot     =
   , par      =
   , columns  =
   , where    =
   , time     =
   , cnsr     = CNSR
   , by       =
   , panel    =
   , atrisk   = yes
   , times    =
   , median   = no
   , conftype = linear
   , level    = 0.95
   , xlabel   =
   , ylabel   = "Survival (%)"
   , ref      =
   , file     =
   , width    = 6.5in
   , height   = 4.5in
   , out      =
   , outpar   =
   , debug    = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: one record per subject, such as a time-to-event data set. (required unless plot= is given) plot= Draw again: the out= of an earlier %kmplot call, changed or not. It is drawn as it is, and no statistic is computed. Give it instead of data=. (optional) par= The drawing parameters of an earlier %kmplot call: its outpar=. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=. (optional) columns= The data set of %columns: it gives the order of the groups and their colours. When not given, the groups come in the order of the data. (optional) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (anl01fl = 'Y'). (optional) time= The time variable: one numeric variable (time = aval). (required unless plot= is given) cnsr= The censoring variable: one numeric variable, 0 for an event and a positive value for a censoring (the ADaM CNSR: 1, 2 ... name the reason). A missing or negative value on a record used stops the macro with an ERROR. (optional, default CNSR) by= The groups: one variable, one curve per group. (required unless par= gives it) panel= A variable: one panel per value (panel = sex). (optional) atrisk= yes: show the number at risk under the axis. (optional, default yes) Accepts: yes, no. times= The ticks of the x axis and the times of the number at risk: numbers separated by blanks (times = 0 30 60 90). When not given, the ticks go from 0 by a round step (1, 2, 2.5 or 5 times a power of 10) to the first tick at or after the longest time. (optional) median= yes: show the median time of each group and its confidence interval as text in the plot. (optional, default no) Accepts: yes, no. conftype= The type of the confidence interval of the median, as CONFTYPE= of PROC LIFETEST: linear, log, loglog, asinsqrt or logit. (optional, default linear) Accepts: linear, log, loglog, asinsqrt, logit. level= The confidence level of the interval of the median: a number between 0 and 1. (optional, default 0.95) xlabel= The label of the x axis: a text in quotes. When not given, the label of time= (or its name). (optional) ylabel= The label of the y axis: a text in quotes. (optional, default "Survival (%)") ref= Reference lines on the y axis: one value or several, separated by blanks (ref = 0 50). (optional) file= The output file without its extension: the macro writes <file>.png (300 dpi) and <file>.rtf. (required unless par= gives it) width= The width of the figure: a length with its unit (width = 9in). (optional, default 6.5in) height= The height of the figure: a length with its unit (height = 6in). (optional, default 4.5in) out= The name of the data set of the numbers drawn. When not given, they are not kept. (optional) outpar= The name of the data set of the drawing parameters, one row each. Give it to par= of a later call to draw the figure again. (optional) debug= yes: keep the work data sets kmplot. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: one row per number drawn, with the variables of panel= and by=, KIND, X, Y, LOWER, UPPER, N and CENSORED. In a row of KIND curve, X is a time (0 and each time with an event or a censoring), Y the survival in percent after it, and CENSORED is 1 when a subject is censored at it. In a row of KIND atrisk, X is a tick and N the number at risk. In a row of KIND median, X is the median and LOWER and UPPER its limits (missing: not reached). The data set of outpar=: one row per drawing parameter, in the order of the table: PARAMETER ($32), its name, and VALUE ($500), its value as drawn (a label in quotes). The files: <file>.png and <file>.rtf.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use %km for the Kaplan-Meier estimates in a table; %kmplot computes its own curve with PROC LIFETEST. The survival is in percent, drawn as steps, with a mark at each censored time. Under the axis is the number at risk at each tick: the subjects whose time is that tick or later. With median=yes, the plot also shows the median time of each group and its confidence interval (NE: not reached). A record with a missing time, group or panel is not used. CNSR 0 is an event and any positive value is a censoring, as in ADaM, where the value names the reason of the censoring: a CNSR of 2 is censored as 1 is. A record used with a missing or negative CNSR stops the macro with an ERROR. To draw the figure again without computing, give plot= the out= and par= the outpar= of an earlier call.

Good to know

Draw again: plot= takes the out= of an earlier %kmplot call, changed or not, and draws it as it is, with no statistic computed. par= takes the outpar= of that call and gives the drawing parameters: columns, by, panel, atrisk, median, level (with plot= only for the heading of the medians), xlabel, ylabel, ref, file, width, height. These change the picture, not the numbers. The other parameters compute; with plot= the log has a NOTE for each one given, as it is not used. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=, and the row wins over the default of the table. With plot=, the ticks are the X of the rows of KIND atrisk.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples run on the example data after examples/setup.sas. The output under each call is the output of that run. They also read adttde (made by the example of %tte), t14_2_1_cols (made by the example of %columns). All examples of the reference run as one program: examples/reference.sas.

Before these examples: the calls that make their inputs

Run examples/setup.sas, then these calls from the examples of %tte, %describe, %anova, %freq, %chisq, %stack, %columns, in this order. Then the examples of this page run as shown.

/* from the example of %tte */
* Makes TTDE. Log NOTE: 2 subject(s) with no event and no censoring date: no record (no TRTEDT).;
%tte(
     subjects      = adsl
   , events        = adae
   , event         = trtemfl = 'Y' AND aebodsys = 'SKIN AND SUBCUTANEOUS TISSUE DISORDERS'
   , date          = astdt
   , start         = trtsdt
   , censor_date   = trtedt
   , seq           = aeseq
   , censor_desc   = "End of treatment"
   , censor_source = "ADSL"
   , event_desc    = aedecod
   , source        = "ADAE"
   , paramcd       = "TTDE"
   , out           = adttde
 )
/* from the example of %describe */
* Summarizes age in each group and in the Total: n, mean, SD, median, minimum and maximum.;
%describe(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_describe
 )
/* from the example of %anova */
* Tests age across the three groups: one row, the p value of the F test.;
%anova(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_anova
 )
/* from the example of %freq */
* Counts each sex in each group and in the Total: n and the percent of the subjects of the group.;
%freq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_freq
 )
/* from the example of %chisq */
* Tests sex across the groups: one row, the p value of the chi square test.;
%chisq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_chisq
 )
/* from the example of %stack */
* Stacks four results in the order of the table: RESULT and ORD tell where each row came from.;
%stack(age_describe age_anova sex_freq sex_chisq, out=t14_2_1)
/* from the example of %columns */
* Makes the four columns with their N from adsl, the Total last, in the order of TRT01AN.;
%columns(
     data  = t14_2_1
   , n     = adsl
   , var   = trt01a
   , order = trt01an
   , total = yes
   , out   = t14_2_1_cols
 )

Draws the curves with the number at risk and the median of each group, and keeps the numbers.

%kmplot(
     data    = adttde
   , columns = t14_2_1_cols
   , time    = aval
   , by      = trt01a
   , median  = yes
   , xlabel  = "Days to the first skin event"
   , file    = &spl_out./figures/f_ttde
   , out     = f_ttde
   , outpar  = f_ttde_par
 )

Draws the figure again from out= and outpar= of the call before: no median, another label.

%kmplot(
     plot   = f_ttde
   , par    = f_ttde_par
   , by     = trt01a
   , median = no
   , ylabel = "Subjects without a skin event (%)"
   , file   = &spl_out./figures/f_ttde_again
 )

Message Fix times=<times> is not a list of numbers give times= the ticks separated by blanks: 0 30 60 90. plot=<plot> has no row of KIND atrisk: its X are the ticks give plot= its rows of KIND atrisk (atrisk=no hides them). cnsr=<cnsr> is missing or negative on <nbad> record(s) used give each record CNSR 0 (an event) or more (a censoring). data= and plot= are both given give data= to compute, or plot= to draw an out= again. plot=<plot> does not exist give plot= an out= of %kmplot (make it first). plot=<plot> has no variable <variable> give plot= the shape of out=: <the variables of out=>. par=<par> does not exist give par= an outpar= of %kmplot (make it first). par=<par> has no variables PARAMETER and VALUE give par= an outpar= of %kmplot. par=<par> has a row of no drawing parameter (with the PARAMETER of the record) give par= rows of outpar= of %kmplot only.

docs.text: data= The stacked results (out= of %stack). (required) columns= The columns (out= of %columns): the place, the header and the N of each column. (required) var= The column variable of the results: the same variable as var= of %columns. (required) page= A group variable of the results, such as page = sex: one page per value, in the order of its numeric twin (SEXN), else of its values. Its values are not rows of the table; each page starts with its first block, and the header of a column on a page has the N of that page. Give %columns the same page=. It goes into the setup. (optional) format= The labels of categories: pairs of a variable and a character format, as in a FORMAT statement (format = sex $sexf. race $racef.). A value that the format decodes shows its label. (optional) label= Column labels for %print: name="text" pairs, separated by blanks. They go into the setup after row=" ". (optional) rows= The rows of a page for %print (rows= of %print): a whole number. It goes into the setup. (optional) file= The output of %print: a path without its extension (file= of %print). It goes into the setup. (optional) nodata= The text that %print prints when there is no row (nodata= of %print): a text without quotes, as in %print, where a quote in it is printed. It goes into the setup. (optional) setup= The name of a global macro variable that keeps the %print call of out=: a SAS name that does not start with SYS or SPL_. When not given, no setup is made. (optional) out= The name of the display data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets layout. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the display data set, one row per printed line: GRP (the rows that stay on one page: a block, or a level of its first group; a row of a value of all groups, such as a p-value in C99 only, has the GRP of the rows of its block before it), ROW (the label of the line, indented, with the format $CHARw.), C1 ... Cn (the cells, labelled with the header of their column) and C99 (All groups: only when a result has a number without the column variable). With page=: also the page variable (with its format of format=) and HEAD_C1 ... HEAD_Cn, the header of each column on its page; C1 ... Cn are then labelled with the column value. The global macro variable: with setup=, the global macro variable of that name.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
%print prints it; %table runs %columns, %ard, %layout and %print in one call. The display data set is the table as the shells show it: each row a printed line, each cell a text. %layout computes nothing: every number is the TEXT of a result. The rows:

  • Each block starts with its label, with a blank row between two blocks.
  • The levels of the groups other than the column variable are indented by two blanks each: a term under its class, a visit under its parameter, vs B under A.
  • The levels are in the order of their numeric twin (AVISITN for AVISIT, PARAMN for PARAMCD: the name with an N added), else of their values. A level of PARAMCD shows its PARAM.
  • A frequency block (only the statistics n, pct, events, lcl and ucl) has one line per category. Any other block has one line per kind of statistic, by the line table below.
  • The p-value of each category (a test of each term, in a block of the same label) stands in the row of its category.
  • A result has at most four groups besides the column variable and the page variable.

The columns:

  • C1 ... Cn: one column per group, with its header and N from %columns.
  • C99, All groups: the numbers of a result without the column variable, such as a p-value of all groups.

The line table: each line by its order and its label, then its template.

  • line 0 (a category of a frequency block): {n} {pct} {events} ({lcl}, {ucl})
  • line 1 (n): {n}
  • line 2 (Events): {events}
  • line 2.5 (Patient-years): {exposure}
  • line 3 (Mean (SD)): {mean} ({sd}) [{se}]. With se and no sd the label is Mean (SE); with both, Mean (SD) [SE].
  • line 4 (Median): {median}
  • line 5 (Q1, Q3): {q1}, {q3}
  • line 6 (Min, Max): {min}, {max}
  • line 7 (LS mean (SE)): {lsmean} ({lsmean_se})
  • line 8 (Difference (SE)): {diff} ({diff_se})
  • line 9 (the estimate, labelled by its STAT): {estimate}. The labels: STAT hr: Hazard ratio; STAT or: Odds ratio; STAT irr: Rate ratio; STAT rd: Risk difference; STAT rr: Relative risk; STAT rate: Rate per 100 patient-years; STAT estimate: Estimate.
  • line 10 (Confidence interval): ({lcl}, {ucl})
  • line 11 (p-value): {pval}
  • line 11.5 (Adjusted p-value): {padj}
  • line 12 (any other STAT, labelled by its name): {value}

In a template:

  • A part that is missing leaves out its piece with its brackets or its comma: a confidence interval without its upper limit prints the lower limit alone.
  • A TEXT that has the brackets of its piece already is not bracketed twice.
  • The counts of a frequency block are right aligned to the widest count.

The setup (setup=):

  • The global macro variable keeps the parameters of %print for out=: data=, by=row, var=c:, together=grp and label=row=" " with the labels of label=; also page=, rows=, file= and nodata= when they are given to %layout. A NOTE in the log shows it.
  • %print(&name.) prints the display data set again after a change. A parameter that is not in the setup is added after it: %print(&name., file=...).
  • A parameter that is in the setup cannot be given again, as SAS stops a call that has a keyword twice: give it to %layout, or write the whole %print call.

When data= has no row, the display data set has no row, and %print prints the text of nodata=.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples run on the example data after examples/setup.sas. The output under each call is the output of that run. They also read t14_2_1 (made by the example of %stack), t14_2_1_cols (made by the example of %columns), t14_1_1 (made by the example of %stack), t14_1_1_cols (made by the example of %columns). All examples of the reference run as one program: examples/reference.sas.

Before these examples: the calls that make their inputs

Run examples/setup.sas, then these calls from the examples of %describe, %anova, %freq, %chisq, %stack, %columns, %ard, in this order. Then the examples of this page run as shown.

/* from the example of %describe */
* Summarizes age in each group and in the Total: n, mean, SD, median, minimum and maximum.;
%describe(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_describe
 )
* Adds sex as a second BY variable: the rows of each group and sex, for a page per sex.;
%describe(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a sex
   , total = yes
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_sex
 )
/* from the example of %anova */
* Tests age across the three groups: one row, the p value of the F test.;
%anova(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_anova
 )
/* from the example of %freq */
* Counts each sex in each group and in the Total: n and the percent of the subjects of the group.;
%freq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_freq
 )
* Adds sex as a second BY variable: the age groups of each group and sex, for a page per sex.;
%freq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = agegr1
   , by    = trt01a sex
   , total = yes
   , label = "Age group"
   , out   = agegr_sex
 )
/* from the example of %chisq */
* Tests sex across the groups: one row, the p value of the chi square test.;
%chisq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_chisq
 )
/* from the example of %stack */
* Stacks four results in the order of the table: RESULT and ORD tell where each row came from.;
%stack(age_describe age_anova sex_freq sex_chisq, out=t14_2_1)
* Stacks age and the age groups by sex: the results of a table with a page per sex.;
%stack(age_sex agegr_sex, out=t14_1_1)
/* from the example of %columns */
* Makes the four columns with their N from adsl, the Total last, in the order of TRT01AN.;
%columns(
     data  = t14_2_1
   , n     = adsl
   , var   = trt01a
   , order = trt01an
   , total = yes
   , out   = t14_2_1_cols
 )
* Gives page=sex: one row per column and sex, the N of each column on the page of its sex.;
%columns(
     data  = t14_1_1
   , n     = adsl
   , var   = trt01a
   , order = trt01an
   , page  = sex
   , total = yes
   , out   = t14_1_1_cols
 )
/* from the example of %ard */
* Writes every number of the table and each column N to one CSV file: the raw value and the text.;
%ard(data=t14_2_1, columns=t14_2_1_cols, file=t14_2_1)

Makes the display data set: one row per printed line, one column per group, sex by its labels.

%layout(
     data    = t14_2_1
   , columns = t14_2_1_cols
   , var     = trt01a
   , format  = sex $sexf.
   , file    = &spl_out./tlf/t14_2_1
   , setup   = t14_2_1_print
   , out     = t14_2_1_display
 )

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
A wrong call writes the message and its fix to the log and stops. The macro also gives the messages every macro shares.

Message Fix format=<format> is not a list of variable and format. write it as in a FORMAT statement: format=sex $sexf. page=<page> is the column variable var=<var> give page= another BY variable, such as sex. columns=<columns> has no page=<page>: its N is not the N of a page give %columns the same page=<page>. setup=<setup> is not a SAS name give setup= a name such as t_sex_print. setup=<setup> is a name of a macro or of SAS give setup= another name, such as t_sex_print. <nopage> row(s) of data=<data> are not by page=<page>. add <page> to by= of its macro, such as by=trt01a <page>. a result of data=<data> has <deep> groups besides var= (4 at most). give each result at most 4 groups besides var=.

The macro also writes these NOTE lines to the log, without stopping:

  • NOTE: [layout] setup=<setup> keeps the print of <out>: <list>
  • NOTE: [layout] print it with %print(&<setup>.)

docs.title: %lineplot
docs.text:
Draws lines through given values, one line per group, as PNG and RTF files and returns the numbers drawn.

Procedure: PROC SGPANEL · Family: Figures

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%lineplot(
     data    =
   , plot    =
   , par     =
   , columns =
   , where   =
   , x       =
   , y       =
   , by      =
   , panel   =
   , lower   =
   , upper   =
   , band    = no
   , xformat =
   , xlabel  =
   , ylabel  =
   , ref     =
   , file    =
   , width   = 6.5in
   , height  = 4.5in
   , out     =
   , outpar  =
   , debug   = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: one row per group and x. (required) plot= Draw again: the out= of an earlier %lineplot call, changed or not. It is drawn as it is, and no statistic is computed. Give it instead of data=. (optional) par= The drawing parameters of an earlier %lineplot call: its outpar=. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=. (optional) columns= The data set of %columns: it gives the order of the groups and their colours. When not given, the groups come in the order of the data. (optional) where= The rows to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (paramcd = 'SYSBP'). (optional) x= The x: one numeric variable (x = avisitn). (required) y= The value: one numeric variable (y = estimate). (required) by= The groups: one variable, one line per group. (required) panel= A variable: one panel per value, one under the other, each with its own y axis (panel = paramcd). (optional) lower= The lower end of the interval: one numeric variable. Give upper= with it. (optional) upper= The upper end of the interval: one numeric variable. Give lower= with it. (optional) band= yes: draw the interval as a band; no: as error bars. (optional, default no) Accepts: yes, no. xformat= The format of the ticks of x, as in a FORMAT statement (xformat = visfmt.). When not given, the format of x. (optional) xlabel= The label of the x axis: a text in quotes. When not given, the label of x= (or its name). (optional) ylabel= The label of the y axis: a text in quotes. When not given, the label of y= (or its name). (optional) ref= Reference lines on the y axis: one value or several, separated by blanks (ref = 0 50). (optional) file= The output file without its extension: the macro writes <file>.png (300 dpi) and <file>.rtf. (required) width= The width of the figure: a length with its unit (width = 9in). (optional, default 6.5in) height= The height of the figure: a length with its unit (height = 6in). (optional, default 4.5in) out= The name of the data set of the numbers drawn. When not given, they are not kept. (optional) outpar= The name of the data set of the drawing parameters, one row each. Give it to par= of a later call to draw the figure again. (optional) debug= yes: keep the work data sets lineplot. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: one row per panel, group and x: the variables of panel= and by=, KIND (line), X, Y, LOWER and UPPER. The data set of outpar=: one row per drawing parameter, in the order of the table: PARAMETER ($32), its name, and VALUE ($500), its value as drawn (a label in quotes). The files: <file>.png and <file>.rtf.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
It computes nothing: use it for values computed before (the LS means of %lsmeans or %mmrm by visit, a rate by month), and %meanplot to compute the mean of the records. The interval of lower= and upper= is drawn as error bars, with the groups a little apart on the x axis, or as a band. A row with a missing x, group or panel is not used. To draw the figure again without computing, give plot= the out= and par= the outpar= of an earlier call.

Good to know

Draw again: plot= takes the out= of an earlier %lineplot call, changed or not, and draws it as it is, with no statistic computed (an interval where LOWER has a value). par= takes the outpar= of that call and gives the drawing parameters: columns, by, panel, band, xformat, xlabel, ylabel, ref, file, width, height. These change the picture, not the numbers. The other parameters choose the values; with plot= the log has a NOTE for each one given, as it is not used. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=, and the row wins over the default of the table.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples run on the example data after examples/setup.sas. The output under each call is the output of that run. They also read f_bp_mean (made by the example of %meanplot), t14_2_1_cols (made by the example of %columns). All examples of the reference run as one program: examples/reference.sas.

Before these examples: the calls that make their inputs

Run examples/setup.sas, then these calls from the examples of %describe, %anova, %freq, %chisq, %stack, %columns, %meanplot, in this order. Then the examples of this page run as shown.

/* from the example of %describe */
* Summarizes age in each group and in the Total: n, mean, SD, median, minimum and maximum.;
%describe(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_describe
 )
/* from the example of %anova */
* Tests age across the three groups: one row, the p value of the F test.;
%anova(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_anova
 )
/* from the example of %freq */
* Counts each sex in each group and in the Total: n and the percent of the subjects of the group.;
%freq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_freq
 )
/* from the example of %chisq */
* Tests sex across the groups: one row, the p value of the chi square test.;
%chisq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_chisq
 )
/* from the example of %stack */
* Stacks four results in the order of the table: RESULT and ORD tell where each row came from.;
%stack(age_describe age_anova sex_freq sex_chisq, out=t14_2_1)
/* from the example of %columns */
* Makes the four columns with their N from adsl, the Total last, in the order of TRT01AN.;
%columns(
     data  = t14_2_1
   , n     = adsl
   , var   = trt01a
   , order = trt01an
   , total = yes
   , out   = t14_2_1_cols
 )
/* from the example of %meanplot */
* Draws the mean change and its SE at each visit, a panel per parameter, with the n of each point.;
%meanplot(
     data    = advs
   , columns = t14_2_1_cols
   , where   = (paramcd IN ('SYSBP' 'DIABP') AND anl01fl = 'Y' AND avisitn < 99)
   , y       = chg
   , x       = avisitn
   , by      = trt01a
   , panel   = param
   , ntable  = yes
   , xformat = VISIT.
   , ref     = 0
   , file    = &spl_out./figures/f_bp_mean
   , out     = f_bp_mean
 )

Draws the means that meanplot kept as lines, with a band between the limits.

%lineplot(
     data    = f_bp_mean
   , columns = t14_2_1_cols
   , x       = x
   , y       = y
   , by      = trt01a
   , panel   = param
   , lower   = lower
   , upper   = upper
   , band    = yes
   , xformat = VISIT.
   , ylabel  = "Mean change from baseline (SE)"
   , ref     = 0
   , file    = &spl_out./figures/f_bp_line
   , out     = f_bp_line
 )

Message Fix lower= and upper= come together give both ends of the interval, or neither. x=<x> is a character variable give x= a numeric variable (AVISITN), xformat= labels. data= and plot= are both given give data= to compute, or plot= to draw an out= again. plot=<plot> does not exist give plot= an out= of %lineplot (make it first). plot=<plot> has no variable <variable> give plot= the shape of out=: <the variables of out=>. par=<par> does not exist give par= an outpar= of %lineplot (make it first). par=<par> has no variables PARAMETER and VALUE give par= an outpar= of %lineplot. par=<par> has a row of no drawing parameter (with the PARAMETER of the record) give par= rows of outpar= of %lineplot only.

docs.title: %locf
docs.text:
Adds last-observation-carried-forward records (DTYPE = 'LOCF') to the analysis windows in which a group has no analysed record.

Procedure: PROC SORT, a DATA step (SET POINT=) · Family: ADaM steps

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%locf(
     data    =
   , windows =
   , where   =
   , by      = USUBJID PARAMCD
   , flag    = ANL01FL
   , day     = ADY
   , length  = $8
   , debug   = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The data set to change in place, such as advs: the new records are added to it. (required) windows= The windows, in the form of windows= of %windows: baseline first, then one window or more after it. (required) where= The records to carry forward: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (paramcd = 'SYSBP'). When not given, all analysed records count. (optional) by= The groups, each carried forward by itself: variables separated by blanks. (optional, default USUBJID PARAMCD) flag= The flag of the analysed records: a character variable that is 'Y' on them. (optional, default ANL01FL) day= The numeric variable of the study day: it gives AWTDIFF of a new record. (optional, default ADY) length= The length of DTYPE, such as $8. (optional, default $8) debug= yes: keep the work data sets locf. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data sets: data=, changed in place: the new records are added, and all records are sorted by the groups, AVISITN and DTYPE.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use %windows first: it gives each record the AVISITN of its window. The rule:

  • An analysed record has flag= equal to 'Y' and a window after baseline.
  • For each window, from the second window after baseline on, that has no analysed record of the group, the macro copies the last analysed record before it and moves the copy to that window.
  • Baseline is not carried forward, and the first window after baseline is not filled.

The new records get the window variables of their window and DTYPE = 'LOCF'; the other records get a blank DTYPE.

docs.text:
The examples run on the example data after examples/setup.sas. The output under each call is the output of that run. All examples of the reference run as one program: examples/reference.sas.

Copies the systolic records of the analysis visits.

DATA vs;
  SET advs;
  WHERE paramcd = 'SYSBP' AND avisitn IN (0 4 12 24);
RUN;

Carries the last value forward into a visit without a value: DTYPE is LOCF on the new records.

%locf(
     data    = vs
   , windows = 0  "Baseline" .   1   1   "<=1"
             # 4  "Week 4"   2   42  28  "2-42"
             # 12 "Week 12"  43  126 84  "43-126"
             # 24 "Week 24"  127 210 168 "127-210"
   , where   = (paramcd = 'SYSBP')
   , length  = $7
 )

docs.title: %logistic
docs.text:
Returns the odds ratios of pairs of groups from a logistic regression, with their Wald confidence limits and p-values.

Procedure: PROC LOGISTIC (LSMEANS) · Family: Compare groups with a model

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%logistic(
     data   =
   , where  =
   , var    =
   , event  = "Y"
   , by     =
   , within =
   , covars =
   , class  =
   , pairs  = all
   , order  =
   , level  = 0.95
   , stats  = or="XX.XX" lcl="XX.XX" ucl="XX.XX" pval="X.XXX"
   , label  =
   , out    =
   , debug  = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set, with USUBJID. (required) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (paramcd = 'RESP'). (optional) var= The response: one variable with two values, numeric or character. (required) event= The value of var= that is the event, in quotes; for a number also in quotes (event = "1"). PROC LOGISTIC alone models the first value in sort order. (optional, default "Y") by= The groups of the model: one character variable. (required) within= One model in each group of these variables, separated by blanks, such as the levels of a subgroup (within = sex). (optional) covars= The covariates: numeric variables separated by blanks (covars = age). (optional) class= The class factors besides the groups: variables separated by blanks (class = sex). (optional) pairs= The pairs of groups to compare. all: each later group against each earlier one, in the order of order= (or of the values). Or the pairs separated by #, each the group first and then the group it is compared with, a value with a blank or a hyphen in quotes: pairs = "Drug" "Placebo" # "High" "Low". (optional, default all) order= The order of the groups: one numeric variable with one value per group (order = trt01pn). (optional) level= The confidence level of the limits: a number between 0 and 1. (optional, default 0.95) stats= The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with the pattern of its printed number, separated by blanks. The names are or, lcl, ucl and pval. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns. (optional, default or="XX.XX" lcl="XX.XX" ucl="XX.XX" pval="X.XXX") label= The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table. (optional) out= The name of the result data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets logistic. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the result shape, one row per pair and statistic: the group in the by= variable, the group it is compared with in VERSUS, and the variables of within=. or is the odds of the event of event= in the group over the odds in VERSUS, adjusted for the covariates and the class factors (an odds ratio above 1: the event is more likely in the group), lcl and ucl its Wald confidence limits, pval its p-value. With pairs=all the group is the later one in the order of order=. GROUPS is the by= variable, VERSUS and the within= variables.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use %risk for a risk difference, relative risk or odds ratio from the 2 x 2 table of a pair, without a model. The model is PROC LOGISTIC of a response with two values: the probability of the event of event= on the groups, the class factors and the covariates, one record per subject (the first with a response). All pairs come from one fit.

Good to know

The iterations go on until no parameter changes by more than 1E-10 (XCONV=). PROC LOGISTIC alone stops at a relative gradient of 1E-8. So the estimate is the maximum to the digits R gives: the odds ratio 7 of a 2 x 2 table is 7, where GCONV=1E-10 gave 6.9999907.

docs.title: %logrank
docs.text:
Returns the p-value of the log-rank test that compares the time to an event between the groups.

Procedure: PROC LIFETEST (STRATA) · Family: Time to an event

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%logrank(
     data   =
   , where  =
   , var    =
   , by     =
   , cnsr   = CNSR
   , strata =
   , stats  = pval="X.XXX"
   , label  =
   , out    =
   , debug  = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: one record per subject, with USUBJID, the time and the censoring variable. (required) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (paramcd = 'TTDE'). (optional) var= The time: one numeric variable, such as aval. (required) by= The groups to compare: one variable. (required) cnsr= The censoring variable: one numeric variable, 0 for an event and a positive value for a censoring (the ADaM CNSR: 1, 2 ... name the reason). A missing or negative value on a record used stops the macro with an ERROR. (optional, default CNSR) strata= The strata of a stratified test: one variable or several, separated by blanks (strata = sitegr1). When not given, the test is not stratified. (optional) stats= The statistic with its pattern of the printed number: pval. (optional, default pval="X.XXX") label= The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table. (optional) out= The name of the result data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets logrank. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the result shape, one row for all groups together: GROUPS (blank), BLOCK, STAT (pval), VALUE and TEXT.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: Use %km for the medians of the groups, and %cox for a hazard ratio with its confidence interval. The test uses one record per subject: when a subject has several records, the first one in the order of USUBJID is used, so where= must select one parameter. With strata=, the test is the stratified log-rank test: each combination of the values of the strata variables is one stratum (STRATA strata / GROUP=by of PROC LIFETEST). With only one group there is no test, and the p-value is missing. CNSR 0 is an event and any positive value is a censoring, as in ADaM, where the value names the reason of the censoring: a CNSR of 2 is censored as 1 is. A record used with a missing or negative CNSR stops the macro with an ERROR.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples run on the example data after examples/setup.sas. The output under each call is the output of that run. They also read adttde (made by the example of %tte). All examples of the reference run as one program: examples/reference.sas.

Before these examples: the calls that make their inputs

Run examples/setup.sas, then these calls from the examples of %tte, in this order. Then the examples of this page run as shown.

/* from the example of %tte */
* Makes TTDE. Log NOTE: 2 subject(s) with no event and no censoring date: no record (no TRTEDT).;
%tte(
     subjects      = adsl
   , events        = adae
   , event         = trtemfl = 'Y' AND aebodsys = 'SKIN AND SUBCUTANEOUS TISSUE DISORDERS'
   , date          = astdt
   , start         = trtsdt
   , censor_date   = trtedt
   , seq           = aeseq
   , censor_desc   = "End of treatment"
   , censor_source = "ADSL"
   , event_desc    = aedecod
   , source        = "ADAE"
   , paramcd       = "TTDE"
   , out           = adttde
 )

Tests the curves of the groups with the log rank test, stratified by sex: one p value.

%logrank(
     data   = adttde
   , var    = aval

   , strata = sex

docs.title: %lsmeans
docs.text:
The ANCOVA of the groups: returns the differences of the LS means of pairs of groups in a linear model, with confidence limits and p-values.

Procedure: PROC MIXED (LSMEANS) · Family: Compare groups with a model

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%lsmeans(
     data   =
   , where  =
   , var    =
   , by     =
   , within =
   , covars =
   , class  =
   , pairs  = all
   , order  =
   , level  = 0.95
   , stats  = diff="XX.X" diff_se="XX.XX" lcl="XX.X" ucl="XX.X" pval="X.XXX"
   , label  =
   , out    =
   , debug  = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set, with USUBJID. (required) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (paramcd = 'SYSBP' AND avisit = 'Week 12'). (optional) var= The response: one numeric variable. (required) by= The groups of the model: one character variable. (required) within= One model in each group of these variables, separated by blanks (within = paramcd). (optional) covars= The covariates: numeric variables separated by blanks (covars = base). (optional) class= The class factors besides the groups: variables separated by blanks (class = sex). (optional) pairs= The pairs of groups to compare. all: each later group against each earlier one, in the order of order= (or of the values). Or the pairs separated by #, each the group first and then the group it is compared with, a value with a blank or a hyphen in quotes: pairs = "Drug" "Placebo" # "High" "Low". (optional, default all) order= The order of the groups: one numeric variable with one value per group (order = trt01pn). (optional) level= The confidence level of the limits: a number between 0 and 1. (optional, default 0.95) stats= The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with the pattern of its printed number, separated by blanks. The names are diff, diff_se, lcl, ucl, pval, lsmean, lsmean_se, lsmean_lcl and lsmean_ucl. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns. (optional, default diff="XX.X" diff_se="XX.XX" lcl="XX.X" ucl="XX.X" pval="X.XXX") label= The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table. (optional) out= The name of the result data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets lsmeans. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the result shape. A row of a difference has the group in the by= variable and the group it is compared with in VERSUS: diff is the LS mean of the group minus the LS mean of VERSUS (a negative diff: a smaller LS mean in the group), diff_se its standard error, lcl and ucl its confidence limits, pval the p-value of the test that it is 0. With pairs=all the group is the later one in the order of order=. A row of an LS mean has VERSUS blank. GROUPS is the by= variable, VERSUS and the within= variables.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: Use %ancova for the test of one numeric term (a dose response), and %mmrm for repeated visits of a subject. The model is PROC MIXED without a random effect (least squares): the covariates, the class factors and the groups, one record per subject (the first with a value; when where= leaves a second record of a subject, the log has a NOTE with their number). Give a where= that leaves one record per subject, such as one parameter at one visit with anl01fl = 'Y'; otherwise each subject has the first of its records in the order of data=, whichever it is. The LS mean of each group comes when stats= asks for it.

docs.title: %meanplot
docs.text:
Draws the mean or median of each group by visit as PNG and RTF files and returns the numbers drawn.

Procedure: PROC MEANS, PROC SGPANEL · Family: Figures

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%meanplot(
     data    =
   , plot    =
   , par     =
   , columns =
   , where   =
   , y       =
   , x       =
   , by      =
   , panel   =
   , stat    = mean
   , error   = se
   , level   = 0.95
   , connect = yes
   , ntable  = no
   , xformat =
   , xlabel  =
   , ylabel  =
   , ref     =
   , file    =
   , width   = 6.5in
   , height  = 4.5in
   , out     =
   , outpar  =
   , debug   = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: one record per subject and visit. (required) plot= Draw again: the out= of an earlier %meanplot call, changed or not. It is drawn as it is, and no statistic is computed. Give it instead of data=. (optional) par= The drawing parameters of an earlier %meanplot call: its outpar=. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=. (optional) columns= The data set of %columns: it gives the order of the groups and their colours. When not given, the groups come in the order of the data. (optional) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (anl01fl = 'Y'). (optional) y= The variable to summarize: one numeric variable (y = aval). (required) x= The visit: one numeric variable (x = avisitn). Its values are the ticks, printed with xformat=. (required) by= The groups: one variable, one line per group. (required) panel= A variable: one panel per value, one under the other, each with its own y axis (panel = paramcd). (optional) stat= The statistic: mean or median. (optional, default mean) Accepts: mean, median. error= The error bars: se, sd or ci for the mean; iqr (Q1 and Q3) for the median; or none. (optional, default se) Accepts: se, sd, ci, iqr, none. level= The confidence level of error=ci: a number between 0 and 1. (optional, default 0.95) connect= yes: join the points of a group by a line. (optional, default yes) Accepts: yes, no. ntable= yes: show the n of each visit and group under the axis. (optional, default no) Accepts: yes, no. xformat= The format of the ticks of x, as in a FORMAT statement (xformat = visfmt.). When not given, the format of x. (optional) xlabel= The label of the x axis: a text in quotes. When not given, the label of x= (or its name). (optional) ylabel= The label of the y axis: a text in quotes. When not given, the statistic, the error bars and the label of y=. (optional) ref= Reference lines on the y axis: one value or several, separated by blanks (ref = 0 50). (optional) file= The output file without its extension: the macro writes <file>.png (300 dpi) and <file>.rtf. (required) width= The width of the figure: a length with its unit (width = 9in). (optional, default 6.5in) height= The height of the figure: a length with its unit (height = 6in). (optional, default 4.5in) out= The name of the data set of the numbers drawn. When not given, they are not kept. (optional) outpar= The name of the data set of the drawing parameters, one row each. Give it to par= of a later call to draw the figure again. (optional) debug= yes: keep the work data sets meanplot. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: one row per panel, group and visit: the variables of panel= and by=, KIND (mean or median), X (the visit), Y (the statistic), LOWER and UPPER (the ends of the error bar; missing for se, sd and ci when there is one value) and N. The data set of outpar=: one row per drawing parameter, in the order of the table: PARAMETER ($32), its name, and VALUE ($500), its value as drawn (a label in quotes). The files: <file>.png and <file>.rtf.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
It computes the statistic from the records; use %lineplot for values computed before (the LS means of %mmrm by visit) and %profileplot for the line of each subject. The error bars are the SE, the SD or the confidence interval of the mean, or Q1 and Q3 of the median. The points of a group are joined by a line, and the groups stand a little apart on the x axis so that their bars do not overlap. With ntable=yes, the n of each visit and group is shown under the axis. The quantiles are those of PROC MEANS with QNTLDEF=5 (R quantile type 2). A record with a missing value, visit, group or panel is not used. To draw the figure again without computing, give plot= the out= and par= the outpar= of an earlier call.

Good to know

Draw again: plot= takes the out= of an earlier %meanplot call, changed or not, and draws it as it is, with no statistic computed (error bars where LOWER has a value). par= takes the outpar= of that call and gives the drawing parameters: columns, by, panel, connect, ntable, xformat, xlabel, ylabel, ref, file, width, height. These change the picture, not the numbers. The other parameters compute; with plot= the log has a NOTE for each one given, as it is not used. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=, and the row wins over the default of the table.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples run on the example data after examples/setup.sas. The output under each call is the output of that run. They also read t14_2_1_cols (made by the example of %columns). All examples of the reference run as one program: examples/reference.sas.

Before these examples: the calls that make their inputs

Run examples/setup.sas, then these calls from the examples of %describe, %anova, %freq, %chisq, %stack, %columns, in this order. Then the examples of this page run as shown.

/* from the example of %describe */
* Summarizes age in each group and in the Total: n, mean, SD, median, minimum and maximum.;
%describe(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_describe
 )
/* from the example of %anova */
* Tests age across the three groups: one row, the p value of the F test.;
%anova(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_anova
 )
/* from the example of %freq */
* Counts each sex in each group and in the Total: n and the percent of the subjects of the group.;
%freq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_freq
 )
/* from the example of %chisq */
* Tests sex across the groups: one row, the p value of the chi square test.;
%chisq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_chisq
 )
/* from the example of %stack */
* Stacks four results in the order of the table: RESULT and ORD tell where each row came from.;
%stack(age_describe age_anova sex_freq sex_chisq, out=t14_2_1)
/* from the example of %columns */
* Makes the four columns with their N from adsl, the Total last, in the order of TRT01AN.;
%columns(
     data  = t14_2_1
   , n     = adsl
   , var   = trt01a
   , order = trt01an
   , total = yes
   , out   = t14_2_1_cols
 )

Draws the mean change and its SE at each visit, a panel per parameter, with the n of each point.

%meanplot(
     data    = advs
   , columns = t14_2_1_cols
   , where   = (paramcd IN ('SYSBP' 'DIABP') AND anl01fl = 'Y' AND avisitn < 99)
   , y       = chg
   , x       = avisitn
   , by      = trt01a
   , panel   = param
   , ntable  = yes
   , xformat = VISIT.
   , ref     = 0
   , file    = &spl_out./figures/f_bp_mean
   , out     = f_bp_mean
 )

docs.title: %mmrm
docs.text:
Returns the differences of the LS means of pairs of groups at one visit from a repeated measures mixed model.

Procedure: PROC MIXED (REPEATED, LSMEANS) · Family: Compare groups with a model

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%mmrm(
     data     =
   , where    =
   , var      =
   , by       =
   , visit    =
   , at       =
   , class    =
   , subject  = USUBJID
   , model    =
   , type     = un
   , fallback =
   , ddfm     = bw
   , method   = reml
   , pairs    = all
   , order    =
   , level    = 0.95
   , stats    = diff="XX.X" diff_se="XX.XX" lcl="XX.X" ucl="XX.X" pval="X.XXX"
   , label    =
   , out      =
   , debug    = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: one record per subject and visit. (required) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (paramcd = 'SYSBP' AND anl01fl = 'Y'). (optional) var= The response: one numeric variable. (required) by= The groups: one character variable. (required) visit= The visit: one variable, the repeated factor of the REPEATED statement. The macro adds it to the class factors. (required) at= The visit of the LS means and their differences: a value of visit= in quotes (at = "Week 24"). (required) class= The class factors besides the groups and the subject: variables separated by blanks. (optional) subject= The subject: one variable. (optional, default USUBJID) model= The fixed effects: the MODEL statement after the equal sign. It must have the term of the groups by visit: model = base trt01p avisit trt01p*avisit. (required) type= The covariance structure: TYPE= of REPEATED (un, cs, ar(1), toep ...). (optional, default un) fallback= Other covariance structures to try in their order when one does not converge, separated by blanks (fallback = toep cs). (optional) ddfm= The degrees of freedom: DDFM= of MODEL (bw is between-within, kr is Kenward-Roger). (optional, default bw) method= The estimation method: reml or ml. (optional, default reml) pairs= The pairs of groups to compare. all: each later group against each earlier one, in the order of order= (or of the values). Or the pairs separated by #, each the group first and then the group it is compared with, a value with a blank or a hyphen in quotes: pairs = "Drug" "Placebo" # "High" "Low". (optional, default all) order= The order of the groups: one numeric variable with one value per group (order = trt01pn). (optional) level= The confidence level of the limits: a number between 0 and 1. (optional, default 0.95) stats= The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with the pattern of its printed number, separated by blanks. The names are diff, diff_se, lcl, ucl, pval, lsmean and lsmean_se. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns. (optional, default diff="XX.X" diff_se="XX.XX" lcl="XX.X" ucl="XX.X" pval="X.XXX") label= The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table. (optional) out= The name of the result data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets mmrm. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the result shape, as in %lsmeans. A row of a difference has the group in the by= variable and the group it is compared with in VERSUS: diff is the LS mean of the group at the visit of at= minus the LS mean of VERSUS at that visit (a negative diff: a smaller LS mean in the group), diff_se its standard error, lcl and ucl its confidence limits, pval the p-value of the test that it is 0. With pairs=all the group is the later one in the order of order=. A row of an LS mean has VERSUS blank. GROUPS is the by= variable and VERSUS. When no structure converges, the macro stops with an ERROR and writes no result.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use %lsmeans for one record per subject, and %ancova for the test of one numeric term. The model is PROC MIXED with a REPEATED statement: one record per subject and visit (the first with a value). When the covariance structure of type= does not converge, the macro tries the structures of fallback= in their order. The log names the structure used, in a NOTE such as "[mmrm] The covariance structure TYPE=un converged." (a structure that did not converge has its own NOTE, and the WARNING lines of PROC MIXED of that fit are not used). The macro adds visit= to the class factors: class= needs only the others. The LS mean of each group at the visit comes when stats= asks for it.

Good to know

The model is fitted by iteration: another program gives the same numbers to about five digits, not to the last one. A structure may converge in one program and not in the other. On visits that are very closely correlated, PROC MIXED stops AR(1) with an infinite likelihood where the R twin of this macro (mmrm() of the R package sapling, a separate product) converges, so the same call may use the next structure of fallback= in SAS. The NOTE "[mmrm] The covariance structure TYPE=... converged" names the structure used. The WARNING lines of a fit that did not converge are followed by a NOTE that says so.

docs.title: %param_wide
docs.text:
Returns the values of several parameters side by side: one record per group, with the variables of each parameter.

Procedure: PROC SORT, MERGE · Family: ADaM steps

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%param_wide(
     data   =
   , where  =
   , params =
   , vars   =
   , by     =
   , out    =
   , debug  = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set, with PARAMCD and the BY variables, such as advs. (required) where= The records to read: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (anl01fl = 'Y'). (optional) params= The parameter codes, separated by blanks (params = sysbp diabp). They are compared with PARAMCD in upper case. (required) vars= The variables to keep of each parameter, separated by blanks (vars = aval chg). (required) by= The groups: variables separated by blanks, such as the subject and the visit (by = usubjid avisitn). (required) out= The name of the data set it writes. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets param_wide. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: one record per group that has a record of every parameter: the BY variables, then <PARAMCD>_<VAR> for each parameter and each variable of vars=.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: The variables of each parameter are named <PARAMCD>_<VAR>, such as SYSBP_AVAL. Only a group that has a record of every parameter of params= gets a record. docs.title: %pick
docs.text:
Gives each subject the value of its first or last record in another data set, as a new variable.

Procedure: PROC SORT, MERGE · Family: ADaM steps

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%pick(
     data   =
   , from   =
   , value  =
   , order  =
   , which  = first
   , length =
   , format =
   , unique = no
   , new    =
   , debug  = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The data set to change in place, such as adsl. (required) from= The data set of the records, with USUBJID. When the value or a sort key is not a variable yet (a date from a text, a difference), make it first in a DATA step. (required) value= The variable of from= that gives the value. (required) order= The sort keys within a subject: variables separated by blanks; write descending before a key as in a BY statement (order = descending astdt). When not given, the records keep the order they have in from=. (optional) which= first or last: the record of the subject that gives the value. (optional, default first) Accepts: first, last. length= The length of the new variable when it is a text, such as $40. (optional) format= The format of the new variable, such as date9. (optional) unique= yes: each subject must have at most one record in from=, so that no order is needed. Two records of a subject give an ERROR line that names the subject. (optional, default no) new= The name of the new variable. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets pick. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data sets: data=, changed in place: the variable new= on every row of a subject, with the value of its first (or last) record in from=. A subject with no record gets a missing value. With unique=yes, a subject with two records gets an ERROR line that names it.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: Use %merge_subject when the other data set has one row per subject. Use %flag_first to flag a record instead of copying a value. The records of a subject are sorted by order=, and which= takes the first or the last one. A missing sort key sorts last. The rows of data= keep their order. A subject with no record in from= gets a missing value. When data= has the variable new= already, the new values replace it and the log says so.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples run on the example data after examples/setup.sas. The output under each call is the output of that run. All examples of the reference run as one program: examples/reference.sas.

Copies the subjects with USUBJID and TRTSDT only.

DATA sl;
  SET adsl;
  KEEP usubjid trtsdt;
RUN;

Takes the date of the first exposure record of each subject, as a text of 10.

%pick(
     data   = sl
   , from   = sdtm.ex
   , value  = exstdtc
   , order  = exstdtc exseq
   , which  = first
   , length = $10
   , new    = exfstdtc
 )

Takes the dose of the last exposure record of each subject.

%pick(
     data  = sl
   , from  = sdtm.ex
   , value = exdose
   , order = exstdtc exseq
   , which = last
   , new   = exldose
 )

Keeps the disposition event of each subject: one record per subject.

DATA ds_eos;
  SET sdtm.ds;
  WHERE dscat = 'DISPOSITION EVENT';
RUN;

Takes the disposition term: unique=yes checks one record per subject, so no order is needed.

%pick(
     data   = sl
   , from   = work.ds_eos
   , value  = dsdecod
   , unique = yes
   , new    = dcdecod
 )

docs.title: %pool
docs.text:
Pools small groups, such as sites, into one group: a new variable that is the group, or the pooled value.

Procedure: PROC FREQ, PROC SUMMARY, MERGE · Family: ADaM steps

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%pool(
     data   =
   , var    =
   , by     =
   , min    =
   , length =
   , new    =
   , into   =
   , debug  = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The data set to change in place, one record per subject, such as adsl. (required) var= The variable of the groups to pool, such as siteid. (required) by= The variable whose every group must have min= records in a group of var=, such as the treatment. (required) min= The smallest number of records: a whole number. (required) length= The length of the new variable, such as $3. (optional) new= The name of the new variable: the value of var=, or into= for a small group. (required) into= The value of the pooled group, without quotes. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets pool. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data sets: data=, changed in place: the variable new=, with the value of var=, or the value of into= for a small group.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: A group of var= goes into the pooled group when it has fewer than min= records in one of the groups of by=, such as a treatment. The macro counts records: in a data set with one record per subject, such as adsl, these are the subjects. A group that has no record in a group of by= counts 0 there and is pooled. The rows of data= keep their order.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples run on the example data after examples/setup.sas. The output under each call is the output of that run. All examples of the reference run as one program: examples/reference.sas.

RUN;

%pool(
     data   = sl
   , var    = siteid
   , by     = trt01p
   , min    = 3
   , length = $3
   , new    = sitegr1
   , into   = 900
 )
