docs.title: %print
docs.text:
Prints a table or a listing with one PROC REPORT into an RTF file and a monospace listing file.

Procedure: PROC REPORT · Family: Build a table

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%print(
     data     =
   , by       =
   , var      =
   , page     =
   , together =
   , label    =
   , rows     = 40
   , file     =
   , nodata   = No data qualified
   , debug    = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The rows to print: the display data set of %layout, or the records of a listing. (required) by= The left columns, printed first: variables separated by blanks. A repeated value is shown once. (optional) var= The other columns, in the order of the print: variables separated by blanks. A list such as c: or c1-c5 is allowed. (required) page= A variable: each value starts a new page, and #BYVAL1 in a title prints the value. A variable HEAD_X gives the header of the column X on the page of its row. (optional) together= A variable: the rows of one value stay on one page, such as together = grp of %layout. (optional) label= Column labels: name="text" pairs, separated by blanks, such as %STR(row=" "). A | splits a header into lines. When not given, the labels of the variables are used. (optional) rows= The rows of a page for together=: a positive whole number. (optional, default 40) file= The output: a path without its extension. The macro writes <file>.rtf and <file>.lst. (required) nodata= The text printed when there is no row: a text without quotes, as the default (a quote in it is printed). (optional, default No data qualified) debug= yes: keep the work data sets print. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The files: <file>.rtf (style journal, landscape) and <file>.lst (the LISTING destination), under the titles and footnotes of the program. With page=: the pages of each value, in the order of the rows.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
It prints a table from its display data set (%layout), and a listing from its records; %table runs %columns, %ard, %layout and %print in one call.

  • The BY columns come first, and a repeated value is shown once. The VAR columns follow: numbers right aligned, text left aligned as written (its leading blanks kept).
  • A text column of var= wider than 40 characters wraps at a width of 40.
  • The header of a column is its pair of label=, else its HEAD_X variable on the page (with page=), else the label of the variable. A | in a header splits it into lines.
  • ODS wraps and pages the RTF. The rows of one value of together= stay on one page of the listing when they fit in rows=; a group that does not fit in what is left of a page starts a new page.
  • A table that is too wide for a page goes on in a second part, and the last BY column is repeated there.
  • With page=, each value of the page variable gets its own pages, in the same two files, under a BY statement, so that a title can name the value (OPTIONS NOBYLINE and TITLE2 "Sex: #BYVAL1").
  • With no row, the report has one row: the text of nodata=.

The setup of %layout (setup=) holds the parameters of a table: %print(&name.) prints its display data set again after a change. A parameter that is not in the setup is added after it: %print(&name., file=...). SAS stops a call that has a parameter twice: change that parameter in %layout.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples run on the example data after examples/setup.sas. The output under each call is the output of that run. They also read t14_2_1_display (made by the example of %layout), t14_1_1_display (made by the example of %layout). All examples of the reference run as one program: examples/reference.sas.

Before these examples: the calls that make their inputs

Run examples/setup.sas, then these calls from the examples of %describe, %anova, %freq, %chisq, %stack, %columns, %ard, %layout, in this order. Then the examples of this page run as shown.

/* from the example of %describe */
* Summarizes age in each group and in the Total: n, mean, SD, median, minimum and maximum.;
%describe(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_describe
 )
* Adds sex as a second BY variable: the rows of each group and sex, for a page per sex.;
%describe(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a sex
   , total = yes
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_sex
 )
/* from the example of %anova */
* Tests age across the three groups: one row, the p value of the F test.;
%anova(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_anova
 )
/* from the example of %freq */
* Counts each sex in each group and in the Total: n and the percent of the subjects of the group.;
%freq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_freq
 )
* Adds sex as a second BY variable: the age groups of each group and sex, for a page per sex.;
%freq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = agegr1
   , by    = trt01a sex
   , total = yes
   , label = "Age group"
   , out   = agegr_sex
 )
/* from the example of %chisq */
* Tests sex across the groups: one row, the p value of the chi square test.;
%chisq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_chisq
 )
/* from the example of %stack */
* Stacks four results in the order of the table: RESULT and ORD tell where each row came from.;
%stack(age_describe age_anova sex_freq sex_chisq, out=t14_2_1)
* Stacks age and the age groups by sex: the results of a table with a page per sex.;
%stack(age_sex agegr_sex, out=t14_1_1)
/* from the example of %columns */
* Makes the four columns with their N from adsl, the Total last, in the order of TRT01AN.;
%columns(
     data  = t14_2_1
   , n     = adsl
   , var   = trt01a
   , order = trt01an
   , total = yes
   , out   = t14_2_1_cols
 )
* Gives page=sex: one row per column and sex, the N of each column on the page of its sex.;
%columns(
     data  = t14_1_1
   , n     = adsl
   , var   = trt01a
   , order = trt01an
   , page  = sex
   , total = yes
   , out   = t14_1_1_cols
 )
/* from the example of %ard */
* Writes every number of the table and each column N to one CSV file: the raw value and the text.;
%ard(data=t14_2_1, columns=t14_2_1_cols, file=t14_2_1)
/* from the example of %layout */
* Makes the display data set: one row per printed line, one column per group, sex by its labels.;
%layout(
     data    = t14_2_1
   , columns = t14_2_1_cols
   , var     = trt01a
   , format  = sex $sexf.
   , file    = &spl_out./tlf/t14_2_1
   , setup   = t14_2_1_print
   , out     = t14_2_1_display
 )
* Makes one page per sex: SEX and HEAD_C1 to HEAD_C4 hold the page and the N of each column on it.;
%layout(
     data    = t14_1_1
   , columns = t14_1_1_cols
   , var     = trt01a
   , page    = sex
   , format  = sex $sexf.
   , file    = &spl_out./tlf/t14_1_1
   , setup   = t14_1_1_print
   , out     = t14_1_1_display
 )

Prints the display data set as RTF and as a listing: the rows of one block stay on one page.

%print(
     data     = t14_2_1_display
   , by       = row
   , var      = c:
   , together = grp
   , label    = %STR(row=" ")
   , file     = &spl_out./tlf/t14_2_1
 )

docs.title: %profileplot
docs.text:
Draws one line per subject through its values by visit as PNG and RTF files and returns the numbers drawn.

Procedure: PROC MEANS, PROC SGPANEL · Family: Figures

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%profileplot(
     data    =
   , plot    =
   , par     =
   , columns =
   , where   =
   , x       =
   , y       =
   , subject = USUBJID
   , by      =
   , panel   =
   , mean    = no
   , xformat =
   , xlabel  =
   , ylabel  =
   , ref     =
   , file    =
   , width   = 6.5in
   , height  = 4.5in
   , out     =
   , outpar  =
   , debug   = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: one record per subject and visit. (required) plot= Draw again: the out= of an earlier %profileplot call, changed or not. It is drawn as it is, and no statistic is computed. Give it instead of data=. (optional) par= The drawing parameters of an earlier %profileplot call: its outpar=. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=. (optional) columns= The data set of %columns: it gives the order of the groups and their colours. When not given, the groups come in the order of the data. (optional) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (anl01fl = 'Y'). (optional) x= The visit: one numeric variable (x = avisitn or x = ady). (required) y= The value: one numeric variable (y = aval). (required) subject= The subject: one variable, one line per subject. (optional, default USUBJID) by= The groups: one variable, one colour per group. (required) panel= A variable: one panel per value, one under the other, each with its own y axis (panel = paramcd). (optional) mean= yes: also draw the mean of each group as a thick line. (optional, default no) Accepts: yes, no. xformat= The format of the ticks of x, as in a FORMAT statement (xformat = visfmt.). When not given, the format of x. (optional) xlabel= The label of the x axis: a text in quotes. When not given, the label of x= (or its name). (optional) ylabel= The label of the y axis: a text in quotes. When not given, the label of y= (or its name). (optional) ref= Reference lines on the y axis: one value or several, separated by blanks (ref = 0 50). (optional) file= The output file without its extension: the macro writes <file>.png (300 dpi) and <file>.rtf. (required) width= The width of the figure: a length with its unit (width = 9in). (optional, default 6.5in) height= The height of the figure: a length with its unit (height = 6in). (optional, default 4.5in) out= The name of the data set of the numbers drawn. When not given, they are not kept. (optional) outpar= The name of the data set of the drawing parameters, one row each. Give it to par= of a later call to draw the figure again. (optional) debug= yes: keep the work data sets profileplot. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: one row per point: the variables of panel=, by= and subject=, KIND, X, Y and N. KIND is subject for a value of a subject, or mean for the mean of a group (the subject is then blank); N is the number of values of a mean. The data set of outpar=: one row per drawing parameter, in the order of the table: PARAMETER ($32), its name, and VALUE ($500), its value as drawn (a label in quotes). The files: <file>.png and <file>.rtf.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use %meanplot for the mean of each group alone, with error bars. Each line is thin, in the colour and line pattern of the group of the subject. With mean=yes, the mean of each group at each visit is also drawn, as a thick line with markers. A record with a missing visit, value, group or panel is not used. To draw the figure again without computing, give plot= the out= and par= the outpar= of an earlier call.

Good to know

Draw again: plot= takes the out= of an earlier %profileplot call, changed or not, and draws it as it is, with no statistic computed. par= takes the outpar= of that call and gives the drawing parameters: columns, subject, by, panel, mean (no: the rows of KIND mean are not drawn), xformat, xlabel, ylabel, ref, file, width, height. These change the picture, not the numbers. The other parameters compute; with plot= the log has a NOTE for each one given, as it is not used. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=, and the row wins over the default of the table.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples run on the example data after examples/setup.sas. The output under each call is the output of that run. They also read t14_2_1_cols (made by the example of %columns). All examples of the reference run as one program: examples/reference.sas.

Before these examples: the calls that make their inputs

Run examples/setup.sas, then these calls from the examples of %describe, %anova, %freq, %chisq, %stack, %columns, in this order. Then the examples of this page run as shown.

/* from the example of %describe */
* Summarizes age in each group and in the Total: n, mean, SD, median, minimum and maximum.;
%describe(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_describe
 )
/* from the example of %anova */
* Tests age across the three groups: one row, the p value of the F test.;
%anova(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_anova
 )
/* from the example of %freq */
* Counts each sex in each group and in the Total: n and the percent of the subjects of the group.;
%freq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_freq
 )
/* from the example of %chisq */
* Tests sex across the groups: one row, the p value of the chi square test.;
%chisq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_chisq
 )
/* from the example of %stack */
* Stacks four results in the order of the table: RESULT and ORD tell where each row came from.;
%stack(age_describe age_anova sex_freq sex_chisq, out=t14_2_1)
/* from the example of %columns */
* Makes the four columns with their N from adsl, the Total last, in the order of TRT01AN.;
%columns(
     data  = t14_2_1
   , n     = adsl
   , var   = trt01a
   , order = trt01an
   , total = yes
   , out   = t14_2_1_cols
 )

Draws the ALT of each subject over the study days: one line per subject, no mean.

%profileplot(
     data    = adlb
   , columns = t14_2_1_cols
   , where   = (paramcd = 'ALT' AND anl01fl = 'Y' AND MISSING(dtype))
   , x       = ady
   , y       = aval
   , by      = trt01a
   , mean    = no
   , file    = &spl_out./figures/f_alt_prof
   , out     = f_alt_prof
 )

docs.title: %proportion
docs.text:
Returns the percent of subjects in each category and group, with its confidence interval by a method you name.

Procedure: PROC FREQ (BINOMIAL) · Family: Describe the data

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%proportion(
     data   =
   , denom  =
   , where  =
   , var    =
   , by     =
   , levels =
   , ci     = clopper-pearson
   , level  = 0.95
   , stats  = n="XX" pct="(XX.X%)" lcl="XX.X" ucl="XX.X"
   , label  =
   , out    =
   , debug  = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: the records, with USUBJID. (required) denom= The subjects of the percent: a data set with one row per subject and the variable of by=. When not given, the subjects of data= (without where=). (optional) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (avisit = 'Week 24'). (optional) var= The category: one variable. (required) by= The groups: one variable, the columns of the table. (required) levels= The planned categories: the variable, then its values in quotes (levels = avalc 'CR' 'PR'). A planned category without a subject shows with n = 0. (optional) ci= The method of the interval: clopper-pearson (the exact interval, CL=EXACT; exact is another name for it), wilson (the score interval, CL=WILSON), wald (CL=WALD) or agresti-coull (CL=AGRESTICOULL). (optional, default clopper-pearson) level= The confidence level: a number between 0 and 1 (level = 0.90). (optional, default 0.95) stats= The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with its pattern of the printed number, separated by blanks. The names are n, pct, lcl and ucl. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns. (optional, default n="XX" pct="(XX.X%)" lcl="XX.X" ucl="XX.X") label= The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table. (optional) out= The name of the result data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets proportion. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the result shape, one row per group, category and statistic: the variables of by= and var=, GROUPS (by= and var=), BLOCK, STAT, VALUE and TEXT. When no record qualifies and levels= is not given, the result has no row.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: Use %freq for counts and percents without an interval. The statistics are n, pct, and lcl and ucl: the limits of the interval, in percent like pct. A subject is counted once in each category. The percent is of the subjects of the group in denom=. The interval comes from the BINOMIAL option of PROC FREQ.

docs.title: %rate
docs.text:
Returns the exposure-adjusted incidence rate of each group, with its exact Poisson confidence limits.

Procedure: PROC FREQ, PROC MEANS, CINV · Family: Describe the data

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%rate(
     data     =
   , denom    =
   , where    =
   , by       =
   , exposure =
   , count    = subjects
   , per      = 100
   , level    = 0.95
   , stats    =
   , label    =
   , out      =
   , debug    = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: the records of the events, with USUBJID. (required) denom= The subjects of the groups with their exposure: a data set with one row per subject, USUBJID and the variable of by=. (required) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (trtemfl = 'Y'). (optional) by= The groups: one variable, in data= and in denom=. (required) exposure= The exposure of a subject: a numeric variable of denom=, or an expression of its variables (exposure = trtdur / 365.25 gives years). (required) count= What the rate counts: subjects (the subjects with a record, each once) or events (every record). (optional, default subjects) Accepts: subjects, events. per= The units of exposure of the rate: a number (per = 1000 gives the rate per 1000 patient-years). The row label of %layout reads "Rate per 100 patient-years"; with another per=, change LABEL in the display data set. (optional, default 100) level= The confidence level: a number between 0 and 1 (level = 0.90). (optional, default 0.95) stats= The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with its pattern of the printed number, separated by blanks. The names are n, events, exposure, rate, lcl and ucl. When not given: n (events with count=events), exposure, rate, lcl and ucl. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns. (optional) label= The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table. (optional) out= The name of the result data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets rate. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the result shape, one row per group and statistic: the variable of by=, GROUPS (by=), BLOCK, STAT, VALUE and TEXT. Every group of denom= has its rows: n = 0 when no subject of it has a record.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use %freq for the percent of subjects with an event, and %rateratio to compare the rates of two groups. The statistics:

  • n: the subjects with a record (PROC FREQ); events: every record
  • exposure: the sum of the exposure of the subjects of the group in denom= (PROC MEANS)
  • rate: n (or events with count=events) divided by the exposure, times per=
  • lcl, ucl: the exact Poisson limits, the chi-square quantiles (CINV) of 2n and 2(n + 1) degrees of freedom, halved, divided by the exposure, times per=

docs.text:

Procedure: PROC GENMOD (LSMEANS) · Family: Compare groups with a model

 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set, with USUBJID: one record per subject. (required) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (trtdurd > 0). (optional) var= The count: one numeric variable (var = teaecnt). (required) by= The groups of the model: one character variable. (required) exposure= The exposure of each subject: a numeric variable, or an expression of variables of data=, such as exposure = trtdurd / 365.25 for years. A subject with an exposure of 0 or less is not used in the model. (required) within= One model in each group of these variables, separated by blanks, such as the levels of a subgroup (within = sex). (optional) covars= The covariates: numeric variables separated by blanks (covars = age). (optional) class= The class factors besides the groups: variables separated by blanks (class = sex). (optional) dist= The distribution of the count: poisson, or negbin (also nb) for the negative binomial. (optional, default poisson) Accepts: poisson, negbin, nb. pairs= The pairs of groups to compare. all: each later group against each earlier one, in the order of order= (or of the values). Or the pairs separated by #, each the group first and then the group it is compared with, a value with a blank or a hyphen in quotes: pairs = "Drug" "Placebo" # "High" "Low". (optional, default all) order= The order of the groups: one numeric variable with one value per group (order = trt01an). (optional) level= The confidence level of the limits: a number between 0 and 1. (optional, default 0.95) stats= The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with the pattern of its printed number, separated by blanks. The names are irr, lcl, ucl and pval. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns. (optional, default irr="XX.XX" lcl="XX.XX" ucl="XX.XX" pval="X.XXX") label= The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table. (optional) out= The name of the result data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets rateratio. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the result shape, one row per pair and statistic: the group in the by= variable, the group it is compared with in VERSUS, and the variables of within=. irr is the rate of the count per unit of exposure in the group over that rate in VERSUS, adjusted for the covariates and the class factors (a rate ratio above 1: more events per unit of exposure in the group), lcl and ucl its confidence limits, pval its p-value. With pairs=all the group is the later one in the order of order=. GROUPS is the by= variable, VERSUS and the within= variables.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use %rate for the rate of each group without a model. The model is PROC GENMOD of a count with the logarithm of the exposure as the offset, on the groups, the covariates and the class factors, one record per subject (the first with a count). The dispersion k of a negative binomial model is estimated by maximum likelihood. All pairs come from one fit.

Good to know

The standard errors of a negative binomial model are those of PROC GENMOD: the observed information of the coefficients and the dispersion together. The R twin of this macro (rateratio() of the R package sapling, a separate product) computes the same.

Compares the event counts in a negative binomial model: STAT irr is the rate ratio.

%rateratio(
     data     = adsl
   , where    = (trtdurd > 0)
   , var      = teaecnt
   , by       = trt01a
   , exposure = trtdurd / 365.25
   , dist     = negbin
   , order    = trt01an
   , out      = ae_rr
 )

docs.title: %relchange
docs.text:
Returns new records with the change from the record before, relative to the normal range, flagged in ANRIND.

Procedure: PROC SORT, a DATA step (LAG) · Family: ADaM steps

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%relchange(
     data   =
   , where  =
   , value  =
   , by     = USUBJID PARAMCD
   , lo     = A1LO
   , hi     = A1HI
   , order  = VISITNUM ADT LBSEQ
   , prefix = _
   , digits = 1
   , limit  = 1
   , reset  = BASE CHG BNRIND R2A1LO R2A1HI BR2A1LO BR2A1HI
   , out    =
   , debug  = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set, such as adlb; it is not changed. (required) where= The records to read: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (paramcd = 'ALT'). The record before is one of these records. (optional) value= The numeric variable of the measured value, such as lbstresn. (required) by= The groups: variables separated by blanks. The first record of a group has no record before. (optional, default USUBJID PARAMCD) lo= The numeric variable of the lower limit of the normal range. (optional, default A1LO) hi= The numeric variable of the upper limit of the normal range. (optional, default A1HI) order= The variables that sort the records of a group and so give the record before, separated by blanks. A missing value sorts first. (optional, default VISITNUM ADT LBSEQ) prefix= The text put before PARAMCD in the new records, without quotes. (optional, default _) digits= The number of decimals of AVAL. (optional, default 1) limit= The limit of ANRIND, in half ranges: H above limit=, L below -limit=. The value 1 is half the normal range. (optional, default 1) reset= The variables that are set missing on the new records, separated by blanks; a variable that data= does not have is skipped. (optional, default BASE CHG BNRIND R2A1LO R2A1HI BR2A1LO BR2A1HI) out= The name of the data set of the new records. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets relchange. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: one new record for each record read, sorted by by= and order=, with the variables of data=. The limits and the variables of reset= are missing. PARAMCD keeps its length in data=, so it must be long enough for the new codes (the generated programs give it the length of the specification, which lists them).

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Each new record compares a value with the value of the record before it in its group (by=, sorted by order=): the change is divided by half the width of the normal range, so 1 is a change as large as half the range, and limit=1 flags a change larger than half the normal range as abnormal. For each record read, the new record has:

  • PARAMCD: prefix= before the code of the record
  • AVAL: (value - the value of the record before) / ((upper limit - lower limit) / 2), rounded to digits= decimals
  • ANRIND: H when AVAL is above limit=, L when it is below -limit=, N between, blank when AVAL is missing

AVAL is missing on the first record of a group, on a record with no AVISITN, and when a value or a limit is missing or the upper limit is not above the lower one. For the change from baseline (CHG = AVAL - BASE), use %baseline and a DATA step.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples run on the example data after examples/setup.sas. The output under each call is the output of that run. All examples of the reference run as one program: examples/reference.sas.

%relchange(
     data  = adlb
   , where = (paramcd = 'ALT' AND MISSING(dtype))
   , value = lbstresn
   , lo    = anrlo
   , hi    = anrhi
   , out   = alt_rel
 )

docs.title: %risk
docs.text:
Returns the risk difference, relative risk or odds ratio of pairs of groups, with its confidence interval and p-value.

Procedure: PROC FREQ (RISKDIFF, RELRISK, CHISQ; COMMONRISKDIFF, CMH) · Family: Compare groups with a model

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%risk(
     data    =
   , where   =
   , var     =
   , event   = "Y"
   , by      =
   , within  =
   , strata  =
   , pairs   = all
   , order   =
   , measure = rd
   , ci      = wald
   , level   = 0.95
   , stats   =
   , label   =
   , out     =
   , debug   = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set, with USUBJID: one record per subject, or per subject and term with within=. (required) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (saffl = 'Y'). (optional) var= The response: one variable with two values, numeric or character. (required) event= The value of var= that is the event, in quotes (event = "DISCONTINUED"). (optional, default "Y") by= The groups: one character variable. (required) within= One comparison in each group of these variables, separated by blanks, such as each term of an adverse event table with the flags of %termflags (within = aebodsys aedecod). (optional) strata= The strata of the Mantel-Haenszel risk difference: variables separated by blanks. Only with measure=rd. (optional) pairs= The pairs of groups to compare. all: each later group against each earlier one, in the order of order= (or of the values). Or the pairs separated by #, each the group first and then the group it is compared with, a value with a blank or a hyphen in quotes: pairs = "Drug" "Placebo" # "High" "Low". (optional, default all) order= The order of the groups: one numeric variable with one value per group (order = trt01an). (optional) measure= The estimate of the group against the group it is compared with: rd, the risk difference, a difference of two proportions between -1 and 1 (0.25 is 25 percentage points), not of percents; rr, the relative risk, the ratio of the two risks; or or, the odds ratio, the ratio of the two odds. A ratio has no unit. (optional, default rd) Accepts: rd, rr, or. ci= The interval of a risk difference: wald, the Wald interval (CL=WALD); newcombe, the hybrid score interval of Newcombe, from the Wilson interval of each risk (CL=NEWCOMBE); mn or miettinen-nurminen, the score interval of Miettinen and Nurminen (CL=MN); ac or agresti-caffo, the interval of Agresti and Caffo, a Wald interval with one event and one non-event added to each group (CL=AC); or mh, the interval of Mantel and Haenszel, which needs strata=. With strata= the interval is always mh, whatever ci= says. (optional, default wald) level= The confidence level of the interval: a number between 0 and 1. (optional, default 0.95) stats= The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with the pattern of its printed number, separated by blanks. When not given: rd="X.XXX" lcl="X.XXX" ucl="X.XXX" pval="X.XXX"; for measure=rr or or, rr="XX.XX" or or="XX.XX" with lcl="XX.XX" ucl="XX.XX" pval="X.XXX". A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns. (optional) label= The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table. (optional) out= The name of the result data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets risk. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the result shape, one row per pair and statistic: the group in the by= variable, the group it is compared with in VERSUS, and the variables of within=. The risk of a group is its subjects with the event of event= over its subjects in the records used. With measure=rd, rd is the risk of the group minus the risk of VERSUS, a difference of two proportions (0.25: 25 percentage points more in the group); with strata=, the Mantel-Haenszel estimate of that difference. With measure=rr, rr is the risk of the group over the risk of VERSUS; with measure=or, or is the odds of the event in the group over the odds in VERSUS. lcl and ucl are the limits of the estimate, pval its p-value. With pairs=all the group is the later one in the order of order=. GROUPS is the by= variable, VERSUS and the within= variables.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use %logistic for an odds ratio adjusted for covariates in a model, and %fisher for only the p-value of an adverse event. For each pair the macro makes the 2 x 2 table of the two groups (the group first) by the event of event= against the rest, one record per subject, with PROC FREQ. measure= gives the estimate:

  • rd: the risk difference, with the interval of ci=
  • rr: the relative risk, with the Wald interval of its logarithm
  • or: the odds ratio, with the Wald interval of its logarithm

The p-value is that of Pearson's chi-square test without continuity correction. With strata= the macro gives the Mantel-Haenszel risk difference (COMMONRISKDIFF, CL=MH) and the p-value of the CMH test.

docs.title: %scatterplot
docs.text:
Draws the values of two variables against each other as PNG and RTF files and returns the numbers drawn.

Procedure: PROC REG, PROC SGPANEL · Family: Figures

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%scatterplot(
     data     =
   , plot     =
   , par      =
   , columns  =
   , where    =
   , x        =
   , y        =
   , by       =
   , panel    =
   , fit      = none
   , identity = no
   , xlabel   =
   , ylabel   =
   , ref      =
   , file     =
   , width    = 6.5in
   , height   = 4.5in
   , out      =
   , outpar   =
   , debug    = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: one record per point. (required) plot= Draw again: the out= of an earlier %scatterplot call, changed or not. It is drawn as it is, and no statistic is computed. Give it instead of data=. (optional) par= The drawing parameters of an earlier %scatterplot call: its outpar=. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=. (optional) columns= The data set of %columns: it gives the order of the groups and their colours. When not given, the groups come in the order of the data. (optional) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (anl01fl = 'Y'). (optional) x= The variable of the x axis: one numeric variable (x = base). (required) y= The variable of the y axis: one numeric variable (y = aval). (required) by= The groups: one variable, one colour and marker per group. (required) panel= A variable: one panel per value (panel = sex). (optional) fit= The line of each group: none, linear (the least squares line) or loess. (optional, default none) Accepts: none, linear, loess. identity= yes: draw the line y = x. (optional, default no) Accepts: yes, no. xlabel= The label of the x axis: a text in quotes. When not given, the label of x= (or its name). (optional) ylabel= The label of the y axis: a text in quotes. When not given, the label of y= (or its name). (optional) ref= Reference lines on the y axis: one value or several, separated by blanks (ref = 0 50). (optional) file= The output file without its extension: the macro writes <file>.png (300 dpi) and <file>.rtf. (required) width= The width of the figure: a length with its unit (width = 9in). (optional, default 6.5in) height= The height of the figure: a length with its unit (height = 6in). (optional, default 4.5in) out= The name of the data set of the numbers drawn. When not given, they are not kept. (optional) outpar= The name of the data set of the drawing parameters, one row each. Give it to par= of a later call to draw the figure again. (optional) debug= yes: keep the work data sets scatterplot. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the variables of panel= and by=, KIND, X and Y. A row of KIND point is one value. With fit=linear, a row of KIND fit is one panel and group, with SLOPE, INTERCEPT, RSQUARE and N (X and Y missing). The data set of outpar=: one row per drawing parameter, in the order of the table: PARAMETER ($32), its name, and VALUE ($500), its value as drawn (a label in quotes). The files: <file>.png and <file>.rtf.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use %profileplot for the values of each subject over time. Typical uses are a shift plot of the baseline and post-baseline values, or two measures of a subject. Each group has its own colour and marker. With fit=linear, the least squares line of each group is drawn, and its slope, intercept and R-square are in out=. With fit=loess, the loess curve of SGPLOT is drawn; SGPLOT chooses its smoothing, and the curve is not in out=. With identity=yes, the line y = x is drawn. A record with a missing x, y, group or panel is not used. To draw the figure again without computing, give plot= the out= and par= the outpar= of an earlier call.

Good to know

Draw again: plot= takes the out= of an earlier %scatterplot call, changed or not, and draws it as it is, with no statistic computed: its points, and the line of each row of KIND fit over the X of the points of its group (a loess curve is not in out= and is not drawn again). par= takes the outpar= of that call and gives the drawing parameters: columns, by, panel, identity, xlabel, ylabel, ref, file, width, height. These change the picture, not the numbers. The other parameters compute; with plot= the log has a NOTE for each one given, as it is not used. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=, and the row wins over the default of the table.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples run on the example data after examples/setup.sas. The output under each call is the output of that run. They also read t14_2_1_cols (made by the example of %columns). All examples of the reference run as one program: examples/reference.sas.

Before these examples: the calls that make their inputs

Run examples/setup.sas, then these calls from the examples of %describe, %anova, %freq, %chisq, %stack, %columns, in this order. Then the examples of this page run as shown.

/* from the example of %describe */
* Summarizes age in each group and in the Total: n, mean, SD, median, minimum and maximum.;
%describe(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_describe
 )
/* from the example of %anova */
* Tests age across the three groups: one row, the p value of the F test.;
%anova(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_anova
 )
/* from the example of %freq */
* Counts each sex in each group and in the Total: n and the percent of the subjects of the group.;
%freq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_freq
 )
/* from the example of %chisq */
* Tests sex across the groups: one row, the p value of the chi square test.;
%chisq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_chisq
 )
/* from the example of %stack */
* Stacks four results in the order of the table: RESULT and ORD tell where each row came from.;
%stack(age_describe age_anova sex_freq sex_chisq, out=t14_2_1)
/* from the example of %columns */
* Makes the four columns with their N from adsl, the Total last, in the order of TRT01AN.;
%columns(
     data  = t14_2_1
   , n     = adsl
   , var   = trt01a
   , order = trt01an
   , total = yes
   , out   = t14_2_1_cols
 )

Draws the ALT at Week 24 against its baseline, with the line where the two are equal.

%scatterplot(
     data     = adlb
   , columns  = t14_2_1_cols
   , where    = (paramcd = 'ALT' AND avisit = 'Week 24')
   , x        = base
   , y        = aval
   , by       = trt01a
   , identity = yes
   , file     = &spl_out./figures/f_alt_scat
   , out      = f_alt_scat
 )

docs.text:

Message Fix data= and plot= are both given give data= to compute, or plot= to draw an out= again. plot=<plot> does not exist give plot= an out= of %scatterplot (make it first). plot=<plot> has no variable <variable> give plot= the shape of out=: <the variables of out=>. par=<par> does not exist give par= an outpar= of %scatterplot (make it first). par=<par> has no variables PARAMETER and VALUE give par= an outpar= of %scatterplot. par=<par> has a row of no drawing parameter (with the PARAMETER of the record) give par= rows of outpar= of %scatterplot only.

docs.title: %stack
docs.text:
Stacks results one under another into one table, a block per result, in the order given.

Procedure: a DATA step (SET INDSNAME=) · Family: Build a table

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%stack(
     <results>
   , out     =
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: results (the first value, without a keyword) The results to stack: data set names separated by blanks, in the order of the blocks. Give them first, without a keyword (%stack(a b, out=t)), or as results= (%stack(results=a b, out=t)); a message names them results=. (required) out= The name of the stacked table. (required)

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: all rows of the results in the result shape, with two more variables: RESULT, the name of the result that the row comes from, and ORD, the place of that result in the list (1, 2, ...). A result with no row keeps its number. A result named twice has the place of its first name. %layout lays out the blocks in the order of ORD.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Call it before %columns, %ard and %layout, which read the stacked table. A result is the data set that a statistics macro writes (%describe, %freq, a test or a model): one row per number. Every result has the same variables, the result shape:

  • the group variables, as in the data (TRT01A, AEDECOD, AVISIT ...); VERSUS: the group that a difference is made with
  • GROUPS: the names of the group variables, in their order
  • BLOCK: the label of the block
  • STAT: the name of the statistic (n, pct, mean, pval ...)
  • VALUE: the number
  • TEXT: the number as printed

A block is the rows of one call in the table: the rows of one result, under its label. A DATA step of your own can write a result in the same shape. Each variable gets the longest length it has in the results, so that no text is cut.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples run on the example data after examples/setup.sas. The output under each call is the output of that run. They also read age_describe (made by the example of %describe), age_anova (made by the example of %anova), sex_freq (made by the example of %freq), sex_chisq (made by the example of %chisq), hr_sex (made by the example of %cox), hr_age (made by the example of %cox), age_sex (made by the example of %describe), agegr_sex (made by the example of %freq). All examples of the reference run as one program: examples/reference.sas.

Before these examples: the calls that make their inputs

Run examples/setup.sas, then these calls from the examples of %tte, %describe, %anova, %freq, %chisq, %cox, in this order. Then the examples of this page run as shown.

/* from the example of %tte */
* Makes TTDE. Log NOTE: 2 subject(s) with no event and no censoring date: no record (no TRTEDT).;
%tte(
     subjects      = adsl
   , events        = adae
   , event         = trtemfl = 'Y' AND aebodsys = 'SKIN AND SUBCUTANEOUS TISSUE DISORDERS'
   , date          = astdt
   , start         = trtsdt
   , censor_date   = trtedt
   , seq           = aeseq
   , censor_desc   = "End of treatment"
   , censor_source = "ADSL"
   , event_desc    = aedecod
   , source        = "ADAE"
   , paramcd       = "TTDE"
   , out           = adttde
 )
/* from the example of %describe */
* Summarizes age in each group and in the Total: n, mean, SD, median, minimum and maximum.;
%describe(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_describe
 )
* Adds sex as a second BY variable: the rows of each group and sex, for a page per sex.;
%describe(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a sex
   , total = yes
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_sex
 )
/* from the example of %anova */
* Tests age across the three groups: one row, the p value of the F test.;
%anova(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_anova
 )
/* from the example of %freq */
* Counts each sex in each group and in the Total: n and the percent of the subjects of the group.;
%freq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_freq
 )
* Adds sex as a second BY variable: the age groups of each group and sex, for a page per sex.;
%freq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = agegr1
   , by    = trt01a sex
   , total = yes
   , label = "Age group"
   , out   = agegr_sex
 )
/* from the example of %chisq */
* Tests sex across the groups: one row, the p value of the chi square test.;
%chisq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_chisq
 )
/* from the example of %cox */
* Gives the hazard ratio against Placebo for each sex: the rows carry SEX, for a forest plot.;
%cox(
     data   = adttde
   , var    = aval
   , by     = trt01a
   , within = sex
   , pairs  = "Xanomeline High Dose" "Placebo"
            # "Xanomeline Low Dose"  "Placebo"
   , out    = hr_sex
 )
* Gives the hazard ratio against Placebo for each age group.;
%cox(
     data   = adttde
   , var    = aval
   , by     = trt01a
   , within = agegr1
   , pairs  = "Xanomeline High Dose" "Placebo"
            # "Xanomeline Low Dose"  "Placebo"
   , out    = hr_age
 )

docs.title: %study
docs.text:
Starts a program: sets the study, the program and the output folder, opens the ADaM library, sets the options.

Procedure: LIBNAME, OPTIONS · Family: Start a program

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%study(
     <id>
   , program =
   , adam    = &spl_root./adam
   , out     = &spl_root./out
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: id (the first value, without a keyword) The name of the study: a text without quotes, given first, without a keyword (%study(CDISCPILOT01, ...)). (required) program= The name of this program, without quotes (program = t14_2_01). %ard names the numbers file after it when its file= is not given. (required) adam= The folder of the ADaM data sets: a path without quotes. The macro opens it as the library ADAM, read only. SPL_ROOT is the folder of the library (it holds macros/): give adam= when the study is in a folder of its own. (optional, default &spl_root./adam) out= The output folder: a path without quotes. The macros write into its folders tlf, listings, figures and ard. SPL_ROOT is the folder of the library (it holds macros/): give out= when the study is in a folder of its own. (optional, default &spl_root./out)

docs.title: Result
docs.text: What it sets: the global macro variables SPL_STUDY, SPL_PROGRAM (in lower case) and SPL_OUT; the library ADAM (read only); the options NODATE NONUMBER NOCENTER LS=160 PS=32767 MISSING=' ' VALIDVARNAME=upcase NOFMTERR FORMDLIM=' '; no TITLE and no FOOTNOTE.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Call it once, at the top of each program, before any other macro of the library. The ADaM library ADAM is read only. %ard names the numbers file after the program when its file= is not given. The macro also clears the TITLE and FOOTNOTE statements. The options, and why each is set:

  • NODATE NONUMBER NOCENTER: no date and no page number at the top of a page, and the text starts at the left margin, as the outputs are laid out.
  • LS=160: a line of a listing is 160 characters wide, the width of a landscape table.
  • PS=32767: the longest page SAS has, so that SAS never breaks a part of a listing; %print starts each page itself (rows=).
  • FORMDLIM=' ': a new page of the LISTING output is a blank line, not a form feed.
  • MISSING=' ': a missing number prints as a blank, not as a period.
  • VALIDVARNAME=UPCASE: the names of the variables a program makes are in upper case, as in the ADaM data sets.
  • NOFMTERR: a format that is not found does not stop the program: the value prints with the default format, and the log has only a NOTE. The risk: a code prints in place of its label (F in place of Female); look for the NOTE "Format ... was not found" in the log.

To set an option back, write an OPTIONS statement after the call of %study: OPTIONS FMTERR stops the program again at a format that is not found, OPTIONS CENTER centers the output again.

docs.title: %summarize
docs.text:
Gives each subject the sum, mean, largest or smallest value of a variable over its records in another data set.

Procedure: PROC SUMMARY, MERGE · Family: ADaM steps

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%summarize(
     data  =
   , from  =
   , value =
   , stat  = sum
   , new   =
   , debug = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The data set to change in place, such as adsl. (required) from= The data set of the records, with USUBJID. When the value is not a variable yet, make it first in a DATA step. (required) value= The numeric variable of from= to summarize. To count records, give a 0/1 variable and stat=sum; for "some record meets it" use stat=max, for "every record meets it" stat=min. (required) stat= The statistic: sum, mean, max or min. (optional, default sum) Accepts: sum, mean, max, min. new= The name of the new variable. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets summarize. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data sets: data=, changed in place: the variable new= on every row of a subject, with the sum, mean, maximum or minimum of value= over its records in from=. A subject with no record gets a missing value.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: Use %summarize_groups for one record per group instead of a new variable on each subject. A subject with no record gets a missing value. A sum of only missing values is missing. The rows of data= keep their order.

docs.title: %summarize_groups
docs.text:
Returns one record per group with the sum, mean, largest or smallest value of each variable over the group.

Procedure: PROC SUMMARY · Family: ADaM steps

docs.title: Syntax

   , out   =

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set. When a value is not a variable yet (a condition as 0 or 1), make it first in a DATA step. (required) by= The groups: one variable or several, separated by blanks (by = usubjid paramcd). (required) vars= The numeric variables to summarize, separated by blanks. (required) stats= One statistic for each variable of vars=, in the same order, separated by blanks: sum, mean, max or min (stats = sum max). (required) out= The name of the data set it writes. (required)

docs.title: %table
docs.text:
Makes a table from the stacked results in one call: %columns, %ard, %layout and %print, in that order.

Procedure: none of its own (those of %columns, %ard, %layout, %print) · Family: Tables in one call

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%table(
     data   =
   , n      =
   , var    =
   , order  =
   , total  = no
   , format =
   , label  =
   , rows   = 40
   , file   =
   , nodata =
   , setup  =
   , out    =
   , debug  = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The results stacked by %stack: one data set in the result shape. (required) n= The population for the N of each column: a data set with one row per subject (n= of %columns). When not given, the columns have no N. (optional) var= The column variable of the results: one variable, such as var = trt01a. (required) order= The numeric twin of var= in the data set of n=, such as order = trt01an: it gives the order of the columns. (optional) total= yes: the results have the group Total, and it is the last column (total= of %columns). A text in quotes is another name for the Total. (optional, default no) format= The labels of the categories: pairs of a variable and a format, as in a FORMAT statement (format = sex $sexf. race $racef.), as format= of %layout. (optional) label= The labels of the columns: pairs name="text", separated by blanks (label= of %print). (optional) rows= The number of rows a page holds: %print keeps the rows of one level on one page when they fit. (optional, default 40) file= The output file without its extension: the macro writes <file>.rtf, <file>.lst and the numbers file <out>/ard/<last part of file>.csv. When not given, nothing is printed. (optional) nodata= The text printed when the table has no row: a text in quotes. (optional) setup= The name of a global macro variable that keeps the call of %print for out=. When not given, no macro variable is left. (optional) out= The name of the display data set. When not given, it is <data>_display. (optional) debug= yes: keep the work data sets of the macros that %table calls. (optional, default no) Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the display data set of %layout. The data sets: <data>_cols, the columns of %columns. The files: <file>.rtf and <file>.lst of %print, and the numbers file of %ard (only with file=). The global macro variable: with setup=, the global macro variable of that name, which holds the parameters of %print for out=.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: Use %table when the defaults of the four steps fit; call %columns, %ard, %layout and %print one by one to change a step between them. It passes them the same parameters as the separate calls and adds no logic of its own. The display data set is the data set %layout writes: one row per printed line, one column per printed column. The numbers file is the CSV file of %ard with every number of the table; the macro writes it only with file=, because it belongs to an output. The columns <data>_cols and the display data set out= stay in WORK. With setup=, a global macro variable also keeps the call of %print for out=: change out=, then print again with %print(&<setup>.). Without file=, the macro prints nothing: change out=, then call %print(&<setup>., file=...).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples run on the example data after examples/setup.sas. The output under each call is the output of that run. They also read t14_2_1 (made by the example of %stack). All examples of the reference run as one program: examples/reference.sas.

Before these examples: the calls that make their inputs

Run examples/setup.sas, then these calls from the examples of %describe, %anova, %freq, %chisq, %stack, %columns, %ard, in this order. Then the examples of this page run as shown.

/* from the example of %describe */
* Summarizes age in each group and in the Total: n, mean, SD, median, minimum and maximum.;
%describe(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_describe
 )
/* from the example of %anova */
* Tests age across the three groups: one row, the p value of the F test.;
%anova(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_anova
 )
/* from the example of %freq */
* Counts each sex in each group and in the Total: n and the percent of the subjects of the group.;
%freq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_freq
 )
/* from the example of %chisq */
* Tests sex across the groups: one row, the p value of the chi square test.;
%chisq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_chisq
 )
/* from the example of %stack */
* Stacks four results in the order of the table: RESULT and ORD tell where each row came from.;
%stack(age_describe age_anova sex_freq sex_chisq, out=t14_2_1)
/* from the example of %columns */
* Makes the four columns with their N from adsl, the Total last, in the order of TRT01AN.;
%columns(
     data  = t14_2_1
   , n     = adsl
   , var   = trt01a
   , order = trt01an
   , total = yes
   , out   = t14_2_1_cols
 )
/* from the example of %ard */
* Writes every number of the table and each column N to one CSV file: the raw value and the text.;
%ard(data=t14_2_1, columns=t14_2_1_cols, file=t14_2_1)

Runs columns, ard, layout and print in one call: the same table as the long program.

%table(
     data   = t14_2_1
   , n      = adsl
   , var    = trt01a
   , order  = trt01an
   , total  = yes
   , format = sex $sexf.
   , file   = &spl_out./tlf/t14_2_1_table
   , setup  = t14_2_1_table_print
 )

docs.title: %table_ae
docs.text:
Makes a table of the subjects with adverse events by system organ class and preferred term in one call.

Procedure: none of its own (those of %freq, %table) · Family: Tables in one call

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%table_ae(
     data      =
   , adsl      =
   , pop       =
   , where     =
   , var       =
   , by        =
   , order     =
   , sort      =
   , threshold =
   , total     = no
   , format    =
   , name      =
   , show      = no
   , label     =
   , stats     =
   , title     =
   , footnote  =
   , file      =
   , debug     = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: the records, with USUBJID. (required) adsl= The subjects: a data set with one row per subject. It gives the population and the N of each column, and its variables are merged onto the records by USUBJID. When not given, the N of a column is the subjects of its records. (optional) pop= The population: a condition on adsl= in parentheses, such as pop = (saffl = 'Y'). It is used only with adsl=. (optional) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (trtemfl = 'Y'). (optional) var= The variables of the rows, nested in their order and separated by blanks, such as var = aebodsys aedecod. (required) by= The groups of the columns: one character variable, such as by = trt01a. (required) order= The numeric twin of by=, such as order = trt01an: it gives the order of the columns. (optional) sort= frequency: the rows of the last variable of var= in the order of their subjects, the most first (order=frequency of %freq). When not given, the rows are in the order of their values. (optional) Accepts: frequency. threshold= A percent: keep only the rows whose percent of subjects reaches it in at least one group (threshold= of %freq), such as threshold = 5. (optional) total= yes: add the column Total, all groups together. (optional, default no) Accepts: yes, no. format= The labels of the categories: pairs of a variable and a format, as in a FORMAT statement (format = sex $sexf. race $racef.), as format= of %layout. (optional) name= The name of the table: the first part of the names of its data sets, such as name = t14_3_01. When not given, the last part of file= is used; without file=, name= is required. (optional) show= yes: write the long program to the log. A file path, without quotes: write the long program to that file. In both cases the macro runs it. (optional, default no) label= The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. (optional) stats= The statistics, each name with its pattern, separated by blanks (stats= of %freq), such as stats = n pct events. (optional) title= The titles of the table: one text in quotes per line (TITLE1, TITLE2 ...). They hold for this table only. When not given, the TITLE statements in force in the program are used. (optional) footnote= The footnotes of the table: one text in quotes per line (FOOTNOTE1, FOOTNOTE2 ...). They hold for this table only. When not given, the FOOTNOTE statements in force in the program are used. (optional) file= The output file without its extension: the macro writes <file>.rtf, <file>.lst and the numbers file. When not given, nothing is printed. (optional) debug= yes: keep the work data sets of the macros that the long program calls. (optional, default no) Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data sets: <name>_ae (the result), <name> (the stacked results), <name>_cols, <name>_display, <name>_pop (with adsl=) and <name>_rec (with adsl= or where=). The files: <file>.rtf, <file>.lst and the numbers file (only with file=). The global macro variable: <name>_print. With show=: the long program, in the log or in a file.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use it for any count of subjects by nested levels of records; to add a block that it does not make, start from its long program (show=). The long program is the program the macro writes and runs: the population, the records, one %freq, %stack and %table, the calls a person would write by hand. The macro computes nothing itself. A subject is counted once in each row, and the percent is of the subjects of the group. These data sets stay in WORK, for a change and a second print:

  • <name>_ae: the result, one row per number (the result shape)
  • <name>: the stacked results
  • <name>_cols: the columns (%columns)
  • <name>_display: the display data set, one row per printed line (%layout)

The global macro variable <name>_print keeps the call of %print: change <name>_display, then print again with %print(&<name>_print.). The table has one block: a system organ class is a heading over its terms and prints without a count, and there is no row of the subjects with any TEAE. To add them, write the long program with show=, and add before the block of the terms in %stack a %freq without var= (any event) and a %freq with var=aebodsys (the subjects of each class), with denom= the population, as the how-to guide "Make an adverse event table" shows.

docs.title: %table_model
docs.text:
Makes a table of a continuous endpoint in one call: descriptive statistics, and the LS means of a model.

Procedure: none of its own (those of %describe, %lsmeans, %mmrm, %table) · Family: Tables in one call

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%table_model(
     data     =
   , adsl     =
   , pop      =
   , where    =
   , var      = CHG
   , covars   =
   , visit    = AVISIT
   , by       =
   , at       =
   , order    =
   , describe =
   , method   = ancova
   , model    =
   , type     = un
   , fallback =
   , pairs    =
   , names    =
   , format   =
   , name     =
   , show     = no
   , stats    =
   , title    =
   , footnote =
   , file     =
   , debug    = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: the records, with USUBJID. (required) adsl= The subjects: a data set with one row per subject. It gives the population and the N of each column, and its variables are merged onto the records by USUBJID. When not given, the N of a column is the subjects of its records. (optional) pop= The population: a condition on adsl= in parentheses, such as pop = (saffl = 'Y'). It is used only with adsl=. (optional) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (paramcd = 'SYSBP'). (optional) var= The response: one numeric variable. (optional, default CHG) covars= The covariates of the model, separated by blanks, such as covars = base. (optional) visit= The variable of the visit: one variable. (optional, default AVISIT) by= The groups of the columns: one character variable, such as by = trt01a. (required) at= The visit of the table: a value of visit= in quotes, such as at = "Week 24". It selects the records of the descriptive blocks and of the ANCOVA, and the visit of the LS means of the MMRM. When not given, the ANCOVA uses all records. (optional) order= The numeric twin of by=, such as order = trt01an: it gives the order of the columns and of the groups in the comparisons. (optional) describe= The variables with a descriptive block before the model, separated by blanks, such as describe = base aval chg. (optional) method= ancova (%lsmeans) or mmrm (%mmrm, which needs at=). (optional, default ancova) Accepts: ancova, mmrm. model= The fixed effects of the MMRM, separated by blanks. When not given: the covariates, the by= variable, the visit= variable and the interaction of the two (such as trt01pavisit). This default has no interaction of a covariate with the visit, such as baseavisit: give model= to add one. (optional) type= The covariance structure of the MMRM: TYPE= of the REPEATED statement, such as un, cs, ar(1) or toep (type= of %mmrm). (optional, default un) fallback= Other covariance structures of the MMRM to try in their order when one does not converge, separated by blanks, such as fallback = toep cs. (optional) pairs= The pairs of groups to compare, separated by #: each group in quotes, then the group it is compared with ("Xanomeline High Dose" "Placebo"). When not given, each later group is compared with each earlier one. (optional) names= The labels of the blocks: pairs variable="text", separated by blanks, such as names = chg="Change from baseline". A block without a pair has the label of its variable, or its name. (optional) format= The labels of the categories: pairs of a variable and a format, as in a FORMAT statement (format = sex $sexf. race $racef.), as format= of %layout. (optional) name= The name of the table: the first part of the names of its data sets, such as name = t14_3_01. When not given, the last part of file= is used; without file=, name= is required. (optional) show= yes: write the long program to the log. A file path, without quotes: write the long program to that file. In both cases the macro runs it. (optional, default no) stats= The statistics of the model block, each name with its pattern. When not given: the LS means with their SE, the difference with its SE and limits, and the p-value. (optional) title= The titles of the table: one text in quotes per line (TITLE1, TITLE2 ...). They hold for this table only. When not given, the TITLE statements in force in the program are used. (optional) footnote= The footnotes of the table: one text in quotes per line (FOOTNOTE1, FOOTNOTE2 ...). They hold for this table only. When not given, the FOOTNOTE statements in force in the program are used. (optional) file= The output file without its extension: the macro writes <file>.rtf, <file>.lst and the numbers file. When not given, nothing is printed. (optional) debug= yes: keep the work data sets of the macros that the long program calls. (optional, default no) Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data sets: <name>_<variable> (the descriptive results), <name>_ancova or <name>_mmrm (the result of the model), <name> (the stacked results), <name>_cols, <name>_display, <name>_at (with at=), <name>_pop (with adsl=) and <name>_rec (with adsl= or where=). The files: <file>.rtf, <file>.lst and the numbers file (only with file=). The global macro variable: <name>_print. With show=: the long program, in the log or in a file. In the printed table, a comparison is in the column of the group, on the rows under "vs" and the group it is compared with: the LS mean of the column group minus the LS mean of the group on the row.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use %table_visit for the statistics at every visit without a model; to add or change a block, start from its long program (show=). A block is the rows of one call in the table. The table has these blocks:

  • one block per variable of describe=: its descriptive statistics on the records of the visit of at= (%describe)
  • with method=ancova: the LS means and the differences of pairs of groups from an ANCOVA on the records of the visit of at= (%lsmeans), in a block with the label "ANCOVA, adjusted for" and the names of covars= in lower case, such as "ANCOVA, adjusted for base" (without covars=: "Analysis of variance")
  • with method=mmrm: the same from a mixed model for repeated measures over all visits, at the visit of at= (%mmrm), in a block with the label "MMRM: " and the visit, such as "MMRM: Week 24"

With method=ancova, the records of the visit of at= must be one record per subject: give where= the parameter and the analysis flag, as %lsmeans uses the first record of a subject (with a NOTE when it leaves one out). The label of the model block is not changed by names=: change its row in <name>_display and print again, or start from the long program (show=). The table has no Total column. The long program is the program the macro writes and runs: the population, the records, one call per block, %stack and %table, the calls a person would write by hand. The macro computes nothing itself. These data sets stay in WORK, for a change and a second print:

  • <name>_<variable> and <name>_ancova or <name>_mmrm: the results, one row per number (the result shape)
  • <name>: the stacked results
  • <name>_cols: the columns (%columns)
  • <name>_display: the display data set, one row per printed line (%layout)

The global macro variable <name>_print keeps the call of %print: change <name>_display, then print again with %print(&<name>_print.).

docs.text:

docs.title: %table_response
docs.text:
Makes a response table in one call: the responders in each group, and the comparisons of pairs of groups.

Procedure: none of its own (those of %proportion, %risk, %logistic, %table) · Family: Tables in one call

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%table_response(
     data     =
   , adsl     =
   , pop      =
   , where    =
   , var      =
   , event    = "Y"
   , by       =
   , covars   =
   , order    =
   , pairs    =
   , ci       = clopper-pearson
   , measure  = rd
   , diffci   = wald
   , format   =
   , name     =
   , show     = no
   , title    =
   , footnote =
   , file     =
   , debug    = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: the records, with USUBJID. (required) adsl= The subjects: a data set with one row per subject. It gives the population and the N of each column, and its variables are merged onto the records by USUBJID. When not given, the N of a column is the subjects of its records. (optional) pop= The population: a condition on adsl= in parentheses, such as pop = (saffl = 'Y'). It is used only with adsl=. (optional) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (trtemfl = 'Y'). (optional) var= The response: one variable with two values. (required) event= The value of var= that is the event: a text in quotes. (optional, default "Y") by= The groups of the columns: one character variable, such as by = trt01a. (required) covars= The covariates, separated by blanks, such as covars = sitegr1: they add a block with the odds ratio adjusted for them (%logistic). When not given, there is no such block. (optional) order= The numeric twin of by=, such as order = trt01an: it gives the order of the columns and of the groups in the comparisons. (optional) pairs= The pairs of groups to compare, separated by #: each group in quotes, then the group it is compared with ("Xanomeline High Dose" "Placebo"). When not given, each later group is compared with each earlier one. (optional) ci= The interval of the percent of responders: clopper-pearson, wilson, wald or agresti-coull (ci= of %proportion). (optional, default clopper-pearson) measure= rd (the risk difference), rr (the relative risk) or or (the odds ratio): the comparison of %risk; none: no comparison. (optional, default rd) Accepts: rd, rr, or, none. diffci= The interval of a risk difference: wald, newcombe, miettinen-nurminen or agresti-caffo (ci= of %risk). It is used only with measure = rd. (optional, default wald) format= The labels of the categories: pairs of a variable and a format, as in a FORMAT statement (format = sex $sexf. race $racef.), as format= of %layout. (optional) name= The name of the table: the first part of the names of its data sets, such as name = t14_3_01. When not given, the last part of file= is used; without file=, name= is required. (optional) show= yes: write the long program to the log. A file path, without quotes: write the long program to that file. In both cases the macro runs it. (optional, default no) title= The titles of the table: one text in quotes per line (TITLE1, TITLE2 ...). They hold for this table only. When not given, the TITLE statements in force in the program are used. (optional) footnote= The footnotes of the table: one text in quotes per line (FOOTNOTE1, FOOTNOTE2 ...). They hold for this table only. When not given, the FOOTNOTE statements in force in the program are used. (optional) file= The output file without its extension: the macro writes <file>.rtf, <file>.lst and the numbers file. When not given, nothing is printed. (optional) debug= yes: keep the work data sets of the macros that the long program calls. (optional, default no) Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data sets: <name>prop, <name><measure> (with a measure) and <name>_adj (with covars=), the results; <name> (the stacked results), <name>_cols, <name>_display, <name>_pop (with adsl=) and <name>_rec (with adsl= or where=). The files: <file>.rtf, <file>.lst and the numbers file (only with file=). The global macro variable: <name>_print. With show=: the long program, in the log or in a file. In the printed table, a comparison is in the column of the group, on the rows under "vs" and the group it is compared with: the risk difference is the proportion of responders of the column group minus that of the group on the row (-0.013: 1.3 percentage points fewer); the relative risk and the odds ratios are the column group over the group on the row.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use %table_ae to count the subjects by levels of events; to add or change a block, start from its long program (show=). A block is the rows of one call in the table. The table has these blocks:

  • the responders, n (%), and the interval of the percent (%proportion)
  • with measure= rd, rr or or: the risk difference, the relative risk or the odds ratio of each pair, with its interval and p-value (%risk)
  • with covars=: the odds ratio adjusted for the covariates, with its interval and p-value (%logistic)

The table has no Total column. The long program is the program the macro writes and runs: the population, the records, one call per block, %stack and %table, the calls a person would write by hand. The macro computes nothing itself. These data sets stay in WORK, for a change and a second print:

  • <name>prop, <name><measure> and <name>_adj: the results, one row per number (the result shape)
  • <name>: the stacked results
  • <name>_cols: the columns (%columns)
  • <name>_display: the display data set, one row per printed line (%layout)

The global macro variable <name>_print keeps the call of %print: change <name>_display, then print again with %print(&<name>_print.).

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%table_shift(
     data     =
   , adsl     =
   , pop      =
   , where    =
   , var      = BNRIND ANRIND
   , within   =
   , by       =
   , keep     =
   , order    =
   , levels   =
   , total    = no

   , name     =

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: the records, with USUBJID. (required) adsl= The subjects: a data set with one row per subject. It gives the population and the N of each column, and its variables are merged onto the records by USUBJID. When not given, the N of a column is the subjects of its records. (optional) pop= The population: a condition on adsl= in parentheses, such as pop = (saffl = 'Y'). It is used only with adsl=. (optional) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (trtemfl = 'Y'). (optional) var= Two variables, separated by a blank: the category at baseline, then the category after baseline. (optional, default BNRIND ANRIND) within= The levels above the two variables of var=, nested in their order and separated by blanks, such as within = paramcd avisit. (optional) by= The groups of the columns: one character variable, such as by = trt01a. (required) keep= Other variables to keep for the names and the order of the rows, separated by blanks (keep= of %freq), such as keep = param avisitn. (optional) order= The numeric twin of by=, such as order = trt01an: it gives the order of the columns. (optional) levels= The planned categories of both variables of var=: values in quotes, separated by blanks, such as levels = 'LOW' 'NORMAL' 'HIGH'. A planned category has a row also without a subject; a record of another category is not counted (levels= of %freq). (optional) total= yes: add the column Total, all groups together. (optional, default no) Accepts: yes, no. format= The labels of the categories: pairs of a variable and a format, as in a FORMAT statement (format = sex $sexf. race $racef.), as format= of %layout. (optional) name= The name of the table: the first part of the names of its data sets, such as name = t14_3_01. When not given, the last part of file= is used; without file=, name= is required. (optional) show= yes: write the long program to the log. A file path, without quotes: write the long program to that file. In both cases the macro runs it. (optional, default no) label= The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. (optional) stats= The statistics, each name with its pattern, separated by blanks (stats= of %freq). (optional) title= The titles of the table: one text in quotes per line (TITLE1, TITLE2 ...). They hold for this table only. When not given, the TITLE statements in force in the program are used. (optional) footnote= The footnotes of the table: one text in quotes per line (FOOTNOTE1, FOOTNOTE2 ...). They hold for this table only. When not given, the FOOTNOTE statements in force in the program are used. (optional) file= The output file without its extension: the macro writes <file>.rtf, <file>.lst and the numbers file. When not given, nothing is printed. (optional) debug= yes: keep the work data sets of the macros that the long program calls. (optional, default no) Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data sets: <name>_shift (the result), <name> (the stacked results), <name>_cols, <name>_display, <name>_pop (with adsl=) and <name>_rec (with adsl= or where=). The files: <file>.rtf, <file>.lst and the numbers file (only with file=). The global macro variable: <name>_print. With show=: the long program, in the log or in a file.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use %table_ae for the subjects by nested levels of events; to add a block that it does not make, start from its long program (show=). The rows are the levels of within= (such as the parameter and the visit), then the category at baseline, then the category after it, in one %freq. The percent is of the subjects of the group that have a record in the records used. The long program is the program the macro writes and runs: the population, the records, one %freq, %stack and %table, the calls a person would write by hand. The macro computes nothing itself. These data sets stay in WORK, for a change and a second print:

  • <name>_shift: the result, one row per number (the result shape)
  • <name>: the stacked results
  • <name>_cols: the columns (%columns)
  • <name>_display: the display data set, one row per printed line (%layout)

The global macro variable <name>_print keeps the call of %print: change <name>_display, then print again with %print(&<name>_print.).

docs.text:
Makes a summary table of the subjects in one call, such as demographics: one block per variable.

Procedure: none of its own (those of %describe, %freq, %table) · Family: Tables in one call

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%table_summary(
     data     =
   , where    =
   , vars     =
   , by       =
   , order    =
   , levels   =
   , total    = no
   , catstats =
