docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: the subjects, one row per subject, such as adsl. (required) where= The population: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (saffl = 'Y'). (optional) vars= The variables of the table in its order, separated by blanks: a name alone for a numeric variable, a name and # for a categorical one, such as vars = age sex# agegr1#agegr1n. (required) by= The groups of the columns: one character variable, such as by = trt01a. (required) order= The numeric twin of by=, such as order = trt01an: it gives the order of the columns. (optional) levels= The planned categories of some categorical variables: each variable, then its values in quotes (levels= of %freq), such as levels = sex 'F' 'M'. A planned category has a row also without a subject. (optional) total= yes: add the column Total, all groups together. (optional, default no) Accepts: yes, no. catstats= The statistics of a categorical variable, each name with its pattern (stats= of %freq). (optional) names= The labels of the blocks: pairs variable="text", separated by blanks, such as names = age="Age (years)". A block without a pair has the label of its variable, or its name. (optional) format= The labels of the categories: pairs of a variable and a format, as in a FORMAT statement (format = sex $sexf. race $racef.), as format= of %layout. (optional) name= The name of the table: the first part of the names of its data sets, such as name = t14_3_01. When not given, the last part of file= is used; without file=, name= is required. (optional) show= yes: write the long program to the log. A file path, without quotes: write the long program to that file. In both cases the macro runs it. (optional, default no) stats= The statistics of a numeric variable, each name with its pattern (stats= of %describe). (optional) title= The titles of the table: one text in quotes per line (TITLE1, TITLE2 ...). They hold for this table only. When not given, the TITLE statements in force in the program are used. (optional) footnote= The footnotes of the table: one text in quotes per line (FOOTNOTE1, FOOTNOTE2 ...). They hold for this table only. When not given, the FOOTNOTE statements in force in the program are used. (optional) file= The output file without its extension: the macro writes <file>.rtf, <file>.lst and the numbers file. When not given, nothing is printed. (optional) debug= yes: keep the work data sets of the macros that the long program calls. (optional, default no) Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data sets: <name>_<variable>_summ (the result of each variable), <name> (the stacked results), <name>_cols, <name>_display, and <name>_pop (only with where=). The files: <file>.rtf, <file>.lst and the numbers file (only with file=). The global macro variable: <name>_print. With show=: the long program, in the log or in a file.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use %table_visit for the values of records at each visit; to add a block that it does not make, start from its long program (show=). A block is the rows of one variable in the table. Name the variables in vars=, in the order of the table:

  • a name alone (age): a numeric variable, described by %describe
  • a name and # (sex#): a categorical variable, counted by %freq
  • a name, # and a numeric variable (agegr1#agegr1n): a categorical variable whose categories are in the order of that variable

A character variable without # stops the macro with an ERROR. The long program is the program the macro writes and runs: the population, one %describe or %freq per variable, %stack and %table, the calls a person would write by hand. The macro computes nothing itself. These data sets stay in WORK, for a change and a second print:

  • <name>_<variable>_summ: the result of each variable, one row per number (the result shape)
  • <name>: the stacked results
  • <name>_cols: the columns (%columns)
  • <name>_display: the display data set, one row per printed line (%layout)

The global macro variable <name>_print keeps the call of %print: change <name>_display, then print again with %print(&<name>_print.).

docs.title: %table_tte
docs.text:
Makes a time-to-event table in one call: the Kaplan-Meier summary, the log-rank test and the hazard ratios.

Procedure: none of its own (those of %km, %logrank, %cox, %table) · Family: Tables in one call

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%table_tte(
     data     =
   , adsl     =
   , pop      =
   , where    =
   , var      = AVAL
   , cnsr     = CNSR
   , by       =
   , time     =
   , strata   =
   , order    =
   , pairs    =
   , format   =
   , name     =
   , show     = no
   , title    =
   , footnote =
   , file     =
   , debug    = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: the records, with USUBJID. (required) adsl= The subjects: a data set with one row per subject. It gives the population and the N of each column, and its variables are merged onto the records by USUBJID. When not given, the N of a column is the subjects of its records. (optional) pop= The population: a condition on adsl= in parentheses, such as pop = (saffl = 'Y'). It is used only with adsl=. (optional) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (trtemfl = 'Y'). (optional) var= The time: one numeric variable. (optional, default AVAL) cnsr= The censoring variable: one numeric variable, 0 for an event and a positive value for a censoring (the ADaM CNSR: 1, 2 ... name the reason). A missing or negative value on a record used stops the macro with an ERROR. (optional, default CNSR) by= The groups of the columns: one character variable, such as by = trt01a. (required) time= A time: adds a block with the percent without an event at that time and its limits (time= of %km), such as time = 182. (optional) strata= The strata of the log-rank test and of the Cox model: variables separated by blanks, such as strata = sitegr1. (optional) order= The numeric twin of by=, such as order = trt01an: it gives the order of the columns and of the groups in the comparisons. (optional) pairs= The pairs of groups to compare, separated by #: each group in quotes, then the group it is compared with ("Xanomeline High Dose" "Placebo"). When not given, each later group is compared with each earlier one. (optional) format= The labels of the categories: pairs of a variable and a format, as in a FORMAT statement (format = sex $sexf. race $racef.), as format= of %layout. (optional) name= The name of the table: the first part of the names of its data sets, such as name = t14_3_01. When not given, the last part of file= is used; without file=, name= is required. (optional) show= yes: write the long program to the log. A file path, without quotes: write the long program to that file. In both cases the macro runs it. (optional, default no) title= The titles of the table: one text in quotes per line (TITLE1, TITLE2 ...). They hold for this table only. When not given, the TITLE statements in force in the program are used. (optional) footnote= The footnotes of the table: one text in quotes per line (FOOTNOTE1, FOOTNOTE2 ...). They hold for this table only. When not given, the FOOTNOTE statements in force in the program are used. (optional) file= The output file without its extension: the macro writes <file>.rtf, <file>.lst and the numbers file. When not given, nothing is printed. (optional) debug= yes: keep the work data sets of the macros that the long program calls. (optional, default no) Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data sets: <name>_km, <name>_surv (with time=), <name>_lr and <name>_cox (the results), <name> (the stacked results), <name>_cols, <name>_display, <name>_pop (with adsl=) and <name>_rec (with adsl= or where=). The files: <file>.rtf, <file>.lst and the numbers file (only with file=). The global macro variable: <name>_print. With show=: the long program, in the log or in a file. In the printed table, a comparison is in the column of the group, on the rows under "vs" and the group it is compared with: the hazard ratio is the hazard of the column group over the hazard of the group on the row (below 1: fewer events in the column group).

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use %kmplot for the Kaplan-Meier curves; to add or change a block, start from its long program (show=). A block is the rows of one call in the table. The table has these blocks:

  • the subjects, the events, and the median time with its 95% interval in each group (%km)
  • with time=: the percent without an event at that time and its limits (%km)
  • the log-rank test of the groups (%logrank)
  • the hazard ratio of each pair of groups from a Cox model, with its interval and p-value (%cox)

The table has no Total column. The long program is the program the macro writes and runs: the population, the records, one call per block, %stack and %table, the calls a person would write by hand. The macro computes nothing itself. These data sets stay in WORK, for a change and a second print:

  • <name>_km, <name>_surv, <name>_lr and <name>_cox: the results, one row per number (the result shape)
  • <name>: the stacked results
  • <name>_cols: the columns (%columns)
  • <name>_display: the display data set, one row per printed line (%layout)

The global macro variable <name>_print keeps the call of %print: change <name>_display, then print again with %print(&<name>_print.). CNSR 0 is an event and any positive value is a censoring, as in ADaM, where the value names the reason of the censoring: a CNSR of 2 is censored as 1 is. A record used with a missing or negative CNSR stops the macro with an ERROR. In the second example the column N of Placebo is 86 (from adsl=) while n of the Kaplan-Meier block is 85: the 2 subjects with a missing TRTEDT have no event and no censoring date, so %tte gives them no record in adttde.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples run on the example data after examples/setup.sas. The output under each call is the output of that run. They also read adttde (made by the example of %tte). All examples of the reference run as one program: examples/reference.sas.

Before these examples: the calls that make their inputs

Run examples/setup.sas, then these calls from the examples of %tte, in this order. Then the examples of this page run as shown.

/* from the example of %tte */
* Makes TTDE. Log NOTE: 2 subject(s) with no event and no censoring date: no record (no TRTEDT).;
%tte(
     subjects      = adsl
   , events        = adae
   , event         = trtemfl = 'Y' AND aebodsys = 'SKIN AND SUBCUTANEOUS TISSUE DISORDERS'
   , date          = astdt
   , start         = trtsdt
   , censor_date   = trtedt
   , seq           = aeseq
   , censor_desc   = "End of treatment"
   , censor_source = "ADSL"
   , event_desc    = aedecod
   , source        = "ADAE"
   , paramcd       = "TTDE"
   , out           = adttde
 )

docs.title: %table_visit
docs.text:
Makes a table of the descriptive statistics of each variable by group, parameter and visit in one call.

Procedure: none of its own (those of %describe, %table) · Family: Tables in one call

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%table_visit(
     data      =
   , adsl      =
   , pop       =
   , where     =
   , vars      =
   , by        =
   , param     = PARAMCD
   , visit     = AVISIT
   , keep      =
   , order     =
   , post      =
   , postwhere = (ablfl NE 'Y')
   , names     =
   , total     = no
   , format    =
   , name      =
   , show      = no
   , stats     =
   , title     =
   , footnote  =
   , file      =
   , debug     = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: the records, with USUBJID. (required) adsl= The subjects: a data set with one row per subject. It gives the population and the N of each column, and its variables are merged onto the records by USUBJID. When not given, the N of a column is the subjects of its records. (optional) pop= The population: a condition on adsl= in parentheses, such as pop = (saffl = 'Y'). It is used only with adsl=. (optional) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (trtemfl = 'Y'). (optional) vars= The numeric variables to describe, separated by blanks: one block each, such as vars = aval chg. (required) by= The groups of the columns: one character variable, such as by = trt01a. (required) param= The variable of the parameter: one variable. (optional, default PARAMCD) visit= The variable of the visit: one variable. (optional, default AVISIT) keep= Other variables to keep for the names and the order of the rows, separated by blanks (keep= of %describe), such as keep = param paramn avisitn. (optional) order= The numeric twin of by=, such as order = trt01an: it gives the order of the columns. (optional) post= The variables of vars= whose block uses only the records of postwhere=, separated by blanks, such as post = chg. (optional) postwhere= The records after baseline: a condition in parentheses. (optional, default (ablfl NE 'Y')) names= The labels of the blocks: pairs variable="text", separated by blanks, such as names = chg="Change from baseline". A block without a pair has the label of its variable, or its name. (optional) total= yes: add the column Total, all groups together. (optional, default no) Accepts: yes, no. format= The labels of the categories: pairs of a variable and a format, as in a FORMAT statement (format = sex $sexf. race $racef.), as format= of %layout. (optional) name= The name of the table: the first part of the names of its data sets, such as name = t14_3_01. When not given, the last part of file= is used; without file=, name= is required. (optional) show= yes: write the long program to the log. A file path, without quotes: write the long program to that file. In both cases the macro runs it. (optional, default no) stats= The statistics, each name with its pattern, separated by blanks (stats= of %describe). (optional) title= The titles of the table: one text in quotes per line (TITLE1, TITLE2 ...). They hold for this table only. When not given, the TITLE statements in force in the program are used. (optional) footnote= The footnotes of the table: one text in quotes per line (FOOTNOTE1, FOOTNOTE2 ...). They hold for this table only. When not given, the FOOTNOTE statements in force in the program are used. (optional) file= The output file without its extension: the macro writes <file>.rtf, <file>.lst and the numbers file. When not given, nothing is printed. (optional) debug= yes: keep the work data sets of the macros that the long program calls. (optional, default no) Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data sets: <name>_<variable> (the result of each variable), <name> (the stacked results), <name>_cols, <name>_display, <name>_pop (with adsl=) and <name>_rec (with adsl= or where=). The files: <file>.rtf, <file>.lst and the numbers file (only with file=). The global macro variable: <name>_print. With show=: the long program, in the log or in a file.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use it for vital signs or laboratory values over the visits; use %table_summary for one row per subject, and %table_model for a model at one visit. A block is the rows of one variable of vars= in the table: one %describe of the records with by= the group, the parameter and the visit. The long program is the program the macro writes and runs: the population, the records, one %describe per variable, %stack and %table, the calls a person would write by hand. The macro computes nothing itself. These data sets stay in WORK, for a change and a second print:

  • <name>_<variable>: the result of each variable, one row per number (the result shape)
  • <name>: the stacked results
  • <name>_cols: the columns (%columns)
  • <name>_display: the display data set, one row per printed line (%layout)

The global macro variable <name>_print keeps the call of %print: change <name>_display, then print again with %print(&<name>_print.).

docs.title: %termflags
docs.text:
Returns one record per subject and term, with a flag that says whether the subject has the term.

Procedure: PROC SORT, MERGE, PROC SUMMARY · Family: Describe the data

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%termflags(
     data      =
   , denom     =
   , where     =
   , terms     =
   , by        =
   , threshold =
   , out       =
   , debug     = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: the records of the events, with USUBJID. (required) denom= The subjects of the groups: a data set with one row per subject (the population), with USUBJID and the variable of by=. (required) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (trtemfl = 'Y'). (optional) terms= The variables of a row: one or several, separated by blanks, nested in their order (terms = aebodsys aedecod: a term within its class). When not given, one row of all the records, such as "any event" of an overview table. (optional) by= The groups: one variable of denom=. (required) threshold= A percent (threshold = 5): keep only the terms with this percent of the subjects or more in at least one group. The macro compares the percent itself, not its rounded text. It needs terms=. (optional) out= The name of the result data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets termflags. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: one record per subject of denom= and term: USUBJID, the variable of by=, the variables of terms= and FLAG ("Y" or "N"), sorted by the variables of terms= and USUBJID.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: Use it before %risk to compare the groups on the subjects with a term; %freq counts the subjects but gives no flag per subject. The macro computes no statistic. A term is each combination of the values of terms= in the records. FLAG is "Y" when the subject has a record of the term and "N" when not. The subjects are those of denom=: a subject with a record who is not in denom= is left out. Then %risk compares the groups on FLAG within each term (within= the variables of terms=), with the subjects of each group as the denominator.

docs.title: %tte
docs.text:
Returns one time-to-event parameter: for each subject the date of the first event, or else of the latest censoring.

Procedure: PROC SORT, MERGE · Family: ADaM steps

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%tte(
     subjects      =
   , events        =
   , censors       =
   , event         =
   , date          =
   , time          =
   , priority      =
   , start         =
   , start_time    =
   , end           =
   , censor_date   =
   , seq           =
   , adtf          =
   , atmf          =
   , keep          =
   , censor_cnsr   = 1
   , end_cnsr      = 1
   , censor_desc   =
   , censor_source =
   , end_desc      = "End of at-risk period"
   , event_desc    =
   , source        =
   , paramcd       =
   , out           =
   , debug         = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: subjects= The data set of the subjects, one record per subject (USUBJID), with the start (and the end) of the period. The result keeps its variables, so it must not have ADT, CNSR, AVAL or the other variables the macro makes. (required) events= The data set of the records the events come from, such as adae. (required) censors= The data set of the records of the censorings, with censor_date=. When not given, the censorings come from subjects=. (optional) event= The records of events= that are events: a condition, such as event = trtemfl = 'Y'. When not given, every record with a date is an event. (optional) date= The date of an event: a numeric date variable of events=. A record with a missing date is no event. (required) time= The time of an event: a numeric variable of events=, in seconds since midnight. It decides an event on the start day, and needs end=. (optional) priority= The variables of events= that order the events of one date, separated by blanks; a missing value sorts last. When not given, the events of one date keep the order of the data. (optional) start= The start of the period and the origin of AVAL: a date variable of subjects=. (required) start_time= The time of the start: a numeric variable of subjects=, in seconds since midnight. On the start day an event counts unless its time is before this time. It needs end=. (optional) end= The end of the at-risk period: a date variable of subjects=. When not given, there is no period and every date counts. (optional) censor_date= The date of a censoring: a date variable of censors= (or of subjects=). (optional) seq= The variable of events= that gives SRCSEQ of an event, such as aeseq. When not given, SRCSEQ is missing. (optional) adtf= The variable of events= that gives ADTF, the imputation flag of the date of an event. (optional) atmf= The variable of events= that gives ATMF, the imputation flag of the time of an event. (optional) keep= Other variables of the record taken, separated by blanks: they must be in events= and in censors= both. (optional) censor_cnsr= CNSR of a censoring: a number, or a numeric variable of censors=. (optional, default 1) end_cnsr= CNSR of a subject censored at the end of the period: a number. (optional, default 1) censor_desc= EVNTDESC of a censoring: a text in quotes, or a variable of censors= (or of subjects=). (optional) censor_source= SRCDOM of a censoring from subjects= and of a censoring at the end of the period: a text in quotes, such as "ADSL". SRCVAR is then the name of censor_date= (or of end=). (optional) end_desc= EVNTDESC of a subject censored at the end of the period: a text in quotes. (optional, default "End of at-risk period") event_desc= EVNTDESC of an event: a text in quotes, or a variable of events=, such as aedecod. (optional) source= SRCDOM of an event: a text in quotes, such as "ADAE". SRCVAR is then the name of date=. (optional) paramcd= PARAMCD of the parameter: a text in quotes, such as "TTDE". (required) out= The name of the data set it writes. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets tte. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: one record per subject with an event, a censoring or (with end=) a period, in the order of subjects=: the variables of subjects=, PARAMCD, ADT, CNSR, AVAL, ATM (with time=), EVNTDESC, SRCDOM, SRCVAR, SRCSEQ, ADTF and ATMF (when their parameters are given) and the variables of keep=. With end=, a subject with no START or no END gets no record and a WARNING that names it; a subject whose START is after its END gets no record. Two records of a subject in subjects= give an ERROR line. Without end=, a subject with no event and no censoring date gets no record, and a NOTE gives their number.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
It writes the records of an ADTTE parameter; %km, %logrank and %cox then analyse them. The rule:

  • An event is a record of events= that meets event= and has a date. The first event of a subject is taken; priority= orders the events of one date.
  • When a subject has no event, the latest censoring is taken: the latest date of censors= (or of subjects=); on one date, the last record.
  • AVAL is ADT - START + 1, in days.

Without end=, every date counts, and a date before START becomes START (as admiral does). A subject with no event and no censoring date gets no record, and the log has a NOTE with the number of such subjects. With end=, the at-risk period runs from START to END: only the events and censorings in it count, and a subject with neither is censored at END. An event on the start day counts unless time= and start_time= are both there and the event time is before the start time.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples run on the example data after examples/setup.sas. The output under each call is the output of that run. All examples of the reference run as one program: examples/reference.sas.

Makes TTDE. Log NOTE: 2 subject(s) with no event and no censoring date: no record (no TRTEDT).

%tte(
     subjects      = adsl
   , events        = adae
   , event         = trtemfl = 'Y' AND aebodsys = 'SKIN AND SUBCUTANEOUS TISSUE DISORDERS'

docs.title: %ttest
docs.text:
Returns the difference of the means of each pair of groups, with its confidence limits and the t-test p-value.

Procedure: PROC TTEST · Family: Test the groups

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%ttest(
     data      =
   , where     =
   , var       =
   , by        =
   , pairs     = all
   , order     =
   , variances = equal
   , level     = 0.95
   , stats     = diff="XX.X" diff_se="XX.XX" lcl="XX.X" ucl="XX.X" pval="X.XXX"
   , label     =
   , out       =
   , debug     = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: one record per subject, with USUBJID. (required) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (avisit = 'Week 24'). (optional) var= The variable to compare: one numeric variable. (required) by= The groups: one character variable (trt01a, not trt01an). (required) pairs= Which groups to compare. all: each later group against each earlier one, in the order of order= (else of the values). Or the pairs, separated by #: in each pair the group first, then the group it is compared with, each value in quotes (pairs = "Drug" "Placebo" # "High" "Low"). (optional, default all) order= The order of the groups: one numeric variable with one value per group (order = trt01an). (optional) variances= equal (Student's test, the Pooled row of PROC TTEST) or unequal (Welch's test, the Satterthwaite row). (optional, default equal) Accepts: equal, unequal. level= The confidence level: a number between 0 and 1 (level = 0.90). (optional, default 0.95) stats= The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with its pattern of the printed number, separated by blanks. The names are diff, diff_se, lcl, ucl and pval. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns. (optional, default diff="XX.X" diff_se="XX.XX" lcl="XX.X" ucl="XX.X" pval="X.XXX") label= The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table. (optional) out= The name of the result data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets ttest. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the result shape, one row per pair and statistic: the variable of by= (the group), VERSUS (the group it is compared with), GROUPS (by= and VERSUS), BLOCK, STAT, VALUE and TEXT. When no record qualifies, the result has no row.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use %wilcoxon when the values are not normal, %anova for one test of all the groups, and %lsmeans for a model with covariates. The test is the two-sample t-test of PROC TTEST, run BY each pair, the group first. The statistics:

  • diff: the mean of the group minus the mean of the group it is compared with
  • diff_se: the standard error of diff
  • lcl, ucl: the confidence limits of diff
  • pval: the two-sided p-value, of Student's test with the pooled variance (variances=equal) or of Welch's test with Satterthwaite's degrees of freedom (variances=unequal)

The macro uses one record per subject: when a subject has several records, the first one.

docs.text:
Gives each record its analysis visit, AVISIT and AVISITN, from the value of its variable VISIT.

Procedure: DATA steps (SET POINT=) · Family: ADaM steps

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%visits(
     data   =
   , visits =
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The data set to change in place, with the variable VISIT, such as adlb. (required) visits= The visits, separated by #. Each visit is "VISIT" AVISITN "AVISIT": the value of VISIT in quotes, then the analysis visit as a number and as a text (# "WEEK 2" 2 "Week 2"). (required)

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data sets: data=, changed in place: AVISIT and AVISITN on each record whose visit is in visits=, missing on the others.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: Use %windows when the analysis visit comes from the study day of the record. The value of VISIT must match exactly, in upper and lower case. A record whose visit is not in visits= gets missing values only when data= does not have AVISIT and AVISITN yet. When data= has them already (from an earlier step), a record whose visit is not in visits= keeps its old AVISIT and AVISITN: drop them before the call when such a record must have none.

docs.title: %wilcoxon
docs.text:
Returns the p-value of the Wilcoxon rank-sum test of each pair of groups, with the Hodges-Lehmann shift and its limits.

Procedure: PROC NPAR1WAY (WILCOXON, HL) · Family: Test the groups

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%wilcoxon(
     data       =
   , where      =
   , var        =
   , by         =
   , pairs      = all
   , order      =
   , correction = yes
   , level      = 0.95
   , stats      = estimate="XX.XX" lcl="XX.XX" ucl="XX.XX" pval="X.XXX"
   , label      =
   , out        =
   , debug      = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: one record per subject, with USUBJID. (required) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (avisit = 'Week 24'). (optional) var= The variable to compare: one numeric variable. (required) by= The groups: one character variable (trt01a, not trt01an). (required) pairs= Which groups to compare. all: each later group against each earlier one, in the order of order= (else of the values). Or the pairs, separated by #: in each pair the group first, then the group it is compared with, each value in quotes (pairs = "Drug" "Placebo" # "High" "Low"). (optional, default all) order= The order of the groups: one numeric variable with one value per group (order = trt01an). (optional) correction= yes: the continuity correction of the normal approximation; no: none. (optional, default yes) Accepts: yes, no. level= The confidence level: a number between 0 and 1 (level = 0.90). (optional, default 0.95) stats= The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with its pattern of the printed number, separated by blanks. The names are estimate, lcl, ucl and pval. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns. (optional, default estimate="XX.XX" lcl="XX.XX" ucl="XX.XX" pval="X.XXX") label= The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table. (optional) out= The name of the result data set. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets wilcoxon. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the result shape, one row per pair and statistic: the variable of by= (the group), VERSUS (the group it is compared with), GROUPS (by= and VERSUS), BLOCK, STAT, VALUE and TEXT. When no record qualifies, the result has no row.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use %ttest when the values are normal and the difference of the means is wanted. The test runs in PROC NPAR1WAY, BY each pair, the group first. The statistics:

  • pval: the two-sided p-value of the normal approximation, with the continuity correction when correction=yes (CORRECT=)
  • estimate: the Hodges-Lehmann estimate of the shift, the group minus the group it is compared with (HL)
  • lcl, ucl: the asymptotic (Moses) confidence limits of the shift

The macro uses one record per subject: when a subject has several records, the first one.

docs.title: %windows
docs.text:
Puts each record into its analysis window by its study day, and gives it AVISIT, AVISITN and the window variables.

Procedure: DATA steps (SET POINT=) · Family: ADaM steps

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%windows(
     data    =
   , windows =
   , day     = ADY
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The data set to change in place, such as advs. (required) windows= The windows in the order of AVISITN, separated by #. Each window is AVISITN "AVISIT" AWLO AWHI AWTARGET "AWRANGE"; a period for AWLO or AWHI is a limit that is open (# 4 "Week 4" 2 42 28 "2-42"). (required) day= The numeric variable of the study day. (optional, default ADY)

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data sets: data=, changed in place: AVISIT, AVISITN, AWLO, AWHI, AWTARGET, AWRANGE, AWU and AWTDIFF on each record in a window, missing on a record in no window.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
Use %visits when the analysis visit comes from the visit name of the record, not from its study day. The macro writes these variables:

  • AVISIT and AVISITN: the analysis visit of the window
  • AWLO, AWHI and AWTARGET: the first day, the last day and the target day of the window
  • AWRANGE: the window as a text; AWU: DAYS
  • AWTDIFF: the distance of the study day to the target day

A record takes the first window, in the order of windows=, that holds its day. A record with no window, or a missing day, gets missing values only when data= does not have these variables yet. When data= has them already (an AVISIT from an earlier step), a record in no window keeps its old AVISIT, AVISITN and window values: drop them before the call when such a record must have none.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples run on the example data after examples/setup.sas. The output under each call is the output of that run. All examples of the reference run as one program: examples/reference.sas.

Copies the systolic records with only the variables the windows need: no old AVISIT or AVISITN.

DATA vs;
  SET advs;
  WHERE paramcd = 'SYSBP';
  KEEP usubjid paramcd param adt ady aval vsseq;
RUN;

Puts each record in the window of its study day, with the limits, the target and the distance.

%windows(
     data    = vs
   , windows = 0  "Baseline" .   1   1   "<=1"
             # 4  "Week 4"   2   42  28  "2-42"
             # 12 "Week 12"  43  126 84  "43-126"
             # 24 "Week 24"  127 210 168 "127-210"
   , day     = ady
 )

docs.title: %worst
docs.text:
Keeps the records of each subject at its worst level, such as the highest severity or toxicity grade.

Procedure: PROC SORT, a DATA step (BY, FIRST.) · Family: Describe the data

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
%worst(
     data   =
   , where  =
   , var    =
   , by     =
   , levels =
   , out    =
   , debug  = no
 )

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: data= The input data set: the records, with USUBJID. (required) where= The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (trtemfl = 'Y'). (optional) var= The graded variable: one variable, character or numeric (var = aesev). (required) by= The variables of a row: one or several, separated by blanks (by = aebodsys aedecod). The macro keeps the worst records of each subject in each row. When not given, the worst of all the records of the subject. (optional) levels= The values of var= from the least to the most severe, separated by blanks: texts in quotes, numbers without (levels = 'MILD' 'MODERATE' 'SEVERE'). (required) out= The name of the data set of the records kept. (required) debug= yes: keep the work data sets worst. (optional, default no)* Accepts: yes, no.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: The data set of out=: the records of data= at the worst level of each subject and row, with all the variables of data=, sorted by USUBJID and the variables of by=.

docs.title: Details
docs.text: Use it before %freq, so that %freq counts each subject once in each row, at its worst level; the macro computes no statistic. The worst level is the value of var= that comes last in levels= (levels= goes from the least to the most severe). The macro looks for it for each subject in each row of by=, or in all the records of the subject when by= is not given. A record whose value is not in levels=, such as a missing grade, is never the worst and is left out. When a subject has several records at its worst level, all of them stay.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples run on the example data after examples/setup.sas. The output under each call is the output of that run. All examples of the reference run as one program: examples/reference.sas.

Keeps the records of each subject and term at the worst severity, the last value of levels=.

%worst(
     data   = adae
   , where  = (trtemfl = 'Y')
   , var    = aesev
   , by     = aebodsys aedecod
   , levels = 'MILD' 'MODERATE' 'SEVERE'
   , out    = ae_worst
 )

docs.title: Tutorial: your first table
docs.text:
In this tutorial you make a table of age and sex by treatment, from the example data to an RTF file. You run one call at a time and look at what each call made. It takes about fifteen minutes.

You need SAS 9.4 and a copy of the repository datastep-labs/sapling-sas. The terms of use of the macros are in the LICENSE of the repository; for commercial use and its price, write to datastep.studio@gmail.com. The whole tutorial is also one program, examples/tutorial.sas: you learn more by submitting the steps one at a time, as below.

docs.title: The example data
docs.text:
The folder examples/data holds the example data: eight data sets of the R packages pharmaverseadam and pharmaversesdtm, the subjects of the CDISC pilot study. The program examples/setup.sas reads them.

  1. Open examples/setup.sas.

  2. Find the line %LET spl_root = /path/to/sapling-sas;, below the header box. Change the path to the folder of your copy of the repository, for example:

    %LET spl_root = /home/me/sapling-sas;

  3. Submit the whole program. The log has the line NOTE: [study] ends after ... seconds. and no ERROR.

The program loads the macros, reads the data, and makes the WORK data sets adsl, adae, advs, adlb, adtte and adrs. It also sets the output folder, examples/out in your copy, which the programs call &spl_out.: every table and file of this tutorial goes there. adsl holds the safety population. These are its first rows:

adsl: the first 5 of 254 rows
USUBJID      TRT01A                TRT01AN  AGE  SEX  RACE
01-701-1015  Placebo                     0   63  F    WHITE
01-701-1023  Placebo                     0   64  M    WHITE
01-701-1028  Xanomeline High Dose       81   71  M    WHITE
01-701-1033  Xanomeline Low Dose        54   74  M    WHITE
01-701-1034  Xanomeline High Dose       81   77  F    WHITE

Each row is one subject. You use trt01a for the columns of the table, age and sex for its rows.

docs.title: Step 1: summarize a numeric variable
docs.text:
Call %describe for the age in each treatment group:

%describe(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = t_age
 )

t_age: the first 7 of 24 rows
TRT01A   BLOCK        STAT           VALUE  TEXT
Placebo  Age (years)  n                 86    86
Placebo  Age (years)  mean    75.209302326  75.2
Placebo  Age (years)  sd      8.5901671271  8.59
Placebo  Age (years)  median            76  76.0
Placebo  Age (years)  min               52    52
Placebo  Age (years)  max               89    89
Total    Age (years)  n                254   254

t_age is the result of the call: one row per number. VALUE holds the number with all its digits. TEXT holds it as the table will print it. total = yes added the group Total.

docs.title: Step 2: count the categories
docs.text:
Call %freq for the sex in each treatment group:

%freq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = t_sex
 )

t_sex: the first 6 of 16 rows
TRT01A   SEX  BLOCK  STAT         VALUE  TEXT
Placebo  F    Sex    n               53  53
Placebo  F    Sex    pct   61.627906977  (61.6%)
Placebo  M    Sex    n               33  33
Placebo  M    Sex    pct   38.372093023  (38.4%)
Total    F    Sex    n              143  143
Total    F    Sex    pct   56.299212598  (56.3%)

The result has the same variables as t_age, and one more: SEX, the category. Every statistics macro writes this shape, so the next calls can use any of them.

docs.title: Step 3: stack the blocks
docs.text:
Put the two results under each other, in the order of the table:

%stack(t_age t_sex, out=t_first)

t_first: the first 4 of 40 rows
RESULT  ORD  BLOCK        TRT01A   STAT    TEXT
T_AGE     1  Age (years)  Placebo  n         86
T_AGE     1  Age (years)  Placebo  mean    75.2
T_AGE     1  Age (years)  Placebo  sd      8.59
T_AGE     1  Age (years)  Placebo  median  76.0

RESULT and ORD say which result each row came from, and its place in the table.

docs.title: Step 4: make the columns
docs.text:
Make the columns of the table and the N of each:

%columns(
     data  = t_first
   , n     = adsl
   , var   = trt01a
   , order = trt01an
   , total = yes
   , out   = t_first_cols
 )

t_first_cols: 4 rows
HEADER                       COLVALUE              COL  BIGN
Placebo|(N=86)               Placebo                 1    86
Xanomeline Low Dose|(N=96)   Xanomeline Low Dose     2    96
Xanomeline High Dose|(N=72)  Xanomeline High Dose    3    72
Total|(N=254)                Total                   4   254

The columns come from the data: three treatment groups, in the order of trt01an, then Total. Each HEADER holds the name of the column and its N.

docs.title: Step 5: keep every number
docs.text:
Write every number of the table to a CSV file:

%ard(data=t_first, columns=t_first_cols, file=t_first)

ard/t_first.csv: the first 8 of 45 lines
result,stat,g1_value,g2_value,g3_value,g4_value,g5_value,raw,formatted
N,n,Placebo,,,,,86,(N=86)
N,n,Xanomeline Low Dose,,,,,96,(N=96)
N,n,Xanomeline High Dose,,,,,72,(N=72)
N,n,Total,,,,,254,(N=254)
T_AGE,n,Placebo,,,,,86,86
T_AGE,mean,Placebo,,,,,75.2093023255814,75.2
T_AGE,sd,Placebo,,,,,8.59016712714192,8.59

The file is examples/out/ard/t_first.csv: file= of %ard is a name, and the macro puts the file in the folder ard of the output folder. Each line holds one number, written with the format BEST32. (raw, at most 15 significant digits), and its printed text (formatted). A second program can check its own numbers against this file.

docs.title: Step 6: lay out the rows
docs.text:
Make the rows of the table:

%layout(
     data    = t_first
   , columns = t_first_cols
   , var     = trt01a
   , file    = &spl_out./tlf/t_first
   , setup   = t_first_print
   , out     = t_first_display
 )

t_first_display: 9 rows
GRP  ROW          C1           C2           C3           C4
  1  Age (years)
  1  n            86           96           72           254
  1  Mean (SD)    75.2 (8.59)  76.0 (8.11)  73.8 (7.94)  75.1 (8.25)

t_first_display holds one row per printed line: ROW is the label, C1 to C4 are the cells of the four columns. GRP numbers the rows that must stay on one page: the age block is group 1, and each category of sex is a group of its own. You can change this data set with a DATA step before you print it, for example to rename a row.

Here file= is a path without its extension: %print adds .rtf and .lst.
